title: Can't Disable profile from camera.
author: Lars
body:
I'm trying to edit a few old photos from my Nikon D3200 in NEF.

Everything works well, but the photos are all displayed and edited in the camera set profile, which in this case is B&W since I shoot a lot in B&W profile, so either the camera profile is being forcefully applied before any LightCraft edits are applied, or LightCraft is acting over the preview image inside the raw rather than on the raw itself.

It's generally not bad to have the camera profile applied directly, if this is what's happening, I just want an option to be able to disable it.

But, I fear LC is acting upon the embedded preview rather than the raw data instead, and it should really really act upon the RAW and not the preview. (If I want the cooked profile, My cameras are now set to output both RAW+JPG so I get the profile on a good JPG and the RAW if I want to edit that).

title: Fillm Roll Scroll
author: Lars
body:
I have two requests/comments regarding the "the film roll" on the bottom (to see, and select the pictures to work on).

First, I would like to search though the roll with the mouse scroll wheel when I'm hovering over the roll.

Second, when I scroll with the scroll bar, as soon as I release the mouse button it jumps back to the currently selected photo. The roll should remain at the point where it was released until there's an action that selects a different photo (like left/right keys) or re-selects the current photo (or maybe if any changes are made to the photo in the edit pane), at which point it can/should snap back to the selected photo.

The snap back issue affects the photo grid mode as well which makes it very hard/almost impossible to scroll through medium/large collections as one second after I stop scrolling it snaps back to the selected photo.

title: Read capture time from XMP sidecars when embedded capture metadata is absent
author: radialmonster
body:
A photo with no embedded capture timestamp but a capture timestamp in its adjacent XMP sidecar did not acquire that capture time through the inspected import path.

Source evidence: engine/src/import.rs assigns Photo.captured from the photo probe, then merges the sidecar. engine/src/sidecar.rs::SidecarData/parse_sidecar/merge_into do not carry capture time into Photo.captured, even for a timestamp the metadata parser recognizes. catalog/src/model.rs::Photo::date falls back to imported when captured is absent.

The user also reported older Local photos under today's header. The active sort/group mode was not recorded, so that observation does not establish an incorrect capture-date header: import-date grouping could legitimately show today. Independently inspected metadata supported an older capture date, but used an EXIF-style colon date; parsing that non-ISO form is a separate interoperability question, not the basis of this issue.

Please merge supported XMP capture timestamps into capture metadata with explicit precedence, preserve embedded dates when appropriate, and handle genuinely unknown dates clearly. Verify with a generated JPEG lacking embedded dates and a minimal valid ISO XMP sidecar. This is static source evidence; no synthetic application reproduction has been run.

Use a generated `sample.jpg` with no embedded capture date and an adjacent `sample.jpg.xmp` containing:

title: Add persistent expandable folder roots to Local
author: radialmonster
body:
Local browsing provides no persistent custom-root workflow. After Browse Folder selects a photo root, clicking a dated child replaces the custom root entry with that child; ancestors and siblings disappear from that sidebar tree. Switching to another location also replaces the current custom entry.

Reported sequence: browse a photo root with year/day subfolders; expand it; select a child; observe that only the child remains as the custom root. Adding photos to My Photos updates library organization but does not preserve Local navigation roots.

Source: ui-egui/src/panels/left.rs::local_section lists built-in locations plus the currently browsed path. Child selection changes that path. Existing breadcrumbs can return to ancestors, but do not provide persistent sidebar roots.

Please add an explicit Add Folder to Local or favorite action supporting multiple saved roots. Keep each root's expandable/collapsible hierarchy and sibling navigation while selecting descendants or other locations; persist roots across restarts. This is a requested saved-location workflow, separate from catalog import or file copying. Restart persistence is requested, not a reproduced restart failure. Removal should be sidebar-only.

## Concrete navigation example

Use this generic equivalent of the reported hierarchy:

```text
Photos/
  2026/
    20260101/
      sample-a.jpg
    20260114/
      sample-b.jpg
```

1. Browse Folder to `Photos` and expand `2026`.
2. Select `20260101`.
3. Current behavior reported: the custom Local root becomes `20260101`, losing the visible `Photos` ancestor and `20260114` sibling.
4. Requested behavior: keep `Photos` as the saved root and highlight `20260101`; the sibling remains reachable.

The names above are a generic example, not supplied test files. Cross-location/restart persistence is the enhancement requested, not an independently tested failure.

title: Local shows a duplicate entry for the selected built-in location
author: radialmonster
body:
On Windows, selecting Downloads in Local shows its tree but also adds a second Downloads entry below Home. The original Downloads entry remains. Desktop and Pictures were reported to behave similarly.

Steps: browse a custom root, then select a built-in Local location. Observe both its built-in shortcut and a second current-location root. This concerns duplicate roots, not a folder legitimately appearing inside a parent hierarchy.

Source: ui-egui/src/panels/left.rs builds shortcut strings using HOME/USERPROFILE plus forward-slash suffixes and deduplicates the current browse path by exact string equality. engine/src/cmd/browse.rs stores the string from std::path::absolute. This confirms a representation-sensitive comparison; the exact differing runtime strings were not captured. Path normalization is a suspected trigger, not a proven diagnosis.

Please recognize equivalent folder locations consistently so an existing root is reused and highlighted. Cover equivalent Windows spellings with synthetic checks rather than special-casing the three reported shortcuts. Runtime symptom is user-reported, not independently reproduced.

## Exact comparison to investigate

The built-in path is constructed with `format!("{home}/{sub}")`. The duplicate guard is `!places.iter().any(|(_, p)| *p == b.path)`. Browse stores a path processed with `std::path::absolute`.

A proposed Windows test uses equivalent strings such as `D:/Example/Photos` and `D:\Example\Photos`. The actual spellings used by the installed app were not captured, so this illustrates the regression case without claiming it is the diagnosed trigger. The acceptance criterion is path identity for every shortcut, not three hard-coded folder names.

title: Switching Local folders temporarily makes LightCraft stop responding
author: radialmonster
body:
With Include subfolders enabled, switching between Local locations repeatedly made LightCraft stop responding. It later recovered. Two read-only process observations showed Responding=false while CPU usage increased, supporting a busy/unresponsive period rather than proving deadlock. Exact stall durations were not recorded.

Reported steps: enable Include subfolders, then switch between built-in Local locations. The sequence eventually reached Home; broad recursive browsing added many Local records. The user has only about 200 library photos, but saved catalog inspection found about 84,000 Local-only records. This distinction matters to reproduction.

Source: engine/src/cmd/browse.rs waits for recursive expansion, import_with/probing and a visible query. Scoped probe workers are joined before return. UI command dispatch is synchronous. This is a blocking path, but each stage's contribution to the observed freeze is unmeasured.

Please perform discovery/probing in cancellable background work with progress and reject results from superseded selections. Measure stages using synthetic folder trees. Related merged PR #2 addresses the File import-review scan; this report concerns Local library.browse, a distinct path.

## Validation scenario and recorded evidence

Proposed isolated reproduction: a generated folder tree with many supported image files; switch repeatedly between roots with Include subfolders enabled, then repeat with it disabled. Record enumeration, probing, index construction, catalog mutation and query timings separately. Also test selecting another root before an earlier scan completes.

The user's two process samples were unresponsive while cumulative CPU time increased from 203.875 to 218.265625 seconds, followed by reported recovery. Sampling interval was not preserved, so these values must not be interpreted as a CPU utilization percentage or stall duration. No exact blocking stage has been profiled.

title: Show active filters and distinguish library totals from matching photo counts
author: radialmonster
body:

The user accepts total library counts. The request is to explain the source/filter intersection, not force a source switch or declare the total count incorrect.

title: Show supported rename-template tags beside the import Rename field
author: radialmonster
body:
After selecting Copy, the user found Rename but could not discover its supported template tags. The dialog shows only a placeholder example and a live filename preview.

Please add visible help or a tag picker beside the field with descriptions and examples for {name}, {seq}, {seq:N}, {date}, {date:format}, {camera}, {title} and {ext}. Document supported date/time directives, sequence padding, automatic extension appending, and blank-template behavior. Keep the live preview; a picker should insert at the cursor rather than replace the template.

Source: ui-egui/src/import.rs shows the example {date}_{seq:3}; engine/src/rename.rs implements the tokens. For example, {date:%Y%m%d_%H%M%S}_{seq:3} can produce 20260114_055848_001.jpg. Help should make unsupported-token and missing-metadata behavior clear. This is discoverability, not a missing rename implementation.

## Supported syntax to expose

| Tag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `{name}` / `{filename}` | Original filename stem |
| `{seq}` / `{n}` | Sequence number |
| `{seq:3}` | Sequence padded to three digits, such as `001` |
| `{date}` | Date as YYYYMMDD |
| `{date:%Y%m%d_%H%M%S}` | Custom date/time format |
| `{camera}` | Camera metadata |
| `{title}` | Photo title metadata |
| `{ext}` | Original extension without the dot |

The implemented date directives are `%Y`, `%y`, `%m`, `%d`, `%H`, `%M`, `%S` and `%%`. The original extension is appended automatically. Unknown tokens remain literal; help should explain that rather than letting a typo silently look like a supported tag.

title: Support custom date-based folder formats when importing
author: radialmonster
body:

Please support that compact day layout, ideally through a custom date-based folder template alongside presets. A proposed template such as {date:%Y}/{date:%Y%m%d} should produce the matching hierarchy; this folder-template syntax is not currently supported.

Show an example full destination before import, document available folder tags, and explain which photo date is used and the missing-date fallback. Apply consistently to Copy and any future Move mode. Filename Rename templates currently do not configure folder layout. No files were imported to test this limitation; the fixed options and layout implementation are source-confirmed.

## Exact preset values and requested output

- `organize="date"`: `2026/2026-01-14/sample.jpg`.
- `organize="month"`: `2026/2026-01/sample.jpg`.

title: Refresh camera-device discovery asynchronously instead of scanning drives during menu rendering
author: radialmonster
body:
On Windows, ordinary in-window menu rendering can perform synchronous camera-device discovery, even with the File popup closed.

Source: ui-egui/src/menubar.rs::show_in_window rebuilds the whole menu model; expanded("Add from Device") calls engine/src/devices.rs::devices. After its two-second cache expires, it scans while holding the global cache mutex. Default Windows discovery tries drive roots D: through Z:, enumerates entries and checks directories for DCIM. A cache limits frequency, but does not make I/O asynchronous.

Please serve a cached device list immediately and refresh in background work without holding the cache lock during I/O. Coalesce requests, retain hot-plug updates and consider targeted DCIM/mount discovery rather than enumerating all root entries. Reusing static menu structure may reduce other overhead but is secondary to eliminating this blocking side effect.

The user reported menu lag while their PC was busy; this path is source-confirmed, but no scan or input-latency timings establish its contribution. Verify with a delayed directory reader, absent/mapped/removable drives and closed popups. This issue is limited to device discovery; missing-file checks are separate.

## Specific refresh behavior to measure

The model is built before popup visibility is checked. Therefore leaving all dropdowns closed is a useful regression test: after the two-second cache expires, a repaint must not wait for drive enumeration. Measure cold and warm refreshes with an instrumented delayed reader, and verify hot-plug updates still arrive.

No actual drive-scan timings or input-to-menu-display latency were recorded in this investigation.

title: Avoid processing the entire visible photo set for unchanged grid frames
author: radialmonster
body:
The grid virtualizes thumbnail drawing and caches geometry, but still performs substantial whole-view bookkeeping each frame. ui-egui/src/panels/grid.rs clones visible IDs, constructs full-view cell bookkeeping, rebuilds the stack index and visits cells to test viewport intersection. Layout/date-run cache keys also hash the complete ID set.

These confirmed operations scale with the visible result size, including large recursive Local views. There are no measured frame times, and this finding does not establish the cause of the separately reported scroll snap-back.

Please share immutable view data, key caches by relevant generations, reuse stack indexes and index row/header bounds to visit only visible/prefetched rows. Preserve grouping, crop/orientation changes, stacks and selection scrolling.

Measure allocations, visited cells and frame-time distributions on unchanged synthetic views of 200, 10,000 and 85,000 results in square and justified layouts. Keep existing background rendering and thumbnail virtualization.

## Operations that remain on unchanged frames

`visible_cloned()` copies the visible IDs; the grid builds a `Vec<Cell>` by zipping all IDs with cached cell rectangles, calls `catalog.stack_index()`, then loops over every cell before deciding whether it intersects the prefetch viewport. `date_runs` and grid-layout keys hash the ID slice.

Measure these separately from image decoding/upload. Success means unchanged frames reuse view/index data and visit only indexed visible/prefetched rows while preserving selection scrolling and date headers. No measured frame budget or speedup is claimed.

title: Cache smart-album counts instead of scanning and allocating during sidebar layout
author: radialmonster
body:
For each rendered smart album, ui-egui/src/panels/left.rs requests album_count. catalog/src/lib.rs obtains album_photos and takes its length, scanning catalog photos, evaluating rules and allocating matching IDs during repeated sidebar layout. title: Reduce UI-thread pauses from catalog persistence and snapshot compaction
author: radialmonster
body:
Top-level engine commands persist before returning, and UI logic also retries pending persistence. engine/src/library.rs can trigger journal compaction; catalog/src/journal.rs serializes the full catalog into JSON and wraps it in another string. catalog/src/store.rs performs durable writes and log reset. Local browsing records enlarge the persisted catalog alongside library records.

These are source-confirmed synchronous operations, not measured compaction stalls. Durability is intentional and must be preserved.

Please instrument append, serialization and compaction, then consider streaming serialization and an ordered persistence worker with consistent snapshot versions and replay-safe journal boundaries. Preserve durable acknowledgement, errors and crash recovery. Any Local-record eviction must preserve edits/references and needs a separate policy decision.

Use large synthetic catalogs at threshold crossings to measure input latency and memory, and test crash recovery plus edits during background snapshotting. Existing perf.frame_ms measures layout, excluding preceding UI logic; include whole-update timing. This concern is separate from filesystem discovery and grid bookkeeping.

## Persistence thresholds and files

Default `SnapshotPolicy` uses 2,000 journal records or 16 MiB. Persistence appends pending operations to `catalog.log`; compaction serializes the catalog into `catalog.snap` and resets the log. Log append calls `sync_data`; atomic snapshot writing calls `sync_all`.

`persist` is cheap when nothing changed and compaction is not due, so this issue does not claim a full rewrite every frame. It concerns the synchronous work at actual writes and threshold crossings. Verify crash recovery and acknowledgement ordering as well as latency; never remove durability merely to reduce timings.

title: Exports are pure black when the GPU path is active (Intel iGPU / Mesa)
author: SYKhayyat
body:
## Exports are pure black when the GPU path is active (Intel iGPU / Mesa)

Exporting from the app produces a structurally valid JPEG whose every pixel is `#000000`. The photo looks correct in the preview at the same time, which is what makes this easy to miss.

Two consecutive exports of the same raw file were both fully black. I have not yet checked whether every photo is affected or only some — I only reproduced it on the one file I had loaded.

### What the output looks like

The file is not corrupt and not truncated; it is a complete image that is entirely black.

```
identify -verbose DSC_5414.jpg
  Geometry: 6000x4000      Colors: 1      Type: Bilevel      Depth: 8/1-bit
  mean: 0 (0)   max: 0 (0)   standard deviation: 0 (0)      (all channels)

convert DSC_5414.jpg -depth 8 histogram:info:-
  24000000: (0,0,0) #000000 black
```

6000x4000 = 24,000,000 pixels, and all 24,000,000 are black. The JPEG markers are all present and well-formed (SOI, APP0/APP1/APP2, DQT, SOF0, DHT, SOS, ~659 KB of entropy data, EOI), and the Huffman tables and quantisation tables were actually written — so the encoder ran and did real work. It was handed zeros.

That points at the GPU→CPU readback rather than at decoding or at file writing.

### Bisection

Source file is a 6016x4016 16-bit NEF. Means are ImageMagick `fx:mean` over the whole frame; `0` means black.

| what | mean | |
|---|---|---|
| the `.NEF` itself, read directly | 0.378 | fine |
| `lightcraft-cli render` — same file, same options | 0.388 | fine |
| GUI export, Intel driver selected | **0.000** | **black** |
| GUI export, `LIGHTCRAFT_GPU=0` | 0.378 | fine |

The CPU path renders the identical image correctly, so the raw decoder, the develop pipeline and the JPEG encoder are all behaving. The difference is which device rendered it.

`ui.inspect` reports the adapter as:

```
"gpu": "Intel(R) UHD Graphics (ICL GT1) (Vulkan)"
```

title: Saving an XMP sidecar replaces an existing one and drops other apps' data
author: radialmonster
body:
When a photo already has an `.xmp` sidecar written by another app (e.g. Lightroom Classic/ACR), **Save Metadata to File** (Cmd/Ctrl+S) — or any edit while XMP auto-write is on — replaces that file with a fresh LightCraft packet. Nothing from the existing sidecar is kept: `write_xmp_lc` deliberately omits the `crs:` namespace, so Lightroom's develop settings and history are lost, as are any other fields LightCraft doesn't model. The write itself is atomic, so this is data loss by replacement, not corruption.

A second case: with the default Stem naming, `IMG_0001.CR3` and `IMG_0001.JPG` share `IMG_0001.xmp`, so saving metadata for one overwrites the other's sidecar.

For users coming from Lightroom (LightCraft's stated target), the sidecars next to their raws are often the only copy of their edits outside the Lightroom catalog.

**Expected:** read the existing sidecar and merge LightCraft's fields into it, preserving unknown namespaces/properties (at minimum `crs:`), or keep a backup before replacing. For the shared-stem case, either merge or warn/switch to Full naming (`IMG_0001.CR3.xmp`) when two catalogued files map to the same sidecar.

title: Export, render and MCP writes can overwrite a photo's original file
author: radialmonster
body:
Nothing stops an export from landing on top of a catalogued original.

**Scenario:** Export a JPEG original with Folder = the photo's own folder, file name `{name}`, format JPEG, and "If file exists" = **Overwrite**. The original is replaced by the re-encoded (possibly resized/watermarked) render. **Export with Previous** reuses the folder and the Overwrite choice, so it can repeat this without the dialog.

Related paths with the same gap:
- The native writer is a plain `std::fs::write` (truncate then write), so a failure mid-write leaves a truncated file. With "Original" format + Overwrite into the source folder, the original is rewritten with its own bytes and is at risk if the write fails.
- The XMP sidecar written with an "Original" export ignores the collision setting even under "Add number", so it can replace an existing sidecar in the destination folder.
- The exact `path` used by the control channel/MCP (`export`, `render_photo`, `ui.render`, merge `previewPath`) is overwritten unconditionally.
- `lightcraft-cli render IMG.jpg -o IMG.jpg` overwrites its own input.

**Expected:**
- Refuse (or require an explicit confirmation) when an export/render target is a catalogued original or the input file, regardless of the conflict setting.
- Write exports to a temp file in the destination folder and rename into place.
- Apply the chosen conflict policy to export sidecars too.

title: Control port: close the connection on input that isn't a command
author: radialmonster
body:
Low priority — the control server is opt-in (`--control` / `LIGHTCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT`) and loopback-only. But it has no authentication, and when it receives a line that isn't JSON it replies with an error and **keeps reading** the same connection.

That means a web page open in the user's browser could probably send a cross-origin `fetch` POST (e.g. `text/plain`, no preflight) to `127.0.0.1:<port>`: the HTTP request line and headers are rejected one by one, but a JSON line in the body would then be executed. Through `engine.execute` that reaches commands such as `folder.move`, `photo.rename`, `library.import` with `mode: "move"`, or an export to any path. This is inferred from the code and not tested; recent Chrome Local Network Access prompts reduce, but don't remove, the exposure across browsers.

**Suggested fix (easy):** close the connection as soon as anything other than a command (a JSON request object) arrives. An HTTP request can then never carry a command through. A token/password would be optional on top of that.

## Source references

- [apps/lightcraft/src/control_server.rs:35-60](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/cd35ebdacef2a546059a3307b656e657d94b2fee/apps/lightcraft/src/control_server.rs#L35-L60) - non-JSON lines produce `bad JSON` and the loop continues.
- [apps/lightcraft/src/control_server.rs:14](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/cd35ebdacef2a546059a3307b656e657d94b2fee/apps/lightcraft/src/control_server.rs#L14) - binds 127.0.0.1, no auth.

title: Rename Photos: a case-only rename can overwrite a different file on case-sensitive file systems
author: radialmonster
body:
`move_file` and the rename planner treat a target that differs from the source only by letter case as "this same file" and skip the "already exists" check. That's correct on case-insensitive volumes (default NTFS, default APFS), but on case-sensitive ones (Linux, case-sensitive APFS, NTFS directories with case sensitivity enabled) two distinct files can differ only by case.

**Scenario (traced, not run):** a folder contains two different files, `IMG_1.JPG` and `img_1.JPG`. Rename Photos with a template producing `img_1` renames `IMG_1.JPG` → `img_1.JPG`; `std::fs::rename` replaces the existing `img_1.JPG`, and that photo is lost. Its sidecar can be replaced the same way.

**Expected:** decide "same file" by file identity (e.g. compare metadata/inode/file ID, or canonicalized paths), not by lowercase string comparison; or use a no-replace rename.

Minor, related: the existence check and `fs::rename` are separate steps (`rename` replaces on both Windows and Unix), so a file created in between could be overwritten; a no-replace rename would close that too.

## Source references

- [crates/engine/src/rename.rs:302-320](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/cd35ebdacef2a546059a3307b656e657d94b2fee/crates/engine/src/rename.rs#L302-L320) - `case_only` bypasses the exists check.

title: Import → Copy doesn't verify copies (Move already does)
author: radialmonster
body:
Move import copies with `copy_verified`: it writes a new file (`create_new`), syncs it to disk, compares it byte for byte with the original and removes a bad partial copy. Copy import uses `copy_into`, which picks a free name with `exists()` and then calls plain `std::fs::copy`: no sync, no comparison. If `fs::copy` returns Ok, the photo counts as imported.

**Why it matters:** the usual card workflow is Copy from the card → see the import complete → format the card. A silently bad copy (flaky card reader, USB disconnect, an external/network drive that hasn't flushed) is then the only copy left. Copy never deletes the original itself, but users rely on it as the step that makes the card safe to wipe.

The `exists()` → `fs::copy` sequence is also check-then-write: `fs::copy` overwrites, so a file that appears at that name in between would be replaced.

**Suggested fix:** use the same verified copy for Copy mode as for Move (`copy_verified` / `link_or_copy` minus the hard link, made `pub(crate)`), retrying the next `-N` name on `AlreadyExists`. Report a failed verification as a failed import so the user knows not to wipe the source. Also applies to the copy step of "Copy as DNG" if it goes through the same helper.

title: Make Rename Folder / Move Folder undoable
author: radialmonster
body:
**Rename Folder…** and **Move Folder To…** (Local sidebar) rename the folder on disk immediately and relink its photos, but they are not undo steps. A mistaken drag or a typo in the name can't be reverted with Undo; the user has to find the folder and move it back by hand (and LightCraft then has to pick up the relink again).

No confirmation dialog is needed — file managers don't ask either — but the operation should be on the undo/redo stack like other edits.

The reason given in the code is that "undoing would point the photos back at a folder that no longer exists." That holds only if undo reverts the catalog alone. Rename Photos already solves this: its `SetFile` op is undoable, and `undo_step` / `redo_step` move the files on disk back and forth (`apply_with_files` → `file_moves` → `move_files`, all-or-nothing). Folder rename/move could work the same way: record one undoable op (the folder move plus the batch of `Relink`s) whose undo renames the folder back (same safety checks: refuse if the original path is now taken) and restores the old paths, and whose redo repeats it.

Out of scope here: Move *import* (originals are deleted from the source after verification), which would need a different mechanism.

title: Thumbnail cache cleanup deletes every file under thumbs/, not just its own thumbnails
author: radialmonster
body:
Low priority; raising it so you can decide.

`DiskCache::scan` collects every regular file one level below `<library>/thumbs/`, and both `prune` (runs automatically when the cache exceeds its budget) and `clear` delete from that list. Cache files have a fixed shape — `<2 hex>/<32 hex>.jpg`, plus the `<32 hex>.tmp…` temp names `put` uses — but nothing checks the name before deleting.

Normally `thumbs/` only contains LightCraft's files, so this is harmless. It matters if the library is opened on a folder the user already uses: `open_library` accepts any directory, and the cache is `<library>/thumbs`. A photo root like `D:\Photos` that already has a `thumbs\...` folder (a common name for other apps' or websites' thumbnails, or a user's own small JPEGs) would have those files removed oldest-first once the cache goes over budget, without any action from the user.

**Suggested fix:** only list (and therefore delete) files whose subfolder is 2 hex characters and whose name is 32 hex characters + `.jpg` (or the cache's own temp suffix). It's a name check in `scan`, so it's negligible next to the `metadata` call already made per file, and `size()` then also stops counting foreign files toward the budget. Optionally: warn when opening/creating a library in a non-empty folder that isn't a LightCraft library.

title: Two processes can open the same library and silently drop each other's edits (no library lock)
author: radialmonster
body:
Nothing stops two processes from opening the same library folder. `FsStore::open` only creates the directory, and neither the desktop app nor `lightcraft-cli` (`mcp --library`, `run --library`, `snapshot --library`) takes a lock. `docs/mcp.md` describes `--library` as "the same crash-safe format the desktop app uses (`~/Pictures/LightCraft Library` by default there)", so pointing the CLI at the everyday library while the app is open is an easy step to take. A library on a NAS opened from two machines is the same situation.

**What happens (traced from the code, not run):** each process has its own in-memory catalog and its own `seq` counter, both starting from the same snapshot. Say both open at seq 100. The app appends records 101–103, and the CLI appends its own 101. On the next load, replay applies the app's 101–103, then skips the CLI's 101 because `seq <= j.seq` ("already in the snapshot"). The record is only counted as `stale`. Each process also writes `catalog.snap` from its own in-memory catalog and resets `catalog.log`, so whichever one snapshots last (at quit, at the latest) replaces the other's edits. Both also write through the same `catalog.snap.tmp` name. Nothing tells the user. The edits are simply missing the next time the library opens.

**Suggested fix:**

- On open, create `<library>/catalog.lock` and hold an exclusive OS lock on it for the life of the session (std `File::try_lock`, or the `fs4` / `fd-lock` crates). Write the PID, host name and app/CLI version into the file for the error message.
- If the lock is held, refuse to open: "This library is open in LightCraft on <host> (PID n)." The desktop app should show that in a dialog, not fall back to an in-memory session (see the separate issue about that fallback). The CLI should exit with the error, and could point to `--connect` for driving a running app.
- Advisory locks over SMB aren't fully reliable, so the lock file's contents are still useful as a hint there.

title: If the library can't be opened, the desktop app quietly runs an unsaved demo session
author: radialmonster
body:
`open_session` falls back to an in-memory session with the demo photos (`Session::with_demo()`) whenever `open_library` returns an error. The only report is an `eprintln!`, and Windows release builds have no console (#7). Settings → General does show "In memory — nothing is saved" as the location, but nothing else in the window does.

Errors that lead there, from the code:

- `catalog.snap` doesn't parse, or has an unsupported format or version (`Journal::open`).
- Any I/O error reading `catalog.snap` or `catalog.log`. Examples: a file briefly locked by antivirus or backup software, or a cloud-sync placeholder that fails to download.
- The library folder can't be created or reached.

**Scenario (traced, not run):** after a crash or a sync problem, the user starts LightCraft and sees demo photos. That looks exactly like a brand-new library, so they may assume theirs was reset. They keep rating and editing. Nothing is written, and all of it is gone at quit. The real library files are left alone (good), but nothing tells the user they still exist.

There is also only one snapshot. If `catalog.snap` itself is damaged (by the disk, a sync tool or a bad restore), there's no previous copy to fall back on. The log can't rebuild the catalog by itself, because it's reset after every snapshot.

**Suggested fix:**

- On an open failure, show a blocking dialog with the path and the error, offering **Retry**, **Choose Another Library…**, **Continue Without Saving** (clearly labeled) and **Quit**. Don't seed demo photos in this case.
- While a temporary session is active, show a persistent banner, not only the Settings row.
- Before replacing `catalog.snap`, keep the previous one (for example, rename it to `catalog.snap.prev` before the new one is renamed in). If the snapshot fails to parse, offer to open from `.prev`. The existing `.damaged-N` handling already covers the log side.

title: catalog.log: a partial append followed by a retry is read back as log damage
author: radialmonster
body:
`FsStore::append` writes a batch of records with `write_all` and then `sync_data`. If `write_all` fails partway (disk full, a network share dropping), part of the batch may already be in the file. The error is returned, but the file isn't cut back to its earlier length, and the append handle is kept for the next call.

On `main`, #82 makes the retry routine. Failed ops stay queued, and every command (plus the frame loop, every 2 s) retries them, which is the right behavior. The retry re-encodes the same `seq` numbers and appends them after the partial bytes. The first retried record then shares a line with the torn fragment, so that line fails its check, and later appends are good records.

**On the next load (traced from the code, not run):** a bad line followed by good ones counts as mid-log damage. Replay stops before it, the log is kept as `catalog.log.damaged-N`, and a fresh snapshot is written without everything after that point. A clean quit whose closing snapshot succeeds loses nothing, because that snapshot is written from memory. The loss happens if the app crashes or is killed before the next snapshot, or if the closing snapshot fails too.

**Related: a dead handle is never reopened.** The append handle is dropped only by `write_atomic`/`truncate` on the log. If the handle itself is no longer valid (for example, after an SMB reconnect), every retry fails on it. `close_library` runs `persist()?` before `snapshot()`, so a failing append at quit also skips the snapshot, even though the snapshot opens fresh files and might have worked. On `main` the top bar now says quitting would lose the changes, but the only way out is to quit anyway.

The `Flaky` test store in main's `tests_persist.rs` fails appends cleanly (nothing written), so the partial-write case isn't covered.

**Suggested fix:**

- On an append error, cut the log back to the last good length. `Journal` already tracks `log_bytes`, so it can call `store.truncate(LOG, log_bytes)`. Alternatively, `FsSt…

title: Catalog format: main adds a journal op and snapshot fields without a version bump
author: radialmonster
body:
On `main`, the catalog gains `Op::SetBrowsed` and two new serialized fields, `Catalog.browsed` and `Photo.local_baseline`. `SetBrowsed` is journaled (inside a `Batch`) whenever a Local folder is browsed. `VERSION` in `journal.rs` is still 1. v0.2.0 itself is consistent; this concerns the next release, and how older builds treat a library it has written.

How a v0.2.0 build, or a v0.2.0 `lightcraft-cli`, reads such a library (traced from the code, not run):

- **Log:** `decode_record` returns `None` for an op it can't deserialize, so the record looks corrupt. If good records follow it, `Journal::open` treats it as mid-log damage. Replay stops there, the log is kept as `catalog.log.damaged-N`, and a new snapshot is written without any later edits. If it's the last record, it's dropped as a torn tail and the file is truncated.
- **Snapshot:** serde ignores unknown fields by default, so `browsed` and `local_baseline` load without complaint and are silently dropped when the older build writes its next snapshot.

So: browse a Local folder in a newer build, keep editing, then open the same library with 0.2.0. From the older build's view, the edits after that browse are gone (they're only in the `.damaged-N` file). The browse metadata is lost for good once the old build snapshots. This takes a downgrade, a side-by-side install, or a CLI and app from different releases, so it's not common. But it's presented as "damaged log" rather than "made by a newer version".

The snapshot path already handles this well: `s.version > VERSION` is refused with a clear error. The log has no equivalent.

**Suggested fix (before a release ships `SetBrowsed`):**

- Bump `VERSION` to 2 for snapshots written by builds that know the new op and fields, so older builds refuse the library ("unsupported format … v2") instead of reading it partially.
- In `decode_record`/`Journal::open`, distinguish "CRC matches but the op doesn't deserialize" from "CRC mismatch". The CRC covers the op text, so a CRC-…

title: Settings files: unreadable prefs/presets reset to defaults, ui.json isn't written safely, quit doesn't confirm unsaved changes
author: radialmonster
body:
Three related gaps around the small settings files, all traced from the code, not run.

**1. An unreadable `prefs.json` or `presets.json` silently becomes defaults, which are then saved over it.** `read_json` turns any read or parse error into `None`. Prefs fall back to `PrefsFile::default()`, and presets to the built-ins. The next `save_prefs` (any preference change) writes those defaults over `prefs.json`. That loses export, metadata, filter and curve presets, label sets, LUT profiles, keyword sets and import defaults. The next preset change similarly rewrites `presets.json` without the user presets. The writes themselves are already atomic (`write_atomic`). The gap is on the read side: a transient read error (for example, a file locked by antivirus) is treated like a missing file, and nothing is shown.

*Suggestion:* treat only `NotFound` as "no file". On any other error, keep the file (for example, rename it to `prefs.json.bad-<time>`, or keep a `.bak` from the last good write), show a notice, and don't save over it.

**2. `ui.json` (which holds the chosen library path) is written once, at exit, non-atomically, with errors ignored.** Settings → Open Library only updates the in-memory `library_path`. `save_prefs` in the desktop host runs from `on_exit` and uses `std::fs::write` (truncate + write, no temp file or sync), ignoring the result. If that write is cut short or fails, `load_prefs` returns `None`, and the next launch opens the default `~/Pictures/LightCraft Library`. If that folder doesn't exist, it's created with demo photos, so the user's library seems to have disappeared. A crash before quitting likewise forgets a library opened during that session.

*Suggestion:* write `ui.json` through temp + rename, save it as soon as the library path changes, and on a parse error keep the bad file and say so.

title: File-system calls on the UI thread still block on slow or offline drives (follow-up to #34/#23)
author: radialmonster
body:
This follows up #34 and #23; those fixes are incomplete. #34 moved the sidebar missing count to a background thread, and #23 covered Local browsing, but several other paths still call the file system synchronously from the egui update, either every frame or once per command. On a local SSD that's cheap. When a NAS is asleep, a share has dropped or a USB drive is spinning up, each call can block for the OS or SMB timeout, and the window stops responding. Traced from the code; no durations measured.

- **Grid thumbnails.** Every visible and near-visible cell calls `request_thumb` → `thumb_job` → `MediaCache::source_ref` each frame. When the decoded source isn't in memory, which is normal once thumbnails come from the disk cache, `source_ref` calls `Path::exists()` on the original, and on the smart preview if the original is missing. Scrolling a grid of NAS photos therefore stats each original on the UI thread, repeatedly.
- **Info panel.** Two `exists()` calls per frame for the active photo (original and smart preview).
- **Grid context menu.** `exists()` on the original every frame while the menu is open.
- **Import.** `import::tick` runs `library.import` synchronously, 8 files per frame (copy, verify, probe/hash). Its progress window has no Cancel; the scan window does. Drag and drop calls `library.import` directly, so walking and probing everything dropped happens in one UI-thread call.
- **Missing Photos.** The view filters with `is_missing` (`exists()` per photo) each time the visible list is recomputed. Find Missing Photos walks the chosen folder recursively and stats candidates in one command.
- **Build Smart Previews.** Decodes and encodes every target photo in one synchronous command, with no progress or cancel.
- **Rename Photos dialog.** Runs `photo.renamePreview` every frame. That plans all selected photos and calls `exists()` for each target name.
- **Local tree.** Each expanded folder is re-listed with `read_dir` every 2 s on the UI thread.

title: Rename Photos ignores rollback errors, and Find Missing (name + size only) can't recover the result
author: radialmonster
body:
**Rollback errors are ignored.** `apply_rename` moves files one at a time. If a move fails, it rolls back the earlier ones with `let _ = move_file(b, a)`. The same pattern appears inside `move_file` (sidecars, and the temporary name used for case-only renames) and in `move_files` (undo/redo). A failed rollback is never reported; the error names only the first failure.

**Scenario (traced from the code, not run):** renaming 200 photos on a NAS share, the connection drops at photo 120. That move fails, and so does the rollback of photos 1–119, for the same reason. The user sees "rename X: …". The catalog keeps the old names, since no op is committed, but on disk 119 files and their sidecars now carry the new names. When the share comes back, they all show as missing.

**Find Missing can't repair that.** `library.findMissing` matches by file name (case-insensitive) and, when it's known, file size. Renamed files have different names, so they're never found, and the only way back is Locate, one photo at a time. Name + size can also pick the wrong file when two files share both. That's plausible for uncompressed raws from one camera after a counter reset, and for re-saved copies. The photo's `content_hash` is stored at import but isn't used here.

Also traced: after Convert to DNG or Import → Copy as DNG, the photo keeps the raw's `file_size` and `content_hash`. Find Missing's size check therefore can't match the DNG. That may be intentional for duplicate detection, but it affects relinking.

**Suggested fix:**

- Collect rollback failures. If any files are left renamed, say which (old → new). Better: commit the moves that actually happened, so the catalog matches the disk, and report the rest.
- Find Missing: when no candidate has the right name, fall back to the stored `content_hash`, hashing only files whose size matches, to keep it cheap. When several candidates match by name and size, prefer the hash match, and otherwise skip rather than guess. Report ambiguous match…

title: Convert to DNG and smart previews write directly to the final file, with no temp file, sync or check
author: radialmonster
body:
**Convert to DNG / Import → Copy as DNG.** `write_dng_for` picks a free name with `exists()`, then calls `std::fs::write` on the final name. There's no temp file, no `sync_all` and no read-back. When it returns Ok:

- **Convert to DNG** relinks the photo (and its virtual copies) to the new DNG. The raw is kept, so nothing is deleted. But if the write was cut short, or the drive hadn't flushed (USB unplugged, share dropped, power loss), the catalog now points at a short or corrupt file. A user may archive or delete the raw, trusting the DNG.
- **Copy as DNG** deletes the intermediate raw copy in the destination (`remove_file(&stored)`) as soon as the DNG write returns. The DNG is then the library's only copy, and the import counts as successful, which is when people format the card.

`exists()` followed by `fs::write` is also check-then-write. `fs::write` truncates, so a file created at that name in between would be overwritten (the same pattern as #96).

**Smart previews.** `library.smartPreviews` writes each `.lcsp` with `std::fs::write` straight to the final name, and treats `path.exists()` as "already built". A preview truncated by a crash or a full drive is therefore never rebuilt. `has_smart_preview` reports it as present (the Info panel says "editing the smart preview"), and when the original goes offline the fallback fails to decode, which is exactly when it's needed. Smart previews can now live on a separate drive (#26), which makes partial writes more likely.

All of the above is traced from the code, not reproduced.

**Suggested fix:**

- DNG: write to a temp name in the same folder (`create_new`), `sync_all`, and verify the result: at minimum re-read and compare it with the bytes written, preferably also `lightcraft_raw::decode` it. Then move it to a free final name without overwriting. Relink, or delete the intermediate raw, only after that succeeds. On failure, remove the temp file and keep the raw.
- Smart previews: temp + `sync_all` + rename. When dec…

title: Web build: data-safety gaps to close before people keep real libraries in it
author: radialmonster
body:
The web build is clearly useful as a preview. It runs the same engine and UI, keeps a persistent library in OPFS/IndexedDB, makes no network calls of its own, can't touch originals on disk, and delivers exports as downloads. The points below matter once someone imports their only copies of photos into it and works there over time, which `docs/web.md` ("A persistent library") invites. Everything here is traced from the code, not run in a browser.

- **No way to get a library out.** Imported originals live only in origin storage (`originals/<hash>`), next to the journal. There's no export or backup of either. Browsers may evict the data when `persist()` isn't granted, clear it with site data, or drop it in private mode. Suggest an "Export library" zip of `library/` and `originals/` (with a matching import), plus a hint to keep the originals elsewhere.
- **No cross-tab lock.** Each tab loads its own in-memory mirror and flushes with full rewrites and offset appends (`write_at(offset)`), so two tabs overwrite each other's journal. Suggest `navigator.locks.request(…, {ifAvailable: true})` and a "LightCraft is open in another tab" screen.
- **Save failures reach only the console.** A failed flush (quota, for example) is logged and retried, but nothing is shown. The web `Store` writes to the mirror and never fails, so #82's unsaved warning on `main` can't fire here. If storing an original fails, the photo is still added. It works until reload, then it's gone. Suggest feeding flush errors into the same unsaved state, and failing the import when the original can't be stored.
- **`panic = "abort"`.** `guard::catch` notes that it can't catch anything on wasm. A decoder panic permanently kills a render worker (`on_error` marks it dead). Once all workers are dead, jobs run inline on the main thread, where the same panic stops the app. Because the grid requests the thumbnail again on load, this could repeat after a reload. Suggest a panic hook that shows a message, plus a `?safe`…

title: Trim write-safety work that costs time without protecting anything
author: radialmonster
body:
Several of the safety reports I filed (#93, #96, #106) led to checks that now run on every file. Most of them are worth it. A few, looking at the merged code, cost real time on large batches, especially on USB drives and NAS, without protecting anything that can't be recreated. Some of this traces back to my own reports, so this is a correction to them, not a complaint about the fixes.

**Keep, these are worth it:**
- never writing over an original (#93)
- the XMP merge
- the library lock
- the format version
- Move's verification before a source is deleted
- the DNG check (raws are often deleted after Convert / Copy as DNG)

**1. Exports, renders and screenshots force a disk sync on every file.** `export::write_file` goes through `write_atomic`, which calls `sync_all` on the temp file before the rename. Exports can always be made again from the original, so writing to a temp file and renaming it is enough to keep a half-written file from replacing a good one. The per-file sync makes a 500-photo export to a USB drive or NAS noticeably slower and protects nothing that can't be re-exported. Suggest: a non-syncing atomic write for exports and renders, keeping `write_atomic`'s sync for the catalog, sidecars and settings.
- [crates/engine/src/export.rs:1137-1143](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/65da36675f78f1c85cb7d135669f95e67e524c70/crates/engine/src/export.rs#L1137-L1143)
- [crates/catalog/src/safe_file.rs:114](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/65da36675f78f1c85cb7d135669f95e67e524c70/crates/catalog/src/safe_file.rs#L114)

**2. Import → Copy reads every source file three times.** The probe already reads each file in full and hashes it (`content_hash`). The copy reads it again. Then `copy_verified` compares the copy with the source, which reads the source a third time. From a memory card that is the slow part: roughly one extra full read of the card per import. The verification itself is reasonable, because people format the card after importing…

title: v0.2.0 crashes at startup on Intel UHD 630 (access violation in igvk64.dll, Vulkan driver)
author: FatfishTH
body:
On Windows 11 with an Intel UHD 630 iGPU, lightcraft.exe (v0.2.0, MSI install) exits within 1-2 seconds of launch and no window appears. The same MSI works fine on a Windows 10 machine with an NVIDIA GPU, so the install itself is OK.

### Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- CPU/GPU: Intel Core i5-10400, Intel UHD Graphics 630
- Intel driver: 31.0.101.2115 (2022-11-16)
- LightCraft: v0.2.0, lightcraft-0.2.0-windows-x64.msi

### Symptoms

- Exit code: -1073741819 (0xC0000005)
- Windows Event Log (Application Error):

    - Faulting module: igvk64.dll, version 31.0.101.2115
    - Exception code: 0xc0000005
    - Fault offset: 0x000000000064ea72

- No console output, since v0.2.0 hides the console window on Windows.
- The same MSI works on a Windows 10 machine with an NVIDIA GPU.

### What I tried

- WGPU_BACKEND=dx12 and WGPU_BACKEND=gl made no difference. It still crashed in igvk64.dll, so the app doesn't seem to honor this variable.
- VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_DISABLE=*igvk64* works as a workaround. With it set, the app starts normally on the same machine. I launch it through a small .cmd wrapper that sets the variable before starting lightcraft.exe.

### Expected behavior
The app should not crash when the Vulkan driver misbehaves. A fallback to DX12 or the CPU pipeline (as the README describes) would be ideal, or an option or environment variable to choose the backend or adapter.

title: Default raw tone curve is flatter than Lightroom's (shadows ~1 EV brighter, contrast slope ~1.0 vs ~1.46)
author: echelon
body:
Found while investigating #138. Compared with Lightroom's default rendering (via each file's embedded preview), LightCraft's standard raw tone curve renders shadows and midtones about 1–1.2 EV brighter and highlights dimmer; the log-domain contrast slope is ~1.0 vs ~1.46. The same gap shows on CC0 Canon 5D3 DNGs, CR2 and NEF samples — it's product-wide (tracked as LR-BEHAV-RENDER-FIDELITY in docs/parity.md), not DNG-specific, and it's what users describe as "washed out / like LOG".

Proposal: retune the default base tone toward a camera-like S-curve (steeper toe, ~1.3–1.5 midtone contrast), measured against the planned render-fidelity suite rather than by eye. This changes the look of every existing raw edit, so it needs a maintainer decision (e.g. versioned process defaults so existing edits keep their look).

title: Bracket-aware auto-stacking and batch HDR merge
author: foxandbrand
body:
## Problem
Property and architectural shoots often contain exposure-bracketed sequences mixed with ordinary frames. Even with HDR merge and photo stacks, finding and merging every bracket group manually adds friction to large folder-based shoots and makes automation harder.

## Request
Extend the existing stack and Photo Merge workflows with conservative bracket detection using capture time and EXIF exposure values (shutter speed, aperture, ISO, and exposure compensation where available). Let photographers review or adjust detected groups, then batch-merge selected or all high-confidence groups through the UI and CLI/MCP workflow. Keep source files unchanged and make merge outputs easy to review alongside their source brackets.

## Acceptance criteria
- Detect likely exposure brackets without grouping unrelated burst frames or adjacent compositions.
- Show the grouped source frames before merge; allow splitting, combining, or excluding a group.
- Support batch HDR merge for selected or high-confidence groups and expose the same operation to automation clients.
- Preserve originals and report groups that are incomplete or unsuitable for a confident merge.

title: colorRange mask selects the whole photo when driven from the CLI (v0.2.1)
author: foxandbrand
body:
A `colorRange` mask created and sampled from the CLI applies its adjustment to the whole photo, not only to the sampled color. The `refine` value makes no difference. Shape masks behave correctly, so it looks specific to color range.

**Version**

v0.2.1 (`fc3fa1a`), built from source with `cargo build --release --locked -p lightcraft-cli`. macOS 27.0, Apple Silicon. Headless (`lightcraft-cli run --import`).

**Steps to reproduce**

Make a test image with two flat patches, a blue-green one on the left and a neutral gray one on the right:

```sh
magick -size 600x400 xc:'rgb(120,150,155)' \( -size 600x400 xc:'rgb(200,198,195)' \) +append -quality 95 two-patches.jpg
```

Add a color-range mask, sample the left patch, and warm it:

```sh
lightcraft-cli run --import two-patches.jpg \
  mask.add kind=colorRange \
  mask.sampleColor x=0.25 y=0.5 \
  mask.adjust 'values={"temp":55,"tint":-35}' \
  app.export path=out.jpg quality=95 percent=100
```

All four commands return `"ok": true`. `mask.sampleColor` returns one sample, `[0.6012, -0.0211, -0.0126]`, and `develop.get` shows it stored on the mask's `colorRange` component with `refine: 50`.

**Expected**

Only the left patch changes. The gray patch on the right was not sampled and is a clearly different color, so it should be outside the mask.

**Actual**

Both patches change by about the same amount. Mean RGB of a 100 px block in each patch:

| | Left (sampled) | Right (not sampled) |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 121, 150, 156 | 199, 198, 194 |

title: fix(desktop): --memory session overwrites ui.json though --help says nothing is saved
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`lightcraft --help` describes `--memory` as a "throwaway in-memory session (alias --demo); nothing is saved", and the README calls it a session that "writes nothing". A `--memory` session still writes the app settings file `ui.json` in the config directory once any UI state changes, unless `LIGHTCRAFT_NO_PREFS` is set. When the user already has a `ui.json`, the throwaway session's UI changes replace the saved values in it, so the next normal launch starts with the throwaway session's settings.

## Runtime or environment

- LightCraft v0.2.1 release, `lightcraft-0.2.1-macos-universal.dmg` from the GitHub release (checksum verified against `SHA256SUMS.txt`), app bundle `ai.storyteller.lightcraft` 0.2.1.
- `main` at commit 5cee0c08d00245a0660d3de3ced6d7e18528a667, built with `cargo build --release -p lightcraft` (rustc 1.95.0).
- macOS 27.0.1, arm64. `lightcraft-cli` 0.2.1 drove the control channel.

## Steps to reproduce

Run every launch with `HOME` pointed at an empty scratch folder so the real config directory is untouched. On macOS the config directory is then `$HOME/Library/Application Support/LightCraft` (`config_dir()` in `apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs`).

```sh
export SCRATCH=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/home"
APP=/path/to/LightCraft.app/Contents/MacOS/LightCraft   # or target/release/lightcraft

HOME="$SCRATCH/home" "$APP" --memory --control 18732 &
until lightcraft-cli run --connect 127.0.0.1:18732 ui.inspect >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 0.5; done
lightcraft-cli run --connect 127.0.0.1:18732 ui.set thumbSize=300
sleep 5
lightcraft-cli run --connect 127.0.0.1:18732 app.quit
find "$SCRATCH/home" -type f
grep thumbSize "$SCRATCH/home/Library/Application Support/LightCraft/ui.json"
```

To see an existing file overwritten, first place a `ui.json` with `"thumbSize": 150.0` (and any `settings.libraryPath`) in `$SCRATCH/home/Library/Application Support/LightCraft/`, then run the same steps.

title: Exported JPEGs differ on every run because the embedded ICC profile header carries the current time
author: htdtkshi
body:
## Summary

Rendering the same photo with the same settings twice produces files that are not byte-identical. The first differing byte is inside the embedded `ICC_PROFILE` segment, and the creation date/time in the ICC profile header equals the wall-clock time of the export. Pixel data is identical (PNG exports of the same photo compared with PIL `ImageChops.difference` have an empty bounding box). This makes output hashes unusable for regression checks and causes spurious diffs when exports are synced or versioned.

## Environment

- LightCraft CLI 0.2.1 (`lightcraft-0.2.1-linux-x86_64`), Ubuntu on x86_64 (GitHub Codespace), headless
- Input: Nikon Z 6 `.NEF` (shown as embedded preview in 0.2.1, see Notes)

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
L=lightcraft-cli
for i in 1 2 3; do $L render DSC_0750.NEF -o np$i.jpg --size 800; sleep 2; done
md5sum np*.jpg                      # three different hashes
cmp np1.jpg np2.jpg                 # differ at a byte inside the ICC_PROFILE APP2 segment
python3 - <<'PY'
import struct
for f in ('np1.jpg','np2.jpg','np3.jpg'):
    d=open(f,'rb').read(); i=d.find(b'ICC_PROFILE\x00'); icc=d[i+14:i+14+128]
    print(f, struct.unpack('>6H', icc[24:36]))   # ICC header creation date/time
PY
```

## Expected

Identical input and settings give byte-identical output (the ICC header date is a fixed value, e.g. zero or a constant).

## Actual

```
np1.jpg ICC header date (2026, 10, 7, 3, 41, 32)
np2.jpg ICC header date (2026, 10, 7, 3, 41, 35)
np3.jpg ICC header date (2026, 10, 7, 3, 41, 37)
```
These match the file modification times of the three exports (03:41:32 / 03:41:35 / 03:41:37 UTC). `md5sum` of the three files is different each time.

## Notes

- Measured n=3 JPEG exports (and a further 12 renders with presets/grain, all with distinct md5 per run). PNG exports of the same photo, same settings, were pixel-identical (n=2).
- Only the JPEG ICC header was inspected; other formats were not checked for the same field.

title: `app.export` accepts unknown parameter names and unparseable values without any error, so typos change nothing silently
author: htdtkshi
body:
## Summary

`photo.rate` and `crop.set` validate their parameters (`rating must be 0..5`, `missing number rating`, `rect needs 4 numbers`), but `app.export` returns `ok:true` for misspelled parameter names and for non-numeric values, and exports with defaults instead. In a script or agent run the typo is invisible: for example `longEdgee=400` writes a 3000 px file, and `longEdge=banana` writes a full-size 6048 px file.

## Environment

- LightCraft CLI 0.2.1 (`lightcraft-0.2.1-linux-x86_64`), Ubuntu x86_64, headless
- Input: Nikon Z 6 `.NEF`

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
L=lightcraft-cli; mkdir -p o
$L run --import DSC_0750.NEF app.export path=o/t1.jpg longEdgee=400          # typo in key
$L run --import DSC_0750.NEF app.export path=o/t2.jpg longEdge=400 qualty=5   # typo in key
$L run --import DSC_0750.NEF app.export path=o/t3.jpg longEdge=400 quality=5  # correct key, for comparison
$L run --import DSC_0750.NEF app.export path=o/t4.jpg longEdge=banana         # non-numeric value
$L run --import DSC_0750.NEF photo.rate rating=9                               # for comparison
$L run --import DSC_0750.NEF photo.rate ratng=3                                # for comparison
```

## Expected

An error such as `invalid parameters for app.export: unknown parameter longEdgee` / `longEdge must be a number`, as other commands already return.

## Actual

```
longEdgee=400   -> ok:true, wrote 3000 x 1996 (default longEdge 3000)
qualty=5        -> ok:true, 32386 bytes   (quality=5 gives 7453 bytes)
longEdge=banana -> ok:true, wrote 6048 x 4024 (full size), 2023553 bytes
photo.rate rating=9 -> ok:false "invalid parameters for `photo.rate`: rating must be 0..5"
photo.rate ratng=3  -> ok:false "invalid parameters for `photo.rate`: missing number `rating`"
```

## Notes

- Measured n=2 (identical results both runs).
- Not checked: whether other commands besides `app.export` also ignore unknown keys.

title: MCP `select_photos` with a nonexistent photo id returns `selected: 1` and leaves no usable active photo
author: htdtkshi
body:
## Summary

In a headless `lightcraft-cli mcp --demo` session, `select_photos {"ids":[9999]}` (an id that does not exist) returns a success result `{"selected": 1}`. The following `render_photo` then fails with `no such photo`, and `get_develop` fails with `no photo`, so the session has silently lost its active photo. A client has no way to tell from the `select_photos` response that the selection was invalid.

## Environment

- LightCraft CLI 0.2.1 (`lightcraft-0.2.1-linux-x86_64`), Ubuntu x86_64, MCP over stdio, protocol 2025-06-18, `lightcraft-cli mcp --demo`

## Steps to reproduce

Send over stdin to `lightcraft-cli mcp --demo` (after `initialize`), in order:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"render_photo","arguments":{"size":32}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"select_photos","arguments":{"ids":[9999]}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":4,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"render_photo","arguments":{"size":32}}}
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":5,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_develop","arguments":{}}}
```

## Expected

Call 3 returns `isError: true` (e.g. `no such photo`) and the previously active photo stays active, so calls 4 and 5 still succeed.

## Actual

```
render_photo {size:32}     -> isError=false  <image content>
select_photos {ids:[9999]} -> isError=false  {"selected": 1}
render_photo {size:32}     -> isError=true   no such photo
get_develop {}             -> isError=true   invalid parameters for `develop.get`: no photo
```

## Notes

- Measured n=2 fresh processes, identical results.
- Related observation (same session type, n=2): `get_develop {"id":9999}` and `apply_preset {"preset":"lc.warm-glow","ids":[9999]}` also return `isError=false` for the unknown id.

title: `app.export` `watermark` object: accepted keys and the unit of `size` are not documented, and out-of-range `size` is silently clamped

title: In-window menu bar: dropdowns open over their menu titles (Linux/Wayland)
author: theDavidCoen
body:
## Summary

On Linux (Wayland), in-window top-menu dropdowns open **on top of** their menu title instead of below it. The first items sit where the menu label should be, so the bar looks covered/eaten by the popup.

Same class of bug as in PhotoCraft (egui 0.36 in-window menubar).

## Screenshot

![LightCraft Photo menu overlapping the Photo title](https://files.catbox.moe/1lu9y6.png)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run LightCraft 0.2.1 linux-x86_64 AppImage on Linux/Wayland.
2. Click **Photo** (or other top-level menus) in the in-window menu bar.
3. Observe the dropdown position relative to the title.

## Expected

Dropdown opens **below** the menu title (native menubar behaviour). The title stays visible above the popup.

## Actual

Dropdown top edge aligns with the top of the menu bar / window content; the popup covers the title (e.g. “Photo”). Submenus inherit the same vertical offset.

## Environment

- LightCraft 0.2.1 (linux-x86_64 AppImage)
- Linux CachyOS, **Wayland** (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`)
- egui / eframe **0.36** (in-window bar via `menubar::show_in_window` → `egui::Popup::menu`)

## Notes / likely cause

- macOS uses the native menu bar; this affects hosts that draw the in-window bar (Linux/Windows/web).
- egui `Popup::menu` defaults to `RectAlign::BOTTOM_START` but `get_best_align()` can pick alternatives (`TOP_START`, etc.). If the chosen align is “above” and then clamped to the window top, the popup overlaps the bar — which matches these screenshots.
- PhotoCraft has the same symptom with `egui::MenuBar` + `ui.menu_button` (filing a sibling issue there).

## Suggested direction

- Force menu popups to prefer below-the-button alignment for the top bar (or disable upward alternatives for top-level menus).
- Verify popup anchor/`screen_rect` under Wayland + eframe 0.36.

title: Import Photos…: File menu stays open; app then stops responding when the file dialog appears (Linux/Wayland)
author: theDavidCoen
body:
## Summary

Choosing **File → Import Photos…** opens the native file picker, but the File dropdown stays drawn on top of the UI. Shortly after, GNOME reports LightCraft as not responding (`«LightCraft (0.2.1)» non risponde`). Force-quit yields AppImageLauncher `child exited with code 9` (SIGKILL).

## Steps to reproduce

1. LightCraft 0.2.1 AppImage on Linux/Wayland.
2. **File → Import Photos…** (or Ctrl+Shift+I).
3. Observe the File menu still open behind/over the file dialog.
4. Interact with the dialog or wait — the app is marked not responding.

## Expected

- The menu popup closes as soon as the command runs.
- The native file dialog is usable without freezing the app.

## Actual

- Menu chrome remains open (same class of in-window menu issues as #189).
- UI freezes / “not responding”; journal shows:
  ```
  [appimagelauncher-binfmt-bypass/lib] ERROR: child exited with code 9
  ```
  after force quit. No Rust panic line in journal — process killed after hang.

## Notes / likely cause

- `file.addPhotos` calls `services.pick_files` which is a **blocking** `rfd::FileDialog::pick_files()` on the UI thread (`apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs`).
- Opening a modal native dialog while an egui `Popup::menu` is still open is a common Wayland/egui freeze pattern.
- Fix direction: close all menu popups before invoking `rfd`, and/or run the picker off the render path (deferred to next frame after `ui.close()`).

## Environment

- LightCraft 0.2.1 (linux-x86_64 AppImage)
- Linux CachyOS, Wayland (GNOME)
- Screenshots: File menu still open with Import Photos… highlighted while the GTK “Apri” dialog is shown; then the system not-responding dialog.

title: XMP photo import silently ignores the selected CameraProfile (Canon Camera Faithful)
author: franciscoxc
body:
Importing a Lightroom-edited DNG carries over settings such as Exposure, but does not tell the user that the selected camera profile was omitted. This makes the migration appear more complete than it is and makes color differences difficult to diagnose.

I understand that camera-matching looks are still missing and Adobe profile formats are deliberately unsupported. This report is about surfacing the unsupported selection during photo import, rather than requesting that proprietary profile assets be bundled.

## File and observed behavior

The file is an Adobe DNG converted from a Canon EOS 6D CR2, with develop settings embedded in XMP:

| Metadata | Value |
| --- | --- |
| DNG embedded `ProfileName` | `Adobe Standard` |
| XMP `crs:CameraProfile` | `Camera Faithful` |
| XMP `crs:Exposure2012` | `+1.68` |
| XMP white balance | Custom, Temperature 6200, Tint +16 |
| XMP `crs:HDREditMode` | `0` |

ExifTool reported no `ExtraCameraProfiles` tag and no additional `ProfileName` for this file. The XMP profile name alone does not supply the selected profile's rendering data.

On macOS, LightCraft 0.2.1 (build `fc3fa1a71b67b3bb2aeccbf0b164bd9543288b9f`) shows the imported +1.68 Exposure, but the image differs substantially from Lightroom. This appearance observation predates the DNG profile-table fix in #145; it is not a claim that #145 failed.

## Source evidence

At main commit `707138f3fe35c46b26f98afdfa12a5d8f44f1abc`:

- [`crs::to_partial_report`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/707138f3fe35c46b26f98afdfa12a5d8f44f1abc/crates/engine/src/crs.rs#L355-L388) returns both imported settings and unmapped field names, including CameraProfile.
- [Photo XMP import](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/707138f3fe35c46b26f98afdfa12a5d8f44f1abc/crates/engine/src/sidecar.rs#L161-L168) keeps only the settings tuple member and drops the unmapped list.

title: XMP Upright import drops saved transforms and recalculates Lightroom geometry
author: franciscoxc
body:
The Lightroom XMP importer carries over `PerspectiveUpright`, but not the saved `UprightTransform_*` matrices. With Auto selected, LightCraft then solves its own transform. Consequently, carrying over the mode does not preserve the geometry saved by Lightroom.

## File and metadata

The affected file is an Adobe DNG converted from a Canon EOS 6D CR2. Its embedded XMP contains:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `crs:PerspectiveUpright` | `1` (Auto) |
| `crs:UprightVersion` | `151388160` |
| `crs:UprightTransformCount` | `6` |
| `crs:UprightCenterNormX` | `0.554156` |
| `crs:UprightCenterNormY` | `0.529745` |
| TIFF orientation | `1` (normal) |

The saved `crs:UprightTransform_1` is:

```text
0.897233402,-0.013204641,-0.030578613,
-0.096087436,0.953621255,0.003270197,
-0.157075841,-0.043520282,1.000000000
```

The packet contains no `HasCrop`, `CropLeft`, `CropTop`, `CropRight`, `CropBottom`, or `CropAngle` fields. This is therefore a saved Upright geometry issue, not evidence that explicit manual crop coordinates failed to import.

The user reported that the framing did not match Lightroom in LightCraft 0.2.1 on macOS (build `fc3fa1a71b67b3bb2aeccbf0b164bd9543288b9f`).

## Source evidence

At main commit `707138f3fe35c46b26f98afdfa12a5d8f44f1abc`:

- [The CRS geometry importer](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/707138f3fe35c46b26f98afdfa12a5d8f44f1abc/crates/engine/src/crs.rs#L316-L352) maps `PerspectiveUpright` to the mode, without importing the stored Upright matrices.
- [`upright::resolve`](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/707138f3fe35c46b26f98afdfa12a5d8f44f1abc/crates/pipeline/src/upright.rs#L588-L596) computes a new automatic transform whenever an automatic mode is enabled and no stored transform is available.
- [The photo import path](https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/blob/707138f3fe35c46b26f98afdfa12a5d8f44f1abc/crates/engine/src/sidecar.rs#L161-L168) discards the unmapped-field diagnostics returned by the CRS importer, so the om…

author: Jagalite
body:

title: [Bug] WebGL context loss blanks the editor while exports continue
author: Jagalite
body:
The entire browser editor becomes blank after its actual WebGL2 context is lost. Production export commands still download correct PNGs, but the user cannot see the editor or an actionable recovery explanation.

## Environment

- Current main `7aab3fd97fed00ffcebdd3cca7fede12f7672194`, fresh release browser build and rechecked on 2026-10-07.
- Rust 1.95.0, wasm-bindgen 0.2.129; local COOP/COEP host, `?store=memory&workers=0`, actual WebGL2 UI context.
- macOS 26.5.2 arm64, Apple M1; isolated headless Chrome 154.0.8037.93, Firefox 155.0 and Playwright WebKit 26.6 (not Safari).

## Reproduction

1. Import a generated 128×128 white PNG with a 32×32 red upper-left corner. Select its detail view.
2. Export PNG and verify the original pixels. Set exposure to −1 EV and export again; verify the expected 188-valued red/gray samples (RGB tolerance 2).
3. Obtain the editor's already-created WebGL2 context from its canvas. The controlled run observed `getContext` before startup to retain that actual context, rather than creating a separate test context.
4. Call `gl.getExtension('WEBGL_lose_context').loseContext()`. Observe the actual `webglcontextlost` event and `gl.isContextLost() === true`.
5. Allow the application to process the loss, inspect the complete viewport, and export PNG again through the production API.

> Exported 0 of 1 photo · 1 failed: green_test.png: Access is denied. (os error 5)

title: [Feature Request] API support for external devices (eg. MIDI controllers)
author: hybridvision
body:
Hello!

First of all, thank you for taking on this mammoth project, I'm really excited to see where it leads! I've used Lightroom since the initial beta (almost 20 years!) and I once respected Adobe as a company but now I despise them. It fills me with hope to see a community-backed alternative emerging.

Since the project is so young, this request is possibly a bit premature but I thought it was worth mentioning now so it can hopefully be implemented as a core feature.

As a professional photographer, I often have to edit many hundreds or thousands of photos and having a comfortable way to interact with the software is critical. For many years, I've used MIDI controllers and software like MIDI2LR or Intech Studio's Grid Editor to streamline my editing workflow.

Workflows are highly personal, so I'd like to see an accessible API that allows external software to send commands to LightCraft. I don't know if sockets are the best approach but it would also be important to be able to receive data from LightCraft when the state of the image changes in the software – this is so the external controller can keep in sync and show appropriate feedback (eg. updating LEDs based on slider values when changing photos or adjusting them with the GUI sliders).

If you look at the work done in [MIDI2LR](https://github.com/rsjaffe/midi2lr) or at Lightroom's official SDK, you'll see that it can be quite awkward to use and there are still many gaps in functionality. Full coverage is probably not realistic but I'd love to see a robust, consistent API that other apps / devices can build upon.

Thanks for your time and efforts so far!

title: RW2 raw format 8: the two green samples of each 2×2 cell are swapped (zipper/colour fringe on every edge)
author: radialmonster
body: Follow-up to #215 (thanks for it: every one of my G9 II files now opens as a real raw). ## What happens On raw format 8 files (GH6, GH7, G9 II, S5 II / IIX, S9, S1R II, S1 II), every sharp edge at 100% has a one-pixel teal/orange zipper and a dark outline. The camera JPEG and other raw formats don't have it. Flat areas look right, so the colour checks and the camera-look fit don't catch it. Each image: a 320 px crop at 100%, shown at 2× (default settings, full-size export). **1** is the camera JPEG, which is what LightCraft showed before #215. **2** is main (`2694d70`, #215 as merged). **3** has the fix below. *Panasonic DC-G9M2, LUMIX G 25/F1.7, ISO 100. The geometry difference between 1 and 2/3 is the missing lens distortion correction, a separate issue.* ## Cause `decode_strip` places a cell's four decoded values in row order: `k / 2` is the row and `k % 2` the column. The stream holds them column by column (top-left, bottom-left, top-right, bottom-right). In an RGGB cell, the only difference is that the two greens trade sites, so every green sample sits one pixel off diagonally. The `format8_strips_round_trip` test encodes in the same row order, so it round-trips either way. Measurements, all from decoded sensor data: - **One vertical edge, 44 rows** (G9 II): red and blue cross the edge at x ≈ 2759.9 on every row. Green on even rows crosses at 2760.8, and green on odd rows at 2758.9, about 2 px apart. With the fix, all four sites cross at 2759.8–2759.9. - **Whole image**, estimated offset of the Gb plane against the Gr plane in half-resolution cells. Correct Bay…

title: RW2: apply the distortion correction Panasonic cameras embed in the file
author: radialmonster
body: Follow-up to #215, whose "Not in this PR" list notes that Panasonic's embedded lens correction isn't applied. ## What happens Panasonic and Leica (Micro Four Thirds and L-mount) cameras record the lens's distortion correction in every RW2/RWL. They apply it to their own JPEG, and many of these lenses are designed to rely on it. LightCraft renders the raw without it, so geometry differs from the camera JPEG, and on wide and kit zooms straight lines bow. I measured it on two of my bodies by fitting a radial polynomial, r_src = scale · r · (1 + k1·r² + k2·r⁴) with r normalised to the half-diagonal, between LightCraft's raw render and the camera JPEG embedded in the same file. One fit per photo lines them up, taking the whole-image correlation from 0.1–0.65 to 0.86–0.99. That's the same model as the DNG `WarpRectilinear` opcode LightCraft already applies. | Camera, lens (photos) | Focal length | k1 | k2 | Missing shift at the corner | |---|---|---|---|---| | DC-G9M2, LUMIX G 25/1.7 (5) | 25 mm | −0.019 to −0.022 | −0.015 to −0.016 | 126–135 px of 5776 (2.2–2.3 %) | | DMC-GX85, LUMIX G 25/1.7 (30) | 25 mm | −0.020 to −0.027 | −0.012 to −0.017 | 39–47 px of 1920 (2.0–2.5 %) | | DMC-GX85, G VARIO 12–32 (9) | 12–13 mm | −0.105 to −0.115 | +0.028 to +0.037 | 95–97 px of 1920 (≈ 5 %) | | DMC-GX85, G VARIO 12–32 (1) | 17 mm | −0.069 | +0.013 | 69 px of 1920 | | DMC-GX85, G VARIO 12–32 (1) | 20 mm | −0.047 | +0.009 | 47 px of 1920 | | DMC-GX85, G VARIO 12–32 (3) | 32 mm | +0.009 to +0.011 | ≈ 0 | 4 px of 1920 (scale 0.986) | The same lens on two bodies gives the same correction, so it follows the lens data in the file, as expected. The GX85 embeds a 1920 × 1440 camera JPEG, and its renders were compared at that size.

Today neither the user nor a maintainer can find out why without running it from a terminal.
