title: Panic in detail filmstrip when file name contains CJK characters (byte-index truncation)
author: chunhc0531
body:
**Version:** v0.2.1 (macOS, Apple Silicon)

### What happens
The app exits (code 101, Rust panic) as soon as the detail view's filmstrip shows a photo whose file name contains multi-byte (CJK) characters. Since the panic message only goes to stderr, from the Dock it just looks like the app silently quits.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Import a folder containing e.g. `202407層三限定訂閱圖(4).jpg`
2. Open any photo in the detail view so that file appears in the filmstrip
3. App panics

### Panic
```
thread 'main' panicked at crates/ui-egui/src/panels/detail.rs:1263:78:
end byte index 13 is not a char boundary; it is inside '限' (bytes 12..15 of string)
   4: lightcraft_ui_egui::panels::detail::filmstrip::{closure#0}
   6: lightcraft_ui_egui::panels::detail::filmstrip
   7: lightcraft_ui_egui::panels::detail::show
```

### Cause
The filmstrip label truncates by byte index (still present on main, `detail.rs:1539`):
```rust
let short: String = if name.len() > 14 { format!("{}…", &name[..13]) } else { name.to_string() };
```
Suggested fix — truncate by chars:
```rust
let short: String = if name.chars().count() > 14 {
    format!("{}…", name.chars().take(13).collect::<String>())
} else {
    name.to_string()
};
```

### Note
Renaming the files on disk doesn't help, because the catalog keeps the old `file_name`; the library had to be rebuilt. It may be worth grepping for other `&name[..n]`-style byte slicing on user-provided strings.

title: Apple ProRAW: JPEG XL–compressed DNGs are rejected
author: BuonBreda
body:
Recent iPhones can save ProRAW with JPEG XL compression (Settings ▸ Camera ▸ Formats, "JPEG-XL lossless / lossy"). Those DNGs use Compression = 52546, which `crates/raw/src/dng.rs` rejects with `Unsupported("JPEG XL DNG")`, so they fall back to the embedded preview: no raw editing, no full-resolution export.

`jxl-oxide` is already a workspace dependency (`crates/codecs/src/jxl.rs`), so decoding the JXL-compressed tiles in the DNG path (DNG 1.7, JXL tiles of LinearRaw / CFA data) looks feasible without new dependencies.

Related: #273 applies the ProRAW `ProfileGainTableMap` (local tone mapping); lossless-JPEG ProRAW files already decode fine.

_Opened with the help of Claude Code._

title: [Feature Request] Networked Catalogs and Multi-User Support (Long-Term Architectural Consideration)
author: thebundok
body:
# [Feature Request] Networked Catalogs and Multi-User Support (Long-Term Architectural Consideration)

### Summary

I understand that LightCraft's current priority is achieving feature parity with Lightroom/Lightroom Classic, but I'd like to propose a longer-term feature that Lightroom Classic has notably lacked: **support for centralized, network-hosted catalogs accessible by multiple users and computers.**

The ability to maintain a shared photo library on a NAS or local server, with multiple users accessing and editing that library from their respective workstations, would be a significant improvement for households, small teams, and collaborative photography workflows.

### Proposed Functionality

Ideally, this would include:

- **Network-hosted catalogs:** Store and manage a centralized catalog on a NAS or local server, rather than requiring a separate local catalog on each workstation.
- **Multi-computer access:** Allow the same catalog to be opened from different computers without requiring manual synchronization or duplication.
- **Multi-user support:** Allow multiple users to work within the same photo library, maintaining consistent metadata, organization, ratings, collections, and edits.
- **Concurrent access (ideally):** Support multiple active users simultaneously, with appropriate mechanisms for coordinating changes and preventing conflicts.

Even sequential access from multiple workstations, without simultaneous editing, would be a substantial improvement over Lightroom Classic.

### Architectural Considerations

This has been a longstanding Lightroom feature request, but my understanding is that Lightroom Classic's architecture makes it particularly challenging to implement reliably. Database integrity, concurrent writes, conflicting edits, preview management, and synchronization all introduce significant complexity.

Looking through LightCraft's repository, I noticed that the catalog architecture appears to use an operation log and snapshots rather …

title: Hold on, I’ve spent the last year working through these same problems
author: dagnele89
body:
Hi everyone,

I’m Daniele, a photographer and full-stack developer. I’ve spent the last year building RedLnx, a complete photo editor written in Rust that I’m preparing to release under the AGPL. I'm in the last bug fix to dehaze pipeline (a little one) and in the clean up. It's finished.

I’ve been reading your code, going through the issues, and following the commits. If your goal is to break free from Lightroom, there’s a lot of wheel-reinventing happening here.

I’m saying this because I recognise the problems you’re running into. I’ve spent the past year working through them, including quite a few that go well beyond demosaicing or checking outputs against a reference.

Colour-space consistency. White balance. Noise reduction. Local inference. Catalog management. Three operating systems and their filesystem differences. The interface. Smart masks. AI denoising. ONNX models. Cropping. Camera colour profiles. Lens corrections and distortion. And the legal work involved in understanding what you can actually ship.

I could keep going for an hour.

My autistic brain wouldn’t let me leave those details alone. I’ve already worked through a lot of what you’re tackling now, and a lot of what comes after it. You don’t have to take my word for that: I’m going to release the source so you can inspect it, run it, and judge it yourselves. If parts are useful to you, you’re welcome to build on them under the AGPL.

That’s why watching this feels so surreal.

From the outside, the story looks like “Claude, make me Lightroom and don’t make mistakes,” followed a week later by everyone talking about a Lightroom replacement. Meanwhile, getting even half of Lightroom’s functionality to a standard you can actually trust with your photographs involves a hell of a lot more than getting the controls onto the screen.

I use AI to write code too. I know how quickly it can produce something that runs. I also know how much work comes after that.

So yes, this is partly a frustrated photog…

LightCraft (v0.2.1) crashes immediately on the second launch on a Windows system using an Intel integrated GPU. title: [BUG] v0.4.0 macOS: Simplified Chinese UI is all tofu — release.yml pins a craft-fonts commit from before Noto Sans CJK SC
author: Ryker0716
body:
### What happens

On the **official v0.4.0 macOS build**, switching **Settings ▸ Language ▸ 简体中文** turns the whole UI (menus, panels, tooltips, status bar) into tofu/□ boxes. English and 日本語 render correctly.

Installing a Chinese system font does **not** help, and can't: LightCraft is egui-based and `theme::font_definitions` builds its `FontDefinitions` from `include_bytes!` (Inter) plus `CRAFT_FONTS` only — nothing is read from the OS font stack at run time. (I tried `brew install --cask font-noto-sans-cjk-sc` first, as a normal macOS user would.)

### Environment

- LightCraft v0.4.0, build `2472021091a28eb93a05947cfc9b941d3911543a`, from `lightcraft-0.4.0-macos-universal.dmg`
- sha256 `c74e45230a54bce09bf86cecee7e22f3374ee46f8ba779ddda3f4ee7910d3f5c` — identical to `SHA256SUMS.txt`, so this is the shipped artifact, not a bad download
- macOS 26.7.1 (25G241), Apple M4

### Root cause: the craft-fonts pin predates Noto Sans CJK SC

`release.yml` checks out `storytold/craft-fonts` at `ref: abb83316d96aa59c1cf64784289e378fe9fa5695` (2026-10-06 14:03Z). That commit's `fonts/manifest.txt` lists only the Japanese faces:

```
Shippori Mincho   | Regular | … | Jpan,Latn
BIZ UDPGothic     | Regular | … | Jpan,Latn
BIZ UDPGothic     | Bold    | … | Jpan,Latn
BIZ UDMincho      | Regular | … | Jpan,Latn
```

`Noto Sans CJK SC` (and Noto Sans Arabic) landed in craft-fonts the same day at `8dcdacd5153e` (2026-10-06 18:29Z) — *after* the pin. The pin was never bumped: on `main` today, all five `ref: abb83316…` occurrences are still that commit.

So the v0.4.0 binaries embed no face for `Hans`, `engine::fonts::cjk_fallback(craft, "Hans", …)` falls back to the Japanese faces, and they have no glyphs for most simplified forms. `CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED=1` can't catch it — the pinned manifest is valid, just old.

Evidence in the shipped app bundle:

- `Contents/Resources/Licenses/` contains exactly `OFL-biz-ud-mincho.txt`, `OFL-biz-ud-pgothic.txt`, `OFL-shippori-mincho.txt` (+ Inter) —…

Importing a `.cube` LUT via **File → Import Profiles & Presets…** succeeds on the engine side, but the imported profile is never shown anywhere in the UI. So there is no way to apply it from the app.

## Environment
- LightCraft v0.2.1, Windows 11 x64
- Code on `main` / v0.4.0 looks identical in the relevant files, so this probably still happens there.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open a library stored on disk (not `--memory`).

title: Canon PowerShot and EOS M CR2s open with a strong green cast: no as-shot white balance is read
author: radialmonster
body:
## Problem

CR2 files from many Canon PowerShot and EOS M bodies open green. Neutral areas (snow, grey stone, sky) measure a* about -13 and b* about +10 against the camera's own JPEG, and the photo reports no as-shot white balance at all (multipliers 1, 1, 1, white point `d65Default`).

Of the 134 `.CR2` files in the raw.pixls.us CC0 archive, 25 are affected. All have the maker-note `ColorData` (tag `0x4001`, ExifTool `ColorDataVersion` -3 or -4) stored as one `undef[5120]` value, and the decoder (`crates/raw/src/vendor/cr2.rs`) reads the tag as a list of numbers. On the 104 files where the tag is a list of 16-bit integers (`int16u[...]`) white balance is read fine.

Affected models (one file each in the archive): PowerShot S95, S100, S100V, S110, S120, G1 X, G1 X Mark II, G1 X Mark III, G3 X, G5 X, G7 X, G7 X Mark II, G9 X, G9 X Mark II, G11, G12, G15, G16, SX50 HS, SX60 HS; EOS M3, M5, M6, M10, M100. Other bodies with the same ColorData versions are probably affected too.

The PowerShot G9 has no `ColorData` at all and stays without white balance. That is a separate case.

## Cause

The reader asks the maker note for the tag's values as numbers. For an UNDEFINED value that gives one number per byte, so the probe for the as-shot `R G G B` levels (it tries word offsets such as 63, 25, 71 ...) sees values below 256 and accepts nothing.

The same data read as little-endian 16-bit words (the maker note's byte order) holds the as-shot levels at word 71, an offset the probe already knows. For the S110 it reads `1988 745 745 1641`; ExifTool prints the same values as `WB_RGGBLevelsAsShot` (and `ColorTempAsShot` 8428 at word 75). The two greens are identical in all 25 files, and the levels give plausible multipliers (R/G 1.39 to 2.67, B/G 1.17 to 2.61).

## Proposed fix

Read a maker-note array by its stored type: BYTE/UNDEFINED data is paired into 16-bit words in the maker note's byte order, other types are read as before. No per-model table, no new offsets.

Use model-backed segmentation for the existing Subject, Background and Sky mask buttons. This would make those one-click actions useful for selecting actual image content without requiring users to discover the Object/Describe workaround.

- Subject uses centre-weighted local contrast, rather than a segmented subject.
- Background inverts that heuristic Subject mask.
- Sky uses brightness, colour and vertical position heuristics.
- Object and Describe already have a model-backed segmentation path.

title: TIFF raws with a thumbnail-only first image (Phase One / Leaf IIQ, Canon EOS-1D / 1Ds, Kodak DCS) open as a tiny ordinary image, with no "preview only" label
author: radialmonster
body:
## What happens

Some raw files keep their raw data in a private block of a TIFF. IFD0 is only a small RGB copy (160 to 640 px), no IFD has a CFA photometric or a raw compression, so `probe()` returns `None` and the file is imported as a plain TIFF of that size. A 150 MP Phase One IQ4 file imports as 640x480, a P65+ IIQ renders 296x220. Nothing says it is only a preview.

Measured on the raw.pixls.us CC0 archive (1870 files, main `48cd9c5`): 50 files, all of them Phase One / Leaf IIQ (`.IIQ`, some `.TIF`) plus Canon EOS-1D, EOS-1Ds and Kodak EOS DCS 3 `.TIF`. Two Raspberry Pi `.raw` and two files named `.dng` are plain JPEGs and are opened correctly; they are not affected.

Evidence from the files (ExifTool tag names, `rawinfo --tree`):

| File | IFD0 | Declared picture | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| Phase One P65+ IIQ | 296x220, 8-bit RGB | 4490x3364 | Exif `PixelXDimension` / `PixelYDimension`, `PhaseOne:ImageWidth`; 11 MB of private data after IFD0's strip |
| Phase One IQ4 150MP IIQ | 640x480 | 14204x10652 | same |
| Canon EOS-1D `.TIF` | 288x192 | 2464x1648 | Exif dimensions |
| Kodak EOS DCS 3 `.TIF` | 160x128 | 1280x1024 (8-bit, in a `SubIFDs` child) | no Exif IFD |

## Expected

A file whose first image is just a reduced copy of a much larger picture is recognised as a raw LightCraft can't decode yet, imports as "preview only" with the reason, and shows what it has instead of looking like the photo.

## Not covered

Decoding IIQ (the codecs are private, no public specification). Hasselblad / Kodak DCR / Epson TIFF raws are separate.

I have a fix ready and will open a PR for it.

title: Raws we can't decode fail to import although they carry a JPEG preview (Canon CRW, Minolta MRW, Sigma X3F, Kodak KDC, Leaf MOS, Epson ERF)
author: radialmonster
body:
## What happens

`40` shows an undecodable raw as "preview only" when the container is recognised and a JPEG is found. These files import with an error instead, although each has a usable JPEG (raw.pixls.us CC0 archive, main `48cd9c5`; 42 files):

| Files | Error today | Preview that exists |
|---|---|---|
| Canon CRW (11 files with a CIFF header) | RawOther files are not supported yet | `JpgFromRaw` 640x480 to 3072x2048 |
| Minolta MRW (8) | same | `PreviewImage` 640x425 to 640x480 |
| Sigma X3F (14) | same | `JpgFromRaw` 2640x1760 to 6192x4128 |
| Kodak KDC (4: P880, P712, Z981, Z990) | required tag `ImageWidth` not found | JPEG at IFD0 tags 513 / 514, 3072x2304 to 4288x3216 |
| Leaf MOS (2) | compression method Unknown(99) | `Leaf:PreviewImage`, about 24 KB |
| Epson ERF (3) | OtherTiff files are not decoded yet, without an embedded preview | `Olympus:PreviewImage` 640x424 |

Causes found in the files:
- CRW, MRW and X3F are not recognised by `lightcraft_raw::probe`; the codec sniffer calls them `RawOther`.
- KDC IFD0 has no `ImageWidth` / `ImageLength` (the pictures are in private SubIFD tags), so the TIFF reader refuses the file.
- MOS uses compression 99, which is not a TIFF value.
- In MRW and ERF the stored preview's first byte is not `ff` (`00`, `02` or `ee` in the files) while the rest is a regular JPEG; for MOS and ERF no tag the parser follows points to it.
- A Canon PowerShot CRW stores its sensor mosaic as a one-component baseline JPEG, larger than the real preview.

Also, none of these extensions (`iiq`, `crw`, `mrw`, `x3f`, `kdc`, `mos`, `erf`) is in the import extension list, so a folder import skips them silently.

## Expected

The same as `40`: preview only, with the reason. A file with no JPEG at all keeps a clear error. (72 TIFF raws, mostly Hasselblad 3FR/FFF and Kodak DCR, carry only an uncompressed RGB reduced image and stay errors; Canon EOS R8 `6587` has only an HEVC thumbnail.)

title: Show a window before the GPU device is created, so a driver that blocks there doesn't leave a black "not responding" window
author: bflatastic
body:
Follow-up to #374. The desktop window's renderer (eframe/egui-wgpu) creates its GPU device before the first frame. When the driver blocks inside device creation, the window stays black and "not responding" with no explanation. #374 was such a case: NVIDIA's driver walked the whole system drive in `D3D12CreateDevice` when its shader cache was disabled.

Ideas:
- Show a minimal native or CPU-drawn window first ("Starting the GPU…"), with a timeout that explains what's happening and how to start with another backend or `LIGHTCRAFT_GPU_BACKEND`.
- Or create the window's device on a worker thread with a watchdog, and record a sentinel (like the compute device's `gpu-init.marker`), so the next launch can say "the GPU driver blocked during startup" and point to `docs/gpu-pipeline.md` → troubleshooting.

Constraints: no OS-level tricks that break the never-crash rules, and it has to work on Windows, macOS and Linux.

title: In-window menu bar: pointing at another title doesn't switch the open menu
author: radialmonster
body:
## Summary

On Windows and Linux (the in-window menu bar; macOS uses the native menu), with one top-level menu open (for example File), moving the pointer over another title (Edit, View, Photo, Window, Help) does nothing. In native menu bars the open menu closes at once and the one under the pointer opens. The user has to close the open menu and click the other title.

This is not a regression. Each title has been its own independent popup since the menu bar was added, so switching on hover never worked.

## Steps

1. Open LightCraft on Windows or Linux with the window wide enough that the titles show (not the single "Menu" button).
2. Click File. The File menu opens.
3. Move the pointer onto Edit.

Expected: File closes and Edit opens, and so on along the bar while a menu stays open.
Actual: File stays open; Edit does nothing until clicked.

## Cause

egui's `Popup::menu` toggles on click of its own button. `MenuBar` doesn't switch top-level menus on hover either (its `bar` flag only decides submenu versus button), so nothing in egui does it for us. The narrow-window "Menu" button already switches between its submenus on hover.

## Proposed fix

`show_in_window` draws all titles first, then their popups. One small function (`switch_open_title`) uses egui's public popup API to open the hovered title's popup while another title's menu is open (egui keeps one popup open at a time), requests a repaint for the switch, and still toggles a title by click. Hovering with no menu open does nothing. Keyboard (Escape), click outside, submenus and their placement (#189), the 24 px title gap (#28, #49) and the widget registry are unchanged.

I have a fix ready and will open a PR for it.

title: Feature request: write develop/crop settings back to XMP sidecars (crs: namespace)
author: jefflaplante
body:
### The problem
LightCraft reads `crs:` XMP sidecars on import and render (docs/xmp-interop.md), but never writes them. Develop settings — exposure, crop geometry, and the rest of the mapped set — live only in LightCraft's catalog database. That makes the XMP bridge one-way: settings flow *into* LightCraft from external tools (Lightroom, Capture One, or AI culling pipelines), but nothing flows back out.

### Why it matters
We run an automated pipeline that relies on this asymmetry every day:

- Our culling tool (`cull`) writes per-frame develop decisions as `crs:` sidecars — exposure suggestion, crop geometry, rating, keywords.
- `lightcraft-cli run` applies them on import, develops, and exports client JPEGs. This works today and works well.
- But any manual adjustment made in LightCraft's GUI after that point is stranded. The settings exist only in the catalog; there's no way to get them back to the file system where our pipeline (or Lightroom, or C1) can see them.

A photographer who hand-tunes a keep in LightCraft should be able to hand that edit back to the rest of the world. Right now the door only opens inward.

### Proposal
When a develop setting or crop geometry changes in the GUI (or via MCP), offer to write the current state to a sidecar in the `crs:` namespace — mirroring the read-mapping documented in `docs/xmp-interop.md`:

- `crs:Exposure2012` ↔ light.exposure
- `crs:CropLeft/Top/Right/Bottom` ↔ crop.geometry (normalized, **oriented/display frame** — see note)
- `crs:Rating`, `crs:Keywords` (dc:subject) as already supported on read

Conventions that would make interop robust, based on our empirical testing:

1. **Oriented frame for crops.** We verified (correlation-tested against rendered output) that LightCraft reads `crs:Crop*` as normalized coordinates in the oriented/display frame — same convention as Lightroom. Writing back in the same frame keeps the loop closed and the convention consistent.
2. **Ownership marker.** A `x:xmptk="lightcraft"` attr…

title: M6: align masking components and interactions with Camera Raw
author: Hanmo123
body:
LightCraft's masking panel and mask components should match Camera Raw's visual structure and interaction logic consistently. The current controls and on-canvas gestures have accumulated differences, so individual fixes should be guided by one coherent behaviour specification.

### Scope

- Observe Camera Raw's masking panel, mask/component hierarchy, selected/hover states, component naming, controls and menus; document the expected behaviour for the native LightCraft UI.
- Align mask/component creation, selection, renaming, duplication, deletion, visibility, inversion, and Add/Subtract/Intersect operations.
- Align on-canvas interactions for supported mask types, especially linear and radial gradients: body/pin dragging, resize/rotation handles, feather controls and modifier keys.
- Make panel selection, canvas selection, focus, shortcuts, and Undo/Redo behave consistently across components.
- Match layout, spacing and visual feedback using LightCraft's own assets and permitted fonts. Reference observation remains clean-room; no Adobe assets are to be copied or published.

### Acceptance criteria

- A documented comparison identifies supported Camera Raw behaviours and any intentional or unsupported differences.
- The masking panel and supported component interactions follow that specification consistently.
- Pointer/keyboard regressions cover selection, gestures and one-step undo/redo; LightCraft screenshots are checked visually.
- Camera Raw parity is not claimed for unsupported mask types or AI capabilities.

Related: #253 and PR #449 (radial-body dragging). The radial fix is a small independent improvement, not completion of this broader task.

Claimed by @Hanmo123 for future work. Tracking only for now: implementation has not started and should wait for a separate go-ahead.

title: Pentax *ist DS/DL, K100D, K100D Super, K110D and Samsung GX-1L PEFs open as preview-only: the raw strip is plain packed 12-bit under a PackBits tag
author: radialmonster
body:
**TL;DR:** Six older 6 MP Pentax-family bodies write their raw strip with TIFF compression 32773 (PackBits), but the strip holds plain 12-bit samples packed two per three bytes; the byte count says so exactly. LightCraft reads the tag, finds no PackBits support in the PEF reader, and shows only the embedded JPEG with a "preview-only" label. The samples can be read directly, and the six files then decode as raws with the right colours and the camera JPEG's framing.

## Problem

In the raw.pixls.us CC0 archive, six PEF files import as preview-only with "PEF compression 32773" (the Samsung GX-1L with "Srw files are not decoded yet"):

| File | Body | Size | Strip bytes | Width x height x 1.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1083 | Pentax \*ist DL | 3040 x 2024 | 9229440 | 9229440 |
| 1309 | Pentax K110D | 3040 x 2024 | 9229440 | 9229440 |
| 2262 | Pentax K100D | 3040 x 2024 | 9229440 | 9229440 |
| 4392 | Pentax \*ist DS | 3040 x 2024 | 9229440 | 9229440 |
| 5804 | Pentax K100D Super | 3040 x 2024 | 9229440 | 9229440 |
| 8115 | Samsung GX-1L | 3040 x 2024 | 9229440 | 9229440 |

All six have one strip, photometric 32803 (CFA), 12 bits per sample, one sample per pixel. The strip length is exactly the size of the samples packed at 12 bits; a PackBits stream of image data this noisy would not come out the same length. The \*ist D from the same family is tagged uncompressed (compression 1, 16-bit words) and already decodes.

The GX-1L is Samsung-branded (`Make` "SAMSUNG TECHWIN"), so it is also routed to the Samsung reader, which cannot decode anything. Its maker note is a Pentax one (it starts with the `AOC` signature), as in the other five.

## Cause

`vendor/pef.rs` accepts compression 1 (uncompressed) and 65535 (Pentax's own Huffman coding) and refuses everything else. The tag value 32773 is the PackBits value in TIFF 6.0, but these files do not hold a PackBits stream.

## Proposed fix

In the PEF reader, accept compression 32773 only when every strip holds exactly the bytes th…

title: Sony A7 (ILCE-7) ARWs render posterized with a cold colour cast at default settings
author: jordanneenan
body:
## Summary

Raw files from the original **Sony A7 (ILCE-7)** render in LightCraft with heavy **posterization** (smooth gradients break up into flat, blotchy patches, especially in out-of-focus backgrounds and shadows) and a **cold, desaturated colour cast** — even with all develop settings at their defaults. The same files decode cleanly with LibRaw (`dcraw_emu -w`), and ARWs from an A7 III (ILCE-7M3) and A7S III (ILCE-7SM3) look fine in LightCraft, so this seems specific to the ILCE-7.

## Environment

- LightCraft **0.4.0** (official release tarball), Linux (Arch-based, kernel 7.2)
- Reproduces in the app and headless: `lightcraft-cli render _DSC3805.ARW -o out.jpg --size 1600`

## Example file

- Camera: Sony ILCE-7 (firmware v3.20), 2018
- ISO 1250, 1/400 s, f/4, 69 mm
- Sensor 6048 × 4024 (image 6024 × 4024), RGGB, ~24.9 MB (Sony compressed ARW)
- Camera WB multipliers (LibRaw): 2232 / 1024 / 1664 / 1024

The XMP sidecar LightCraft wrote for the photo contains only default settings (no crop, no curve, exposure 0, profile `lc.color`, WB `asShot`), so this is the default raw rendering, not an edit.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Import an ILCE-7 ARW (lossy compressed, which is the camera's default).
2. Open it in Develop with no adjustments, or run `lightcraft-cli render` on it.

**Expected:** a smooth image with natural colour, like LibRaw's output or the camera's embedded JPEG preview.
**Actual:** strong banding and posterization in smooth tonal areas, plus a bluish, washed-out cast across the whole image.

## Notes

- I can see this on all ~670 ILCE-7 files I've checked (2016–2020). None of my ~6,200 ILCE-7M3 / ILCE-7SM3 files show it.
- The posterization looks like a decode problem rather than a colour-matrix one. Something like the Sony tone curve or bit depth not being applied correctly for this older body's compressed ARW would fit. The colour cast may be related to #156 (NEX-5, also an older Sony body).

title: Pentax PEFs: red and blue are exchanged on 25 files from 15 bodies (K10D, K-3, K-70, K-1, K-3 Mark III, 645Z, *ist D, ...)
author: radialmonster
body:
**TL;DR:** The PEF reader assumes every Huffman-compressed Pentax file has a BGGR sensor layout, but the K10D/K200D/K2000 and every body from the K-3 on (K-70, KP, K-S1/S2, K-1, K-3 Mark III, 645Z, KF) are RGGB. On those files red and blue photosites are exchanged before demosaicing; the file's own Exif `CFAPattern` already says which layout it is, and it is right for all 33 colour files I could measure.

## What happens

`crates/raw/src/vendor/pef.rs` uses `Cfa::bayer_static("BGGR")` from the array origin for compression 65535 (and for compression 1). That is right for the K-7 / K-5 generation and the 645D, wrong for the rest. Where the engine can fit a starting look to the file's own camera JPEG, the fitted matrix hides most of it (hue-dependent colour and the red/blue interpolation stay off); where the fit is rejected the swap is plain: a K-3 Mark III sample of a Rubik's cube renders with an orange cast and the red faces blue, and its garden sample has a lime-green sky.

![before (main), after the fix, camera JPEG](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dfcaaca4-7281-4600-85e2-c24fc571fd46)

## Measurements

33 colour PEFs and 36 Pentax/Ricoh DNGs with a clear alignment, from the public raw.pixls.us set (CC0). For each file the four phase planes of the decoded mosaic were fitted against the embedded camera JPEG (log R/G and log B/G block chroma correlation, summed, range -2..2) for all four possible layouts. The DNGs, which state their CFAPattern, all agree with the method.

| Exif CFAPattern | Bodies (compression 65535 unless noted) | Main today | Measured at the array origin |
|---|---|---|---|
| BGGR | K-7, K-x, K-r, K-5, K-5 II, K-5 II s, K20D, 645D | BGGR | BGGR (correct) |
| RGGB | K10D, K200D, K2000, K-3, K-3 II, K-70, KP, KF, K-S1, K-S2, K-1, K-1 Mark II, K-3 Mark III, 645Z; \*ist D (compression 1) | BGGR | RGGB (red and blue exchanged) |

Examples (main's BGGR score / best score): K10D 0.66 / 1.91, K200D -0.28 / 1.86, K-3 Mark III -0.65 / 1.83, K-1 M…

title: lightcraft.exe aborts at startup with exit code 1 on Windows 11
author: fireapache
body:
# `lightcraft.exe` exits immediately with code 1 — `dxil.dll` missing from the MSI payload

**Version:** 0.4.0 (`lightcraft-0.4.0-windows-x64.msi`)
**Status:** confirmed root cause, workaround verified

## Summary

After installing 0.4.0 from the MSI, `lightcraft.exe` refuses to start. It exits with code 1
within a second and never opens a window. The MSI payload contains only `lightcraft.exe` and
`lightcraft-cli.exe` — no `dxil.dll`. The GUI's wgpu DX12 backend needs the DXIL signing library
at runtime; without it the shader compilation fails validation, the D3D12 device is lost, and
`eframe` aborts.

Nothing is wrong with the GPU, the driver, or the app logic. `lightcraft-cli` works fully.

## Error output

`lightcraft.exe` prints the following on stderr before exiting:

```
lightcraft: ERROR wgpu_core::indirect_validation: indirect-validation error:
  ComputePipeline(Internal("DXC compile error: warning: DXIL signing library (dxil.dll,libdxil.so)
  not found.  Resulting DXIL will not be signed for use in release environments.\r\n\n"))

lightcraft: WARN  gpu_allocator::allocator::free_list_allocator: leak detected: { ... }

lightcraft: ERROR eframe::native::run: Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Parent device is lost
Error: Wgpu(RequestDeviceError(RequestDeviceError { inner: Core(Device(Lost)) }))
```

Exit code: `1`

## Root cause

1. The MSI installs only the two executables. `dxil.dll` is not shipped.
2. On startup the GUI creates a wgpu device on the **DX12** backend.
3. `wgpu-hal` 30.0.1 compiles compute pipelines through the DXC shader compiler, which requires
   the **DXIL signing library** (`dxil.dll`) to produce signed DXIL.
4. `dxil.dll` is absent, so pipeline creation fails wgpu's indirect validation.
5. The D3D12 device is lost; `request_device` returns `Core(Device(Lost))`.
6. `eframe::native::run` treats this as fatal and exits 1 — silently, with no dialog.

The error surface is poor: the app exits 1 with no UI and no message. Only the GPU block …

title: Nikon Z 6_2 NEF (14-bit lossless): default render turns fine texture into flat, hard-edged "painted" patches at 100% (camera JPEG stays smooth)
author: toply79
body:
## Summary

A full-size render of a Nikon Z 6II (`NIKON Z 6_2`, 14-bit lossless-compressed NEF, 6064×4040) comes out with flattened, posterised areas in textured regions (fabric, stucco, foliage) when viewed at 100%. The same frame's embedded camera JPEG shows smooth, continuous tones. The overall colour of neutral areas is close to the camera JPEG, so this is a separate symptom from the muted-colour reports in #211 and #299 (it looks like what #211 calls "broad, flat patches"). I have not isolated the cause.

## Environment

- LightCraft **0.4.0** (macOS universal `.dmg` and `lightcraft-cli` 0.4.0 from the GitHub release), Apple M1 Max, Metal
- Camera: Nikon Z 6_2, lens 24-70mm f/2.8G, 70 mm, f/2.8, 1/2000 s, ISO 100
- File: `TON_5516.NEF`, 28 MB, 6064×4040, `NEFCompression: Lossless`, 14-bit
- Reference: the full-size JPEG embedded in the NEF (`exiftool -b -JpgFromRaw`, 6048×4024)

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
lightcraft-cli render TON_5516.NEF -o lc_default_full.jpg --size 6064
exiftool -b -JpgFromRaw TON_5516.NEF > camera_embedded.jpg
```

Open both at 100% and compare, for example, the fabric of a light blouse or a stucco wall with a window. No edits, no library, no masks, CLI defaults only.

## Actual behaviour

- Soft gradients are replaced by flat patches with hard boundaries. Shadows in fabric become separate "islands" with crisp edges, and stucco relief turns into cartoon-like shapes (see `crop_2` and `crop_3`).
- On the painted fence (`crop_4`) the render instead shows mottled bright specks and halos along edges, and the dark detail between the slats is lost; the camera JPEG is smooth there.
- Edge energy (std of a 3×3 edge filter on the region) is higher than the camera JPEG in all four regions I measured (10.5 → 11.3 and 12.1, 13.1 → 14.7, 9.9 → 11.6), consistent with hard edges and specks appearing where the camera has smooth transitions. title: Lightroom catalog import drops every crop (`HasCrop` missing), and rotated or straightened crops land in the wrong frame
author: rock-meister
body:
## Summary

`library.importLightroom` ignores the crops in a Lightroom Classic catalog. On a real 1918-photo catalog,
**all 987 cropped or straightened photos were imported uncropped**: the import report lists `CropLeft`,
`CropRight`, `CropTop`, `CropBottom` and `CropAngle` as unmapped.

With the one-line fix below, plain crops import correctly, but crops on rotated (portrait) photos and crops
with a straighten angle still come out the wrong shape. Those look like two separate coordinate-frame issues (details below).

Related: #197 (catalog import feature request). Not the same as #205 (Upright from XMP).

## Environment

- LightCraft `main` at c435d14 (catalog import is not in the v0.4.0 release), Linux x86_64, built from source
- Catalog: Lightroom Classic 11.x–15.x on Windows, ~1900 Sony ARWs, process versions 11.0 and 15.4

## Cause 1: the catalog has no `HasCrop`

Catalog develop settings (`Adobe_imageDevelopSettings.text`, Lua) store the crop like this:

```lua
CropAngle = 2.39897,
CropConstrainAspectRatio = true,
CropLeft = 0.042702,
CropRight = 0.957298,
```

There is no `HasCrop` key; XMP has `crs:HasCrop`, the catalog doesn't. In this catalog,
`select count(*) from Adobe_imageDevelopSettings where text like '%HasCrop%'` returns **0**, while 848 rows
have `CropLeft`. `crs.rs` only maps a crop when `crs:HasCrop` is `True`:

```rust
// crates/engine/src/crs.rs
match boolean(props, "crs:HasCrop") {
    Some(true) => { /* map Crop* to crop.geometry */ }
    Some(false) => { /* reset crop */ }
    None => {}   // ← every catalog photo ends up here
}
```

Also, edges at their default value are left out (e.g. no `CropTop` when it is 0), so the
default fallbacks in that block matter.

### Fix (tested)

Infer `HasCrop` in the catalog path only. The shared XMP mapper stays as it is, because in XMP
`HasCrop="False"` together with crop fields means the crop is switched off.

```diff
--- a/crates/engine/src/lightroom_catalog.rs
+++ b/crates/engine/src/lightroom_catalog.…

title: Allow Blacks/Whites adjustments beyond ±100 and clarify the scale for TIFF scans
author: JohannesMaierhofer
body:
## Use case

I use the latest available LightCraft release to edit scans stored as `.tiff` files. In the **Light** panel, the available **Blacks** and **Whites** adjustment range is not sufficient for my workflow: I would like to push these adjustments further than the current magnitude of 100 to make better use of the tonal information present in the dark and bright areas of the scans.

The displayed values also have no clear unit or explanation of their scale. It is unclear what an adjustment of 100 represents and why it is the limit.

## Requested improvement

- Allow **Blacks** and **Whites** adjustments beyond **-100 / +100**, for example through an optional extended slider range or direct numeric entry beyond the normal slider endpoints.
- Ensure that extended values produce a stronger adjustment, rather than merely displaying a larger number while internally clamping the effect to the existing limits.
- Explain the scale in a tooltip or documentation: are these dimensionless relative adjustment values, percentages, exposure-related units, or something else? Describe what the endpoints mean.
- Keep fine control around neutral and within the existing range, and preserve existing edits and presets when introducing the extended range.

The aim is to bring out tonal detail already present in the TIFF data. I am not asking to reconstruct information that was clipped during scanning. If extending these particular controls is unsuitable for the tone-mapping algorithm, an explicit black-point/white-point or levels control for scanned TIFFs would be a useful alternative.

## Expected result

When a TIFF scan needs more adjustment after Blacks or Whites reaches an endpoint, I can continue in the same direction and see an additional effect. The UI makes the meaning of the numeric scale clear, and extended settings remain intact when the edit is saved and reopened.

title: Local folder import header overlaps breadcrumbs and controls in narrow panes
author: QuirkyTurtle94
body: ### What happens In the Local folder view used before adding photos to the library, long folder breadcrumbs overlap **Include subfolders**, the **Add … to My Photos** button and the photo count. The text becomes jumbled when the centre pane is narrowed by the sidebars. Observed on macOS in LightCraft 0.4.0. The supplied screenshot shows 2,408 selected photos, a long path on an external volume and the Presets/right sidebar open. The affected code is also present on main at c435d143. ### Reproduce 1. Browse a Local folder with a long name/path (for example `/Volumes/Photography archive/Trips and holidays/A very long folder name with many photographs to import`). 2. Leave both sidebars open, or narrow the window so the grid centre pane is approximately 590 logical pixels wide. 3. Select multiple photos and inspect the header above the grid. **Actual:** breadcrumb text and import controls paint over each other. **Expected:** folder navigation, selection/photo count and import controls stay readable, have separate hit targets and remain within the centre pane. A long path should shorten visually with its full value available on hover; controls should wrap if necessary. ### Diagnosis and proposed fix `folder_header` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/grid.rs` adds unbounded breadcrumb labels in a left-to-right layout, then adds the controls in a right-to-left layout in the remaining space, all inside a fixed 44-point header. Neither the breadcrumb nor the controls have a guaranteed independent region. Give the path/count their own bounded row and the import controls a wrapping row whose height participates in grid layout. Retain clickable ancestor breadcrumbs, Include subfolders and Add to My Photos behaviour. Add headless regression coverage for painted-text bounds and overlap at narrow/wide widths, multiple locales and display scales. The original screenshot includes personal directory names, so the reproduction above uses synthetic names.

title: GoPro GPR files import but can't be opened, with only 'TIFF compression 9' as the reason
author: radialmonster
body:
**TL;DR:** GoPro `.GPR` raw files import, but then cannot be shown or exported, and the only message is "unsupported raw (TIFF compression 9) without an embedded preview", which does not say what the file is. The files carry no preview image, so there is nothing to fall back to.

## What happens today

I tried all 17 CC0 GoPro `.GPR` files on raw.pixls.us (HERO5 to HERO11 Black and FUSION; ids 936, 1634, 2556, 2557, 2558, 2786, 2846, 2908, 5766, 3949, 5767, 4483, 4883, 4894, 7319, 7370, 7371) on current `main` (c435d14).

- Importing works: the photo is added to the library with the right size.
- Rendering or exporting fails for every file with `unsupported raw (TIFF compression 9) without an embedded preview` (`lightcraft-cli render FILE -o out.jpg` exits with status 1).

## What is in the files

Measured from the TIFF structure of all 17 files, they are identical in layout:

- one image directory only (IFD0), no SubIFDs, no thumbnail strip, no `JPEGInterchangeFormat` pointer, so there is no embedded preview of any size;
- `NewSubfileType` 0, `PhotometricInterpretation` 32803 (CFA), 16 bits per sample, one sample per pixel, one tile holding the whole image;
- `Compression` 9, the value GoPro uses for the VC-5 (SMPTE ST 2073) coded raw data of its GPR format. The files also have `DNGVersion`, colour matrices and the other usual DNG tags.

## Expected

Decoding VC-5 is a separate piece of work. Until then the file should fail with a message that says what is wrong, for example `DNG compression 9 (GoPro VC-5) is not decoded yet`, rather than a bare TIFF compression number.

title: Lightroom Custom white balance imports as a large blue shift on relative-WB raws (absolute Kelvin read on the relative scale)
author: rock-meister
body:
## Summary

A Lightroom **Custom** white balance on a raw imports as an absolute Kelvin value, but for cameras LightCraft renders with **relative** white balance (no measured illuminant, e.g. Sony ARW without a calibration) `wb.temp` is read on the relative scale, where 6500 / 0 means *as shot*. A small custom tweak therefore turns into a very large shift. In a real catalog, all 3 photos with `WhiteBalance = "Custom"` came out strongly blue.

Found while testing `library.importLightroom` (#197, #483). It affects XMP sidecars too, since they go through the same `crs` mapper.

## Example

Sony ILCE-7RM4 ARW, indoor tungsten light, camera WB Auto. Lightroom Classic catalog develop settings:

```lua
WhiteBalance = "Custom",
Temperature = 3578,
Tint = -5,
CustomTemperature = 3578.95,
CustomTint = -5,
```

Neighbouring photos from the same session, left at "As Shot", have `Temperature` 3550–3650, so this custom value is a small adjustment in Lightroom.

`crs.rs` maps it for raws as `wb.mode = "custom"`, `wb.temp = 3578`, `wb.tint = -5`. `pipeline::local::effective_wb` then uses `(s.wb.temp, s.wb.tint)` directly when `info.relative_wb`, so 3578 is read as far cooler than as-shot.

Compared with Lightroom's own export of the same photo (CIE76 ΔE on 24 px downscales, mean b*):

| LightCraft white balance | ΔE vs Lightroom export | Δb* |
|---|---|---|
| Imported (`wb.temp` 3578, relative) | 22.2 | −21.0 (very blue) |
| As shot (6500 / 0) | 11.9 | +10.6 |
| Relative 5000 (best of a sweep) | **4.9** | −1.9 |

The other two custom-WB photos behave the same way: ΔE 15.6 and 22.0 as imported.

## Why it isn't a one-liner

Converting Lightroom's absolute value to LightCraft's relative scale needs Lightroom's *as-shot* Kelvin for that photo. For an As Shot photo Lightroom writes it into `Temperature`. For a Custom photo the catalog doesn't keep it: there's no `AsShotTemperature`, the history only has the import step, and `Adobe_imageDevelopBeforeSettings` is empty. The camera record…

title: [BUG] Brush mask feathering hardens with stationary hold duration instead of brush passes
author: Hanmo123
body:
### Problem
With brush size, feather and flow unchanged, holding the mouse button down while leaving the brush stationary changes the result according to how long it stays there. A short hold produces a normally feathered spot; a longer hold produces a much harder edge.

The attached screenshots were captured by the reporter in LightCraft's native development build on macOS. The Camera Raw comparison below is the reporter's observation.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Open a photo in Develop and create a brush mask with visible feathering.
2. Enable the mask overlay. Keep size, feather and flow unchanged throughout the comparison.
3. Press and hold briefly at one location without moving the pointer, then release.
4. At an unpainted location, press and hold longer without moving the pointer, then release.
5. Compare the edges of the two painted spots.

### Actual behavior
A brief hold gives a soft feathered edge. A longer stationary hold builds up coverage until the edge becomes hard, despite unchanged brush settings and no additional brush passes.

### Expected behavior / Camera Raw comparison
The reporter observes that Adobe Camera Raw accumulates coverage according to how many times the brush passes over an area, rather than how long it is held stationary there. LightCraft should preserve normal repeated-pass accumulation and flow behavior, but merely waiting at the same point with the mouse button held down should not add extra passes or progressively harden the feathered edge.

title: [BUG] Mask overlay obscures local adjustments instead of hiding when sliders change
author: QuirkyTurtle94
body:
### What happens

After adding a mask (for example a Linear Gradient), moving a local adjustment such as Exposure leaves the red mask overlay covering the photo. This makes it difficult to judge the adjustment without manually hiding the overlay first.

### Reproduce

1. Open a photo in Detail and open Masking.
2. Add a Linear Gradient with the overlay visible.
3. Move the mask's Exposure slider.
4. The red overlay remains visible during the adjustment and after release.

### Expected

Hide the overlay when a local adjustment is applied, so the effect is immediately visible. Keep the mask itself enabled and retain its adjustments. The existing O shortcut or overlay eye should allow showing the overlay again.

Handle successful `mask.adjust` commands at the shared frontend command entry point. Turn off the preview overlay for local adjustments (including Amount, numeric edits and resets), while retaining the overlay when refining the mask's shape/edges. This also gives the control channel the same behavior as the UI. Failed adjustment commands and global Develop adjustments should not change overlay visibility.

Add headless coverage for the actual Exposure slider, rendered overlay selection, manual restoration, failed commands and other local adjustments. This is separate from the brush stroke coverage/feathering reports #517 and #518.

Source inspected at `65ad290e8968cb589a13b859457e922fce2ec118`: local sliders dispatch `mask.adjust`, but only explicit overlay controls currently change `ui.mask_overlay`. No overlapping issue or open PR found in the masking/overlay searches.

title: browse_a_local_folder test fails on Windows (path separator in assertion)
author: HarrisXiu
body:
`headless::tests::browse_a_local_folder` fails on Windows, including on an untouched `main` (65ad290):

```
thread 'headless::tests::browse_a_local_folder' panicked at crates\ui-egui\src\headless.rs:1673:9:
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: "C:\Users\…\AppData\Local\Temp\lc-ui-browse-43756"
 right: "C:/Users/…/AppData/Local/Temp/lc-ui-browse-43756"
```

```
cargo test -p lightcraft-ui-egui --lib -- browse_a_local_folder
```

## Cause
The assertion came in with b9f9519 (#491, merged in #512):

```rust
assert_eq!(h.app.session.browse.as_ref().unwrap().path, dir.to_string_lossy().replace('\', "/"));
```

Clicking a breadcrumb builds a `/`-joined path (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/grid.rs`, `folder_breadcrumbs`) and passes it to `library.browse`, which opens the right folder but stores the path with Windows separators. The app behaves correctly; the test compares two spellings of the same path as strings. On macOS and Linux both sides use `/`, so the test passes there.

## Suggested fix
Compare paths, not strings. For example, compare `Path::new(&browse.path)` with `dir`, or canonicalize both sides. Alternatively, `library.browse` could normalize the paths it stores, and the test would then compare against that normal form.

## Possibly related (not verified)
While reading `folder_breadcrumbs`, I noticed the prefix it rebuilds keeps a leading `/` but not a leading `\`. So on Windows, clicking a breadcrumb under a UNC path (`\server\share\photos\…`) may open `server/share/…`. It may be worth checking while fixing the test.

title: Highlight recovery produces pink/magenta highlights in iPhone 15 Pro Max RAW photos
author: codic12
body:
## Description

When editing photos taken on an iPhone 15 Pro Max, reducing overexposed highlights causes the affected areas to turn pink/magenta instead of recovering to a neutral white or their original color.

This is particularly noticeable in bright, nearly clipped areas of an image. Other RAW processors, including Lightroom, handle the same photos without introducing this strong pink tint.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a RAW photo taken on an iPhone 15 Pro Max that contains overexposed highlights.
2. Reduce the **Highlights** slider to recover detail in bright areas.
3. Observe the color of the recovered highlights.

## Expected Behavior

Recovered highlights should retain natural colors or appear neutral white when detail cannot be recovered, as they do in Lightroom and other RAW processors.

## Actual Behavior

The recovered highlights become noticeably pink/magenta, making highlight recovery largely unusable for affected photos.

## Additional Information

- **Device:** iPhone 15 Pro Max
- **Comparison:** Lightroom and other RAW processors
- **Possible cause:** An issue with highlight reconstruction, white balance, or handling clipped color channels in the RAW processing pipeline.

This appears to be a color reconstruction issue rather than simply an overly aggressive highlight adjustment.

title: lightcraft-cli and the headless MCP server record every import and edit as `2026-09-30T12:00:00` (hard-coded test clock)
author: wzsxb233
body:
**Summary**

`Session::new()` has a fixed clock as its default: `clock: Box::new(|| "2026-09-30T12:00:00".to_string())` in `crates/engine/src/lib.rs`. The desktop app replaces it with `.with_system_clock()` (`apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs:519-527`). The headless paths do not. `Headless::default()` and the demo constructor in `crates/mcp/src/headless.rs` (lines 34 and 45) are built without it, and `lightcraft-cli` uses them for `run` and `mcp`. The sessions created directly in `apps/lightcraft-cli/src/main.rs` (lines 394, 655, 735-740) are also built without it. As a result, photos imported or edited via `lightcraft-cli run --library …` or `lightcraft-cli mcp` get a fake `imported`/`edited` time, and that time is saved in the real library. Sorting by import or edit date, "Previous Import"-style views and anything date-based is then wrong once the user opens the library in the app. Agents driving LightCraft over MCP are the main audience for this path.

**Environment**
- LightCraft `main` @ da6cbcf (v0.4.0), `lightcraft-cli` release build
- Linux x86_64 (Debian 13), Rust 1.99; run on 2026-10-09

**Steps to reproduce**
```sh
mkdir -p imgs && cp any.jpg any.tif imgs/
lightcraft-cli run --library lib library.import 'paths=["'$PWD'/imgs"]'
lightcraft-cli run --library lib library.select 'ids=[1]' develop.set control=light.exposure value=0.5
lightcraft-cli run --library lib photo.inspect id=1
```

**Expected**
`imported` and `edited` are the current local time, as when the same steps are done in the desktop app.

**Actual**
```
'imported': '2026-09-30T12:00:00', 'edited': '2026-09-30T12:00:00'
```
This is the same for every import and edit, whatever the real date. The values are written to the library catalog.

**Suggested fix**
Call `.with_system_clock()` in `Headless::default()`/the demo constructor and on the sessions created in `lightcraft-cli`, or make the system clock the default in `Session::new()` and let tests opt into the fixed clock.

title: Improve Precision and Visual Feedback in Color Grading Wheels
author: radialmonster
body:
Problem

The current color grading wheels make it difficult to determine the exact position and magnitude of a color adjustment. While dragging the control point allows users to adjust color balance, there is limited visual or numerical feedback to indicate how far the adjustment has moved from the neutral center or what values are currently being applied.

This makes precise adjustments difficult, particularly when making subtle corrections or attempting to reproduce a previous setting.

Proposed Enhancement

Improve the color grading wheels by providing clearer visual feedback and numerical information about the current adjustment.

Possible improvements include:

Center reference: Make the neutral center of each wheel clearly identifiable.

Position indicator: Provide a visual indication of the adjustment's direction and distance from the center.

Numerical readout: Display the current adjustment values, updating in real time as the control point moves.

Precise input: Optionally allow users to enter numerical values directly for fine adjustments.

Expected Behavior

Users should be able to determine both the direction and strength of a color adjustment without relying solely on visual estimation.

The numerical values should correspond to the underlying color grading parameters, allowing users to make precise, repeatable adjustments.

Benefits

Greater precision when making subtle color corrections.

Easier identification of neutral and adjusted positions.

More consistent and reproducible color grading.

Reduced reliance on trial and error.

Improved usability for both beginners and experienced users.




(Note, this was issue was requested by a user who emailed me)

When I import photos into Lightcraft, the folder they came from does not appear under the Local section. This makes it harder to track where images originated, especially when working across multiple shoots or directories.

Expected Behavior (Lightroom)
In Lightroom Classic, the original folder structure is visible in the Library module under “Folders” after import. This allows users to navigate their actual disk folders directly inside the app. It would be helpful if Lightcraft displayed the source folder under Local in a similar way.

title: Ctrl+= / Ctrl+- scale the whole UI instead of zooming the photo (Windows); Ctrl+wheel doesn't zoom in Edit view (v0.4.0)
author: bitshiftza
body:
**Environment:** Windows 10 Pro 22H2, LightCraft v0.4.0 (x64 .msi), downloaded Oct 9, 2026.

**Problem:** View ▸ Zoom In / Zoom Out zoom the photo correctly, but their listed shortcuts (Ctrl+= / Ctrl+-) scale the entire interface instead. Ctrl+0 (Zoom to Fit) also resets the interface scale.

**Cause:** egui's `Options::zoom_with_keyboard` is left at its default (`true`). At the end of every frame egui consumes Cmd/Ctrl+Plus, Cmd/Ctrl+Equals, Cmd/Ctrl+Minus and Cmd/Ctrl+0 and applies its browser-style interface zoom. The app's `view.zoomIn` / `view.zoomOut` / `view.zoomFit` bindings fire too, but the interface scaling is what the user sees. macOS is unaffected only because the native menu bar takes those keys before egui does; Windows and Linux use the in-window menus.

**Separately:** Ctrl+wheel over the photo in the Edit view doesn't zoom in v0.4.0. This landed on main after the tag (912f56c, LR-VIEW-ZOOM trackpad zoom and pan), so it is fixed in the next release.

**Fix:** disable `zoom_with_keyboard` when the app configures its egui context, with headless regression tests for both the shortcuts (photo zoom changes, `zoom_factor` stays) and Ctrl+wheel in the Edit view.

title: Option to start raws from a neutral look instead of the fitted camera look
author: radialmonster
body:
**TL;DR:** for raws without a measured colour matrix (most ARW, NEF, RW2, RAF, CR2, CR3 and PEF files), LightCraft fits each photo's starting look to the camera's embedded JPEG. Two users have asked for a way to opt out and start from a neutral, scene-referred rendering instead. This issue collects feedback on whether, and how, to offer that.

## Requests so far

- #244 (@bwees): wants raws to start like a typical raw developer does, not "looking like the JPEG". Part of the brightness difference is Sony's DRO, which #568 addresses, but the request is about the approach itself.
- #314 (@tjbbjt): "will there be any way to remove camera JPEG fits if I want to manually reject a fit and instead start with a neutral look?"

## How it works today

- The fit (matrix, optional hue/saturation table, tone curve, chroma curve) is accepted only when it passes held-out error checks (`docs/camera-preview-colour.md`). Otherwise the photo uses a generic neutral rendering.
- There is no user setting for this. Users can't skip the fit, and they can't keep the camera JPEG's look for a photo whose fit was rejected.
- The neutral fallback itself is currently dark, flat and often tinted. Public samples show this (#535, #515), and work on a better fallback is in progress. So today "neutral" isn't yet a good place to start from.

## Possible shapes (for discussion)

1. **A per-photo or per-camera choice of starting look:** "Camera look" (today's default) or "Neutral". It could be set on import and in the Profile panel, and be part of the develop settings, so it syncs and copies like any other.
2. **A preference** for the default on new imports, with the per-photo switch from option 1.
3. **Leave it as is.** Improve the fallback so rejected fits look reasonable, and let users who want a neutral start build a preset.

Questions for the maintainers and users:
- Should "Neutral" mean today's generic fallback, or a dedicated neutral rendering (for example, the per-photo tone curve without the ca…

1. **Lights Dim** — everything except the photo (panels, toolbar, filmstrip, menu area) is dimmed with a semi-transparent dark overlay; the photo stays at full brightness.
2. **Lights Out** — everything except the photo goes fully black.
3. **Lights On** — back to normal.

**Why**
It's a quick way to judge a photo without the interface distracting you, while staying in the current view. It's different from Full Screen Preview (F): the panels stay where they are, so you can tap L, look, and tap L again to carry on editing — nothing re-lays out. Lightroom users press L out of habit, and right now it selects the Linear Gradient tool instead.

**Nice to have (Lightroom has these too)**
- Settings for the dim level (Lightroom defaults to 80%) and the screen colour (black by default).
- Works in both Grid and Detail views.

**Shortcut**
Lightroom uses L, which LightCraft currently uses for Linear Gradient. Lightroom's own gradient key is M, so L could move to Lights Out — your call.

Environment: LightCraft 0.4.0, macOS.

title: [Feature Request] Hold Shift while dragging a crop handle to keep proportions (like Lightroom)

body:
**What**
Holding **Shift** while dragging a crop handle should temporarily keep the crop's current proportions, as it does in Lightroom Classic and Photoshop. Releasing Shift goes back to free cropping. It shouldn't change the Lock toggle.

Lightroom and Photoshop users reach for Shift out of habit to keep proportions while resizing. title: Crash at exit: a GPU render still running on a worker thread segfaults in the NVIDIA Vulkan driver
author: cajax
body:
## Summary

If the process exits while a render job on an `lc-job-N` preview worker is inside the GPU path (wgpu → Vulkan
`vkCreateCommandPool`), it segfaults in `libnvidia-glcore`. The pool's workers are detached, and nothing on the way
out waits for them or stops GPU work. So `main` returns, process teardown begins, and a render is still calling
into the driver.

- **Users:** quitting while previews or an export are rendering on the GPU can end in a SIGSEGV instead of a clean
  exit. Our safety net cannot catch a SIGSEGV (the panic hook, and the `catch_unwind` around the GPU render at
  `crates/gpu/src/lib.rs:350`), so the user gets a crash report or core dump and no message. `on_exit` saves
  preferences and the library before the process ends, and exports are written atomically, so we don't expect
  data loss (not verified). It is still a crash, and under "Never crash" that outranks feature work.
- **Developers:** test binaries that use the GPU intermittently exit with 139 after printing `test result: ok`.

## Environment

- Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu, kernel 7.0), NVIDIA RTX 500 Ada Generation Laptop GPU, proprietary driver **595.91.07**,
  Vulkan backend
- wgpu / wgpu-core / wgpu-hal 30.0.1, ash 0.38.0+1.3.281, eframe 0.36.2, rustc 1.99.0 (b940084d7 2026-09-28),
  debug test profile
- Seen on the branch of PR #601 (#345). The code involved is older than #345: `JobPool` dates from M1.5 and the
  `GPU` static from M5.2a.

## Reproduction

On the PR #601 branch, first remove the test-only workaround: delete the `h.settle(..)` calls in `demo()`,
`slow_import()` and `bracket()` in `crates/ui-egui/src/tests_activity.rs` and in `demo()` in
`crates/ui-egui/src/lightroom_import.rs` (added in f8fc7f0). Then build once and
run the test binary in a loop:

```sh

n=60; segv=0
for i in $(seq "$n"); do
  "$BIN" lightroom tests_activity >/dev/null 2>&1

title: Face scan deadlocks when two scan jobs need the same demo scene (rayon work-stealing vs. the scene cache's OnceLock)
author: cajax
body:
## Summary

The background face scan can deadlock forever. Its photo jobs run as rayon jobs in a process-wide scan pool
(`ThreadPool::install`). For a demo photo, each job loads the procedural scene through `demo::scene_pixels`, which
generates the scene with a rayon `par_chunks_mut` *inside* a process-wide `OnceLock::get_or_init`. A scan-pool thread
that steals a chunk of that generation and then waits in a nested join may pick up another scan job for the **same**
scene. That job parks on the `OnceLock`, on top of the chunk the generation is waiting for. The generation never ends,
so the `OnceLock` is never filled, and every other caller of that scene waits forever too.

Impact:

- **Product, verified in one process with one session.** I ran `lightcraft-cli mcp --library` (a debug build of the
  #345 branch) on a library holding only the demo photos, with recognition on and a few virtual copies of a demo photo
  that has face regions. On 4 CPUs the scan deadlocked in 5–8 runs out of 20; on 22 threads, in 1–2 out of 10. A
  deadlocked scan never indexes another face. Any later request for that scene at that size waits forever too, and
  `faces.index` from the MCP client blocked the session thread, so the server stopped answering. Libraries of real
  files are not affected by this particular wait. But every new library starts with the demo photos
  (`apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs:7-8`), so they are what a new user tries face recognition on.
- **Tests.** `tests_face_recognize` hangs in about half the runs on this 22-thread machine and never finishes. The
  synchronous tests have no deadline, so the whole `cargo test` run blocks. Two parallel tests that each run the
  background scan are enough.

By the project's never-crash standard this counts as a crash: the work in progress is lost, nothing reports an
error, and the guard around command dispatch (`guard::catch`, which is on the stuck session thread's stack) only
catches panics.

title: Highlights slider flattens detail in bright areas (raws and 16-bit TIFF lose 30-40 % local contrast)
author: radialmonster
body:
Highlights flattens the detail in bright areas instead of only lowering their tone. Raws and 16-bit TIFFs are both affected. Reported in #632.

## Measurement

**Setup:**
- **Build:** main 88ea1a8.
- **File:** a CC0 Nikon D5 NEF from raw.pixls.us (id 2218: garden house, bright overcast sky, white walls).
- **Pixels measured:** those between 80 % and 98.5 % brightness in the unedited render.
- **Detail:** the standard deviation of a 9×9 high-pass of the luminance, divided by that region's mean brightness.

| Render | Bright mean | Detail ÷ brightness | Midtones mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| No edit | 0.891 | 0.085 | 0.386 |
| Highlights −50 | 0.788 | **0.059** | 0.386 |
| Highlights −100 | 0.735 | **0.053** | 0.386 |
| Exposure −1 (for reference) | 0.768 | 0.079 | 0.242 |
| 16-bit TIFF of the same scene, Highlights −100 | 0.570 | **0.064** | 0.354 |

**What the numbers show:**
- Highlights leaves the midtones alone, as it should.
- In the bright areas it removes about 30 % (at −50) to 40 % (at −100) of the local contrast.
- Exposure −1 lowers the same tones by a similar amount and keeps their detail.
- The result is dull, flat skies and walls rather than recovered texture.

## Where

`crates/pipeline/src/finish.rs:434-438`:
- Highlights adds a shift in log luminance, `hh * 1.7 * smooth(-1.0, 2.8, base)`.
- `base` is the edge-aware base layer from `crates/pipeline/src/local.rs` (fast guided filter, `BASE_EPS`).

The flattening suggests that the base follows too much of the fine detail. Detail that belongs in the residual gets shifted, and so compressed, together with the tone.

## Expected

At any strength, Highlights should keep the local contrast of bright areas close to what Exposure keeps, while still lowering their tone.

## Not the same as

- #196: overall strength of the sliders.
- #523: values compared with other editors.
- #607: clipped highlights staying neutral.
- #548: magenta highlights.

title: Drag-and-drop import does nothing on Linux under Wayland (winit 0.30 has no Wayland file drop)
author: radialmonster
body:
Dragging photos onto the LightCraft window does nothing on Linux under Wayland, which is the default session on current GNOME and KDE. It works on Windows, macOS and Linux under X11.

## Cause

LightCraft imports dropped files from egui's `raw.dropped_files` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:676`). egui gets them from winit, and winit 0.30.13 (the version in `Cargo.lock`, 0.4.0 and main) emits `WindowEvent::DroppedFile` only in its Windows (`platform_impl/windows/drop_handler.rs`), macOS (`platform_impl/macos/window_delegate.rs`) and X11 (`platform_impl/linux/x11/event_processor.rs`) backends. The Wayland backend has no drag-and-drop support, so the app never sees the drop.

## Workarounds

- File ▸ Import from Folder… or File ▸ Import Photos….
- Run under XWayland by starting LightCraft with `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=` unset, so winit uses X11.

## Related

- #503: drag and drop on macOS works, but there's no hover feedback or Import review on drop.
- #342: the file dialogs on Linux matched extensions case-sensitively; fixed for 0.5.0.

title: Implement GitHub Issue Templates to Standardize Reporting
author: Maijin
body:
### Description:
I suggest implementing GitHub issue templates for this repository to standardize incoming reports. Currently, it can be difficult for contributors to gauge what information is required for effective troubleshooting. See https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/about-issue-and-pull-request-templates

By introducing a structured template, you can require essential details such as the user's OS version, app version, and a clear step-by-step reproduction path (like attachments etc.). 

**Benefits of this approach:**
- **Improved Triage:** Standardized data allows maintainers to process issues more efficiently.
- **Reduced Duplicates:** A clear structure can guide users to check for existing issues before creating new ones, encouraging them to add a "+1" to relevant threads instead.
- **Higher Quality Reports:** Providing a generic structure sets expectations for what constitutes a useful bug report, leading to faster resolutions. (e.g sending the RAW file)
- You can link the feedback button to a template as well and could also include logs / version directly

I recommend having AI analyze all existing/closed issues to identify common themes, which can then be used to create basic categories (e.g., Bug Report, Feature Request, or Performance Issue) to help streamline the triage process.

title: Preview-only flags from older versions are never re-checked
author: valenfys
body:
## Problem

When a raw is imported and LightCraft can't decode it, the catalog stores the decoder's reason in `Photo::preview_only` (`crates/catalog/src/lib.rs:210`). That reason is never re-checked. After an update adds a decoder for the format, photos imported earlier stay preview-only and keep showing the old message. For example, a CR3 imported under 0.4.0 still says:

> LightCraft can't decode this raw variant yet (Cr3 files are not decoded yet). You're editing the camera's embedded JPEG preview…

Current code can no longer produce that text for a CR3 (`crates/raw/src/lib.rs:329` sends CR3 to the CRX decoder), but the saved flag survives the update. The user keeps editing the embedded JPEG and has no reason to think anything has changed.

The only fix today is to select the photos and run **Photo ▸ Reload from Disk** (`photo.reload`, `crates/engine/src/cmd/convert.rs:234`) or re-import them. Nothing tells users this.

## Reports so far

The same symptom has come up for three formats:

- #556: CR3 on 0.5.0 still showed "Cr3 files are not decoded yet". Reload from Disk cleared it.
- #473: same CR3 message. Not resolved in the thread.
- #314: RW2s imported on 0.2.1 stayed preview-only after updating until they were reloaded.

Every format the decoder learns will cause this again (compressed ORF, more CRX variants, Samsung SRW, Nikon HE …).

## Related: other data that is only read at import

#314 also found that lens data is only read at import. RW2s imported before lens-correction support never got it until Reload from Disk was taught to fill it in. Any per-photo data taken from the file at import time has the same staleness problem.

## Proposed fix

Agreed in the comments below. Still needs @echelon's OK on the catalog format bump to v7.

- **Stamp the flag with the app version.** `Photo::preview_checked: String` (`#[serde(default)]`) holds the `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` of the build that set `preview_only`. It is set at import and by `content_op`, so `photo.reload` a…

body:
## Summary

Soft proofing (View ▸ Soft Proofing, **S** in the Detail view) can only proof against five built-in RGB spaces:
sRGB, Display P3, Adobe RGB, ProPhoto RGB and Rec. 2020. There's no way to load an ICC profile, so you can't check a
photo against a printer and paper profile, a lab's profile or a press profile before printing. That's the main reason
to soft-proof. Lightroom Classic's Soft Proofing profile menu has **Other…**, which lists the installed ICC profiles
(printer, paper and CMYK ones included) and adds the chosen ones to the menu.

Tracked in `docs/parity.md` as **LRC-DEV-SOFTPROOF** (🟡). Its "Missing" list starts with printer ICC profiles.

## Where it stands

- `crates/pipeline/src/output.rs`: `Proof { space: OutputSpace, dest_warning, display_warning }`. The proof is a
  3×3 matrix into `space` and back (`Proof::params`, `params_display`).
- `crates/pipeline/src/finish.rs` (the per-pixel finish stage) maps into the proof space by desaturating towards
  luminance (`gamut_map_to`). The destination warning (red) marks what that mapping changed.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/edit.rs` (`soft_proofing`) has the Profile combo over `OutputSpace::ALL`. The command is
  `view.softProof {space, destWarning, displayWarning}`.
- Soft proofs already render on the CPU (`crates/gpu/src/lib.rs` skips requests with `proof`).
- ICC support exists, but for the monitor only. `crates/codecs/src/display.rs` reads monitor profiles through
  `moxcms`: matrix/TRC profiles exactly and LUT-based ones through the CMS, with a 32 MB cap (`MAX_PROFILE_BYTES`).
  It's relative colorimetric only. Settings ▸ Display (`app.displayProfile`) is where a profile is chosen.

## Proposal

1. **Choosing a profile**
   - The Profile combo gets **Other…**, which lists the ICC profiles installed on the system and has a file picker
     for any `.icc` / `.icm` file. System folders:
     - Linux: `~/.local/share/color/icc`, `/usr/share/color/icc`
     - macOS: `~/Library/ColorSync/Profiles`, `/…

title: Soft proofing: rendering intent switch (Perceptual / Relative Colorimetric)
author: cajax
body:
## Summary

Soft proofing has no rendering intent. Colors the proof profile can't hold are always handled one fixed way: each
out-of-gamut color is desaturated towards its luminance until it fits, and everything in gamut is left alone. Lightroom
Classic's Soft Proofing panel has an **Intent** choice, **Perceptual** or **Relative**, and photographers switch
between them to see which one keeps a saturated photo looking right on a given paper. The same choice decides how
the photo is converted when it's printed or exported for that profile.

Tracked in `docs/parity.md` as **LRC-DEV-SOFTPROOF** (🟡). "Rendering intent" is in its "Missing" list.

## Where it stands

- `crates/pipeline/src/output.rs`: `Proof { space, dest_warning, display_warning }`, with no intent.
- `crates/pipeline/src/finish.rs`: `gamut_map_to` desaturates out-of-gamut colors towards luminance. That's close to
  relative colorimetric with a soft clip. In-gamut colors don't move.
- `crates/codecs/src/display.rs` (monitor profiles, through `moxcms`) is relative colorimetric throughout.

## Proposal

1. **UI and commands**
   - Two choices under the Profile combo in Soft Proofing: **Perceptual** and **Relative**. Set the default to match
     Lightroom's (check against the observed UI in `plan/lightroom/`).
   - Saved like the other proof settings, and part of Create Proof Copy's name.
   - `view.softProof {intent: "perceptual" | "relative"}`, also reported by `ui.inspect`.
2. **Pipeline**
   - `Proof` gets `intent: Intent { Perceptual, RelativeColorimetric }` (serde default for old settings) and
     includes it in `Proof::key()`, so cached proofs don't mix intents.
3. **With an ICC profile** (#669)
   - Use the profile's tables for the chosen intent through `moxcms`: A2B0/B2A0 for perceptual, A2B1/B2A1 for
     relative colorimetric.
   - Many profiles carry no perceptual tables, or only one. Fall back to the tables the profile has, and say so in the
     panel ("this profile has no perceptual rendering…

title: Flaky test: mcp e2e export_progress_and_cancel finishes before its cancel arrives (parallel export lanes + 100 ms progress throttle)
author: cajax
body:
## Summary

`crates/mcp/tests/e2e.rs::export_progress_and_cancel` fails about half the time on a multi-core machine, on main
too: 4 of 8 runs failed at 54369512 on Linux x86_64 with 22 hardware threads. So `cargo xtask ci` fails at `test` for
reasons unrelated to the change being tested. Cancellation itself works. What fails is the test's assumption that the
export is still running when its cancel arrives.

```
thread 'export_progress_and_cancel' panicked at crates/mcp/tests/e2e.rs:237:5:
only completed photos remain: [".../cancelled/LC01333.png", ... 8 files ...]
```

## Why

The test exports 8 demo photos (`longEdge: 1200`, PNG) through `command_run app.export`. It waits for the first
`notifications/progress` with `progress > 0`, sends `notifications/cancelled`, and then expects fewer than 8 files.
Two things on main make that racy:

1. **Parallel export lanes (#504, #496).** `run_batch` now renders `export_parallelism(n)` photos side by side
   (`crates/engine/src/export.rs`: `(cores / 4).clamp(1, 4)`, so 4 here), up to `ahead` photos past the last one
   written. Eight small photos finish in about the time one took before.
2. **Progress is throttled.** `crates/mcp/src/progress.rs` (`progress_hook`) sends at most one progress notification
   per 100 ms, apart from the final one (`done == total`). So the first notification with `progress > 0` can be the
   last one, "8 of 8". By then every photo is written, and the cancel has nothing left to stop.

With one lane (`cores < 8`, as on smaller CI runners), each photo takes long enough that intermediate notifications go
out first, so it usually passes there.

Cancellation does what `progress_hook` documents ("cancellation stops before the next photo"). The hook runs as
each photo is placed, and the lanes stop with `queue.stop()`, so this isn't a product bug. One small product note:
photos the lanes rendered ahead are thrown away on cancel, which is fine.

## Fix

Make the test independent of timing. Any of these works:…

title: Flaky test: export_falls_back_to_the_cpu_when_gpu_work_is_lost reads process-wide GPU fallback state other tests overwrite
author: cajax
body:
## Summary

`crates/engine/src/tests_export.rs::export_falls_back_to_the_cpu_when_gpu_work_is_lost` fails intermittently when
the whole engine library test binary runs, on main too (1 of 2 full `cargo test --workspace --lib` runs at 54369512,
and 4 of 6 on a branch based on it). It passes every time on its own. The fallback works. The test reads GPU state
that every other test in the process shares.

```
thread 'tests_export::export_falls_back_to_the_cpu_when_gpu_work_is_lost' panicked at crates/engine/src/tests_export.rs:198:9:
device failure during the render: stopped after a GPU failure: a GPU render panicked          (main)
GPU render: out of device memory: Out of Memory                                                 (branch)
```

## Why

`crates/gpu/src/lib.rs` keeps some of the fallback state per thread and some for the whole process:
- `FAULT` (from `inject_fault`) is **thread-local**, so the injected `DropWork` only hits this test's own next render.
- `LAST_FALLBACK` ("the latest render that fell back from the GPU to the CPU and why"), `BROKEN` and `BROKEN_REASON`
  are **process-wide statics**, and `reset_failures()` clears all three.

The test injects the fault, exports (falls back), then asserts `last_fallback().contains("incomplete")` and that the
GPU is now off for the process. Meanwhile the other engine tests in the same binary are rendering on the GPU in
parallel. When one of their renders falls back for its own reason, it overwrites `LAST_FALLBACK` between this test's
export and its check. That reason was out of device memory under the parallel load, or once "a GPU render panicked".
The test also turns the GPU off for every test running at that moment, and `reset_failures()` at its end can clear
another test's genuine broken state.

## Fix

Either:
- **Ask about this render, not the last one in the process.** For example, have the export or render report its own
  fallback reason (the render path knows it when it falls back; today only the latest on…
