title: Library lock stays held after LibraryLock is dropped while another thread spawns a process (flaky second_opener_is_refused_until_the_first_lets_go)
author: cajax
body:
## Summary

`LibraryLock` (`crates/catalog/src/lock.rs`) frees the library by closing its `File`: `Drop` removes the owner note, then the handle closes and the OS is expected to release the lock. On Unix the lock is an `flock` lock. Those belong to the *open file description*, not to the descriptor, and stay held until **every** descriptor that refers to it is closed.

When any thread of the process spawns a child, `posix_spawn` (or `fork`) copies the whole descriptor table into the child, `catalog.lock` included. `O_CLOEXEC` closes the copy only when the child reaches `execve`. If another thread drops a `LibraryLock` inside that window, the lock outlives it. Re-acquiring the library then fails with `LockError::InUse(None)`, i.e. "This library is already open in another LightCraft program", even though nobody has it open. `None` because the owner note is already gone.

That is the flake in `tests_lock::second_opener_is_refused_until_the_first_lets_go`: `tests_lock::lock_held_by_another_process_is_released_when_it_dies` spawns the test binary on a parallel libtest thread at the same moment. The cause is in the product code, not the test: the test only exposes it. The fix is three lines: release explicitly with `File::unlock()` in `Drop` (see *Proposed fix*).

## Impact

- **CI / developers:** `cargo xtask ci` fails intermittently. The catalog test binary fails 15/30 (reported) and 6/20 (re-measured) runs, always on this one test.
- **Users:** nothing reproduces it today in the shipped app or CLI (see *Is the product affected?*). The race is in the product code, though, and the symptom is a false "already open" refusal that sends the user looking for another program. It doesn't crash and doesn't damage the library: a retry succeeds.
- **Other test binaries (suspected):** the engine test binary has the same mix. One test spawns a child: `demo::tests::scenes_are_generated_when_the_global_pool_is_broken` (`crates/engine/src/demo.rs`). Others drop a session and reopen the…

title: Add to Album accepts Local (browsed) photos, which album views never show: the album looks empty
author: bitshiftza
body:
**Steps**
1. In the sidebar, browse a folder under Local (photos not added to My Photos).
2. Right-click a photo ▸ Add to Album ▸ an existing album, or Photo ▸ Add to Album ▸ New Album…, or drag it onto an album row.
3. Open that album.

**Observed:** the album shows 0 photos, and its count is 0. The catalog does hold the photo: `album.create` / `album.addPhotos` take `targets()` (the selection) without looking at `Photo::local`, so the album record lists a photo that album views never show (by design, `docs/parity.md` LR-IMP-LOCAL: "browsed photos stay out of All Photos, albums and counts"). The result is an album with an invisible member and a cover that never renders.

Found while testing #676 with a Local folder open: the new album had the right-clicked photo in `catalog.snap` (`"photos":[81]`, with `"local": true` on photo 81) and nothing on screen.

**Expected (one of):**
- *Lightroom's model:* albums are for library photos only; Add to Album (context menu, Photo menu, drag onto an album row) is disabled for a Local-only selection, with a hint to Add to My Photos first, and `album.addPhotos` / `album.create {addSelected}` refuse or skip Local photos with a clear error / `skipped` count.
- *Friendlier:* adding a Local photo to an album first adds it to My Photos (`photo.addToLibrary`), in one undoable step, and says so in a toast.

Either way the engine should not commit an album member that can never be seen. The existing-album entries and drag-and-drop have had this since Local browsing landed; #676 only makes it reachable from one more place.

title: In-window menus that scroll clip the right edge of their rows: shortcut text is cut off (Linux, Windows)
author: bitshiftza
body:
**Where it shows.** A menu taller than the room under the menu bar (a short window, or a large interface scale: the View menu on a 1000 px tall window at 1.75×) switches to the window-bounded scrolling mode of `crates/ui-egui/src/menu_level.rs` (issue #189), with the ▲ / ▼ strips. In that mode the last few points of every row are clipped on the right, so the shortcut text loses its last character: `Shift+C` → `Shift+`, `Ctrl+Shift+L` → `Ctrl+Shift+`, single-letter shortcuts (`D`, `N`, `F`, `Y`, `J`, `S`, `O`) disappear almost entirely. Menus that fit are never clipped.

Reproduces headless on main (v0.5.0) at 1.0 scale, so KDE, the compositor and the display scale are not involved:

```
lightcraft-cli snapshot --demo --script view.jsonl -o out.png --size 1600x700
# view.jsonl: ui.settle · ui.set {"view":"detail"} · ui.settle · ui.clickWidget {"id":"menu:View"} · ui.screenshot
```

![View menu in scrolling mode with its shortcut text cut on the right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bitshiftza/lightcraft/issue-assets/menu-scroll-clip.png)

**Suspected cause.** The rows live in a vertical egui `ScrollArea`, which clips its content to the width it was given and does not report the rows' real width back to the popup. A popup that fits grows to its widest row (label + gap + shortcut); in scroll mode the popup keeps the width it had when the scroll area appeared, the widest rows overflow it by a few points, and egui's `Button` right-aligns the shortcut to the row's edge, inside the clipped strip. In the render above the registered scroll level ends at x = 514 while the shortcut text reaches about 518. The floating scrollbar reserves no width, and the ▲ / ▼ strips have none, so neither is the cause.

Only the in-window menu bar is affected (Linux, Windows, and macOS with the native menu bar off); the native macOS menu bar does not go through this code.

title: Regression: DSC-F828 SRF and DSLR-A100 ARW no longer open (Sony probe needs raw evidence since #281)
author: AlexChambers
body:
**Regression on `main` b70ae17:** two public Sony raws that opened on `main` 5436951 are now refused as "not a readable photo":

| raw.pixls.us file | `main` 5436951 | `main` b70ae17 |
|---|---|---|
| DSC-F828 `DSC06227.SRF` | opens (`lightcraft-cli render` writes 600×450) | `not a readable photo` |
| DSLR-A100 `DSC0258.ARW` | opens (600×450) | `not a readable photo` |

The other 133 Sony files of my sweep (129 raw.pixls.us files covering all 100 Sony bodies there, 4 corpus files and the two from #244) render as before.

**Cause:** the camera-TIFF reconciliation for #281 (fb6dda44) made `probe` require raw evidence for Sony: `make.starts_with("SONY") && has_cfa`, where `has_cfa` is `has_raw_ifd`. Neither file has any of the evidence `has_raw_ifd` looks for (a CFA photometric, compression 34713 / 32767 / 32769 / 32770 / 99 / 65535, tag 0x7010, a CFA pattern tag):

- **DSC-F828 SRF:** IFD0 is `PhotometricInterpretation` RGB, uncompressed, `BitsPerSample` 14 14 14, 3360 wide; the raw and its keys are in Sony's SRF structure, not in tags `has_raw_ifd` reads. IFD0's tags are 256–306 only (no private tags).
- **DSLR-A100 ARW:** IFD0 is the old-JPEG thumbnail; the raw is located by tag 330 (`SubIFDs`, which the A100 uses as a plain offset to its raw data, exiftool's `A100DataOffset`) and a Minolta-style raw block.

So both now fall through to `None`.

**Suggested fix** (I can open a PR if you'd like): extra Sony raw evidence that a camera-authored or exported TIFF doesn't have, for example:
- `BitsPerSample` of 12 or 14 in IFD0 (an ordinary TIFF image uses 8 or 16), and
- tag 330 present on IFD0 together with `Model` `DSLR-A100` (or more generally, a `SubIFDs` value that isn't a valid IFD offset).

…plus a probe test for each layout, next to the ones #281 added for Pentax and Samsung.

Found with a sweep of public Sony files against `main` before and after the batch (`lightcraft-cli render --size 1200`, same settings).

title: `probe_info` decodes the whole Huffman stream of compressed NEFs (~390 ms per file instead of < 1 ms)
author: PiMinusMax
body:
### What

`lightcraft_raw::probe_info` (used for every file an import adds, via `probe_bytes` in `crates/engine/src/files.rs`) is meant to read headers only. For every format it takes well under 1 ms, except compressed NEF: on a Nikon D750 14-bit lossless NEF (CC0, raw.pixls.us) it takes **386 ms**, about the same as a full decode (395 ms). Importing a folder of 1,000 such NEFs spends ~6–7 minutes just probing.

| File | full decode | `probe_info` |
|---|---|---|
| ARW α77 II | 88 ms | 0.2 ms |
| CR2 5D III | 681 ms | 0.1 ms |
| CR3 EOS R (C-RAW) | 839 ms | 0.2 ms |
| DNG Ricoh GR III | 808 ms | 0.2 ms |
| **NEF D750 lossless 14-bit** | 395 ms | **386 ms** |
| RAF X-A5 | 74 ms | 0.0 ms |

(main @ b70ae174, release build, `crates/raw/tests/corpus.rs` with `LIGHTCRAFT_CORPUS` pointing at the six files, i7-7820HQ.)

### Where

- `crates/raw/src/lib.rs` (`decode_with`): NEF/NRW is the only format called without `mode`: `vendor::nef::decode(bytes)`.
- `crates/raw/src/vendor/nef.rs`: the samples are needed for `trailing_masked_columns` (added in M3.7 for uncompressed NEFs). Since compressed NEFs decode too, the same path now runs the full Huffman decode in header mode.
- The `probe_info` doc says these formats read their samples "unpacked, nothing to decompress", which no longer holds for compressed NEFs.

### Options

1. In header mode, decode only as many rows of a compressed NEF as the masked-column test needs. The stream is sequential, so this means changing the test to look at the first N rows (e.g. 256) instead of rows spread over the whole height. Risk: a dark top of the frame could change the result, so `probe_info` and the full decode might disagree on `active_area`.
2. In header mode, skip the masked-column test for compressed NEFs when maker note CropArea (`0x0045`) is present and valid, and let the full decode refine `active_area`. Changes the "probe equals decoded info" contract for those files.
3. Find out which bodies actually write masked trailing columns …

title: Smart previews render visibly different from the original (8-bit JPEG proxy: ΔE2000 mean 1.1–2.2, P99 4.4–8.6)
author: PiMinusMax
body:
### What

A photo rendered from its smart preview differs visibly from the same edit rendered from the original: JPEG 8×8 block artefacts, banding in smooth gradients (sky) and a small constant colour shift (a* +0.3 to +0.4, +0.7 with strong colour edits). Today this only matters while an original is offline, but it rules out ever using smart previews for faster editing (an option to edit from smart previews instead of originals; tracker LR-CLOUD-SMARTPREVIEW / LR-PREF-PERFORMANCE).

### Where

- `crates/engine/src/smart.rs` (`encode`): the scene-linear source is scaled so the brightest 0.05 % clip at 1.0, sRGB-encoded to **8 bits** and stored as **JPEG q92** (4:4:4).
- Tracker row: LR-CLOUD-SMARTPREVIEW (✅).

### Measurement

File: Sony α77 II ARW (`ILCA-77M2`, CC0 from raw.pixls.us). Ten edit sets (sharpening and colour noise reduction off). Each set exported as a 16-bit PNG once from the original and once with the original offline (smart preview only, 2560 px long edge, 482 KB). Measured on main @ b70ae174. Both are compared on the smart-preview grid (linear 4×4 area average of the full export), CIEDE2000.

| Edit set | mean | P99 |
|---|---|---|
| default | 1.57 | 5.88 |
| white balance (3800 K, tint +12) | 1.09 | 8.63 |
| exposure +0.8, contrast +40 | 1.71 | 6.54 |
| highlights −80, shadows +70 | 1.63 | 6.19 |
| whites +40, blacks −40 | 1.57 | 5.86 |
| clarity +60 | 1.62 | 5.97 |
| texture +60 | 1.67 | 6.20 |
| vibrance, saturation, mixer | 2.19 | 7.54 |
| parametric curve | 1.50 | 5.79 |
| crop + 6° straighten | 1.40 | 4.38 |

For comparison, another raw editor that stores its proxies as half-float scene-linear data (lossless entropy coding, mantissa rounded below the noise level, about 11 MB at 2560 px) measures 0.08–0.40 mean and 0.26–1.49 P99 on the same file and sets. Its test is measured inside its pipeline in float, so the numbers are indicative, not 1:1. A per-pixel ΔE map of ours shows where the error comes from: 8×8 JPEG block patterns across the whol…

title: Control channel (and MCP --connect) stalls while the window is not visible on Wayland
author: jazzautomations
body:
## Summary

With the app running `--control 7980` on Linux/Wayland (sway), every control-channel request stalls for as long as the LightCraft window is not visible — on another workspace, or fully covered by a fullscreen window. `lightcraft-cli run --connect …` reports `"error":"timeout"` for each request; the moment the workspace with the window is shown again, all the queued requests run at once. The app itself is fine (1–2 % CPU, no busy threads), it just never gets a frame.

The MCP server in `--connect` mode has the same behaviour, since it is the same channel — an agent driving the app while the user works on another workspace sees every tool call time out.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `LIGHTCRAFT_GPU=0 lightcraft --control 7980` on sway (Wayland). Any photo selected.
2. Switch to another workspace (or put another window fullscreen on top).
3. `lightcraft-cli run --connect library.state` → hangs, then `{"command":"library.state","error":"timeout","ok":false}`.
4. Switch back to the workspace with LightCraft → the stalled requests complete immediately (e.g. `view.zoom100` reported `"ms":51603.0`, the time the window was hidden).

Same with `develop.set`, `library.import`, `ui.screenshot`.

## Expected

Control requests are served whether or not the window is currently visible (they are dispatched on the UI thread today, `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs` → `handle`, and reach it only from `update`). Headless rendering (`docs/control-protocol.md`) is not a substitute for driving the live app the user is looking at (or will look at in a moment).

## Why (as far as I can tell)

On Wayland a surface that is not visible gets no frame callbacks; winit/eframe then does not deliver `RedrawRequested`, so `App::update` never runs and the control requests queue up behind it. `ctx.request_repaint()` from the control thread does not help: the wakeup arrives, but the frame is still gated on the compositor. Possible directions: a timer-driven poll of the control queue independent …

```
thread 'tests_denoise::a_photo_waits_for_its_turn_unless_pictures_are_not_made_on_their_own_or_have_nowhere_to_go' panicked at crates/engine/src/tests_denoise.rs:710:9:
assertion failed: !x.s.denoise_busy()
```

Line 710 is the third `denoise_busy()` check: after `denoise.queue` and `pump_until_ready(&mut x.s, 1)` have brought the photo to `PhotoState::Ready`, the session is still reported busy.

## Suspects

- `pump_until_ready` returns once the photo's state is `Ready`, but `denoise_busy()` may also count work that is still being torn down or written (the picture being saved beside the library, a worker handing back its result), so there is a window where the photo is ready and the session is still busy, widened when the machine is loaded by the other tests.
- Or `denoise_busy()` reads shared worker state (a global pool, `LIGHTCRAFT_DENOISE_*`) that another denoise test in the same process is using at that moment, as the GPU fallback state was in #675.

## Reproduce

```sh
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do cargo test -q -p lightcraft-engine --lib 2>&1 | grep -E "a_photo_waits_for_its_turn.*FAILED|tests_denoise.rs:710"; done
cargo test -p lightcraft-engine --lib -- a_photo_waits_for_its_turn   # alone: passes
```

Linux x86_64, NVIDIA RTX 4090 (Vulkan), 24 threads, with the test binary's default parallelism.

title: Absolute Kelvin white balance for raws whose camera has colour matrices
author: cajax
body:
## Problem

The white-balance scale is chosen by file extension, not by whether LightCraft knows the camera's colour:

- UI / catalog: `Photo::relative_wb()` (`crates/catalog/src/model.rs:314`) puts every ARW, NEF, NRW, RW2, RWL, RAW, RAF, CR3, CR2, PEF, SRW and ORF on the relative −100…+100 scale.
- Render: `crates/engine/src/files.rs:370` sets `relative_wb` when the file has no colour matrices *of its own*, decided before the spectral lookup, so even raws that fall back to the spectral matrices keep relative WB (adapted generically in `crates/pipeline/src/local.rs:35` instead of through the camera matrices).

So the 52 models with measured matrices in `lightcraft_raw::spectral` (e.g. ILCE-7M3, ILCE-7M4, ILCE-7RM3, D850, EOS 5D Mark III) never get a Kelvin readout, unlike Lightroom. For most of their files the matrices are not used at all: the JPEG fit (`camera_preview::starting_colour`) wins, and the matrices are only the fallback when it fails.

## Proposal

When a camera has colour matrices (its own in the file, or a `spectral` table row), show As Shot and the Temp slider in Kelvin:

- The colour look stays as it is (JPEG fit or bundled per-model profile). The matrices only convert white balance to and from Kelvin: as-shot multipliers → As Shot Kelvin/tint; slider Kelvin/tint → multipliers → the shift applied relative to the as-shot look.
- Raws without matrices keep the relative scale.
- The catalog decision (`Photo::relative_wb`) and the render decision (`files.rs`) must agree.

## Must handle

- **Existing edits:** catalogs and XMP sidecars hold Custom WB on the relative scale (6500 = as shot). Upgrading must not change any photo's look (same class of bug as #510): mark or convert those values.
- **XMP interop:** Lightroom writes `crs:Temperature` for these raws as absolute Kelvin, which is currently shifted from `crs:AsShotTemperature` (#510); with an absolute scale this becomes direct.
- **Presets** (Daylight, Cloudy, Shade, Tungsten, Fluorescent, Flash) ma…

title: Straighten slider / Angle field let the crop box extend past the photo: the crop.angle control skips the constrain-to-image fit that crop.straighten applies
author: bitshiftza
body:
## What

Setting the crop angle through the **Straighten slider** (Geometry panel), the **Angle field** under the Straighten tool, or `develop.set {"crop.angle": …}` rotates the crop box without shrinking it to fit the photo, so the box advertises a crop that includes empty canvas outside the image. Dragging the rotation handle in the crop tool, or `crop.straighten {angle}`, shrinks the box to the largest rectangle of the current aspect that fits at that angle, as Lightroom's "Constrain to image" does. The two paths disagree about the same photo.

Seen while fixing #731 (the +15° frames in #739's screenshot show the box past the photo's edges).

## Where

- `crates/geom/src/crop.rs`: `CropGeometry::constrained` and `max_inscribed_scale` already implement the fit.
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/develop.rs`: `crop.set` calls `constrained(w, h)` after any change; `crop.straighten` keeps the current rect if `is_within_image`, else `crop_fit_angle`.
- `crates/develop/src/controls.rs:255`: `"crop.angle" => crop.geometry.angle` is a plain develop control, so the generic slider path (`develop.set`, the Geometry panel slider via `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/right.rs:196`, the Angle field) writes the angle and nothing re-fits the rect.

## Expected

Every way of setting the angle gives the same geometry as `crop.straighten`: keep the rect if it still fits, else shrink about its centre keeping the aspect. The exported image should be checked too: if it is clamped to the valid area today this is overlay-plus-model only; if it writes empty corners it is a real defect.

## Reproduce

```sh
lightcraft-cli snapshot --demo --script s.jsonl -o out.png --size 1600x1000
# s.jsonl: open a photo in the loupe, enter the crop tool, then
# {"method":"engine.execute","params":{"command":"develop.set","params":{"crop.angle":15}}}
# versus
# {"method":"engine.execute","params":{"command":"crop.straighten","params":{"angle":15}}}
```

The first leaves the box past the photo; the second shrinks it.

title: White Balance Selector samples the wrong point in the Before view of side by side / top-bottom
author: PiMinusMax
body:
### What

With Before / After set to side by side (or top / bottom), the White Balance Selector (W) works when clicking the After view, but a click on the Before view silently picks a different white balance: it samples the wrong point of the photo (at Fit, its edge), not the point under the cursor. The other click tools on the loupe (colour-range and point-colour samplers, targeted adjustment) go through the same mapping, so they are likely affected too; the regression test covers the White Balance Selector.

The split (wipe) views show one image and are not affected.

### Steps

1. Detail view, any photo; View → Before/After → side by side.
2. Press W, click a neutral spot in the **left** (Before) view.
3. The white balance differs from clicking the same spot in the right (After) view.

Measured headless on main @ b70ae174 (procedural demo photo, the same image point in both views; the absolute values only matter in that they differ): the After view gives 2710 K / +33, the Before view 8202 K / +116.

### Cause

`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/detail.rs`: the `CanvasMap` that turns screen positions into normalized image coordinates is built once from the After view's rectangle (`img_rect`). A click in the Before view maps outside the photo (x < 0, or y < 0 when stacked), and `develop.wbPick` clamps that to the edge.

### Fix

PR to follow: for the click tools handled by `general_interaction`, use the Before view's image rectangle when the pointer is in the Before view's pane (the pane, not the image rectangle: zoomed in, an image reaches past its pane). Both views show the same frame. New regression test `crates/ui-egui/src/tests_before_after.rs` clicks the same image point in the After and Before views (side by side and top / bottom, at Fit and at 100 %) and expects the same white balance; it fails without the fix.

Tracker: LR-VIEW-BEFOREAFTER (note added with the fix).

title: Compare: a filmstrip click makes a hidden photo active (edits and ratings go to a photo that isn't shown)
author: PiMinusMax
body:
### What

In Compare, clicking a photo in the filmstrip doesn't change the two photos shown, but it makes the clicked photo the active one. The Edit panel then shows that photo's settings, and sliders and rating / flag keys act on it, although it is on neither side. Only the arrow keys change the candidate. Same at Fit and zoomed in.

### Steps

1. Select two photos, View → Compare (Shift+C).
2. Click a third photo in the filmstrip: Select and Candidate stay the same, the Edit panel switches to the clicked photo.
3. Press 3: the hidden photo gets three stars.

Reproduced headless on main @ b70ae174 (demo library): after the click the pair stays, the clicked photo is active, and `3` changes its rating from 2 to 3.

### Cause

The filmstrip click (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/detail.rs`, `filmstrip`) runs `library.select` in every view. Compare keeps its pair separately (`app.ui.compare`, `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/compare.rs`) and only replaces it when one of its photos is gone.

### Proposal

- In Compare, a filmstrip click puts the photo into the **active side**: the candidate after entering Compare, the select after clicking the select's photo. A photo already on the other side swaps the two. The clicked photo becomes active, so what is edited is always on screen.
- New UI command `compare.set {id, side?: "select" | "candidate"}` for the same through the control channel / MCP.
- Questions: is "active side" the behaviour you want, or should a click always replace the candidate? Would drag and drop from the filmstrip onto either side be welcome as a follow-up?

A PR with this behaviour and headless tests follows; happy to adjust it to your answer.

Tracker: LR-VIEW-COMPARE.

title: Sharpening: Radius and Detail have no effect, and Sharpening works at ~11 px (the texture band), not pixel scale
author: radialmonster
body:
Found while looking at #741 (soft A6000 ARWs, where the reporter also noticed that Radius and Detail do nothing).

**What happens (on `main` b70ae174 and in 0.5.0):**
- **Radius and Detail are never read.** `detail.sharpen_radius` and `detail.sharpen_detail` are stored, and read from and written to XMP (`crates/engine/src/crs.rs`), but no pipeline code reads them. On the A6000 file from #741, exports with Radius 3 or Detail 100 are byte-identical to the default.
- **Sharpening works on the texture band, not on fine detail.** `finish.rs` builds sharpening from `l_pre - texture_blur`. `texture_blur` is a Gaussian with σ = 0.0018 × the long edge (`local.rs` `plane_sigmas`), which is **about 11 px on a 6000 px image**. So the Sharpening slider boosts mid-scale texture. It doesn't sharpen edges at the pixel level, which is what a 1 px radius should do. Raw renders look soft at 100 % even though sharpening is on by default (40), and the default sharpening adds texture instead of acuity.
- **Masking is the only modifier that works.** It gates on the same texture-band detail.

**Expected:**
- **Radius:** sets the σ of the sharpening blur, in source pixels (0.5 to 3, default 1), scaled to the render's resolution so that previews and exports match.
- **Detail:** controls how much of the finest detail, and halo suppression, is kept (0 = dampen halos, 100 = full deconvolution-like boost).
- **Masking:** keeps working as an edge mask.
- **CPU and GPU:** `finish.wgsl` must match the CPU path.

**Repro:** `lightcraft-cli run --import <A6000 ARW> develop.set control=detail.sharpenRadius value=3 app.export path=a.png`. The output is identical to the export without the `develop.set`.

`docs/parity.md` lists LR-EDIT-DETAIL-SHARPEN as ✅. It should be 🟡 until Radius and Detail work.

I'm working on this.

title: Library: move photos between folders, and create folders on disk
author: PiMinusMax
body:
The Folders section can rename and move whole folders (`folder.rename`, `folder.move`, one undo step, photos relinked, sidecars included). There's no way yet to move individual photos to another folder, or to create a folder on disk. `docs/parity.md` lists both under the LRC-LIB-LIBFOLDERS limits: "creating a folder and moving photos between folders are not here".

**Proposed behaviour**
- Drag selected photos from the grid onto a folder in the sidebar, or use *Move to Folder…* from the photo's context menu.
- The files move on disk with their XMP sidecars, the photos are relinked, and the whole move is one undo step. A name that's already taken in the destination gets -1, -2…, as in Import. Nothing is overwritten.
- Moving across volumes copies, verifies and only then removes the source, like Move import. Undo does the same in the other direction.
- Long moves show a row in the activity stack.
- *New Folder on Disk…* on a folder row creates a subfolder. (The existing *New Folder…*, `dialog.newFolder` / ⌘⇧N, creates an album folder, so the disk command needs a distinct label.)

**Commands** (so CLI and MCP can use them too): `folder.create {parent, name}` and `photo.moveToFolder {ids?, folder}`.

**Edge cases**
- An offline or missing original is refused with a clear error.
- Virtual copies share their master's file, so they always move with it.
- Local (not imported) photos are refused.
- Open question: should moving the top of a collapsed stack move the whole stack?

**Building blocks that already exist:** `Op::Relink`, the undo pattern of `move_folder` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/browse.rs`), the verified copy from Move import (`import_move.rs`), and dragging photos onto sidebar rows (albums).

**Plan:** two PRs, `folder.create` first, then the move. Tracker: LRC-LIB-LIBFOLDERS. Related: #294 (per-folder sync, where moving photos is how users would choose what syncs).

I'd be glad to work on this.

title: Esc in the crop tool jumps to the grid instead of leaving the tool
author: PiMinusMax
body:
### What

With the crop tool open (C) in Detail, pressing Esc doesn't close the tool: it goes straight back to the grid. To leave the crop tool and stay on the photo you have to press C again or click the crop icon.

### Steps

1. Open a photo in Detail, press C.
2. Press Esc: the grid appears; the crop tool is never closed on the photo.

Reproduced headless on main @ b70ae174.

### Cause

Esc runs `view.back` (`crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs`). It first closes dialogs, the keyword painter, full screen and an armed on-image tool (`app.ui.tool`), then changes the view. The crop tool is a right panel (`RightPanel::Crop`), not an `app.ui.tool`, so nothing catches it and the next step leaves Detail.

### Related: Esc in a text field also runs Back

Esc in a text field (e.g. the crop tool's Angle field) should only leave the field. egui drops the field's keyboard focus as the Esc key arrives, before `shortcuts::handle` reads the keys, so its `egui_wants_keyboard_input()` check no longer sees the field and Esc runs `view.back` as well. Today that silently goes to the grid; with the crop step above it would close the crop tool. The existing test `escape_in_the_angle_field_keeps_the_angle` only checks the crop panel, so it doesn't notice the view change.

### Fix

PR to follow:
- In Detail with the crop tool open, Esc closes the crop tool like C does (the crop stays); the next Esc goes back to the grid as before.
- The app remembers whether a text field had the keyboard at the end of the last frame; Esc that ends such an edit does nothing else (like Esc that closes a popup).

New headless tests in `crates/ui-egui/src/tests_crop_tool.rs`; both fail without the fix.

Tracker: KEY-ESC.

title: Flip H / Flip V don't show in the crop tool
author: PiMinusMax
body:
### What

With the crop tool open, Flip H and Flip V (buttons in the Crop panel, or Photo → Flip) change the photo, but the crop tool's view doesn't show it: the photo and the crop box stay unflipped until the tool is closed. Then the cropped result appears mirrored, so the box was drawn over a picture that isn't what you get.

### Steps

1. Open a photo in Detail, press C, set a crop away from the centre.
2. Click Flip H: nothing changes on screen.
3. Close the crop tool: the result is mirrored.

Reproduced headless on main @ b70ae174.

### Cause

`crates/pipeline/src/geometry.rs` (`Frame::with_lens`) turns the flips off together with the crop (`flip_h: apply_crop && s.crop.flip_h`). The crop tool renders and maps the uncropped frame (`apply_crop = false`), so it loses the flips too. A flip isn't part of the crop.

When the flips are kept, the crop overlay needs one more change: the dimming outside the box pairs each photo corner with a box corner in data order (`crop_overlay` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/detail.rs`). With a flipped photo the box's corners reach the screen mirrored, so the dimming would land inside the box.

### Fix

PR to follow: the frame keeps the flips without the crop, and the dimming takes the box's corners in screen order. The crop box, its handles and drags already go through the frame's mapping, so they follow the mirror. Tests: `uncropped_frame_keeps_the_flips` (pipeline, fails without the fix) and a unit test for the corner order; checked visually with headless screenshots for H, V and H+V.

Note: PR #739 rewrites the same dimming code (#731) with a mesh that doesn't depend on the corner order; with it, only the `geometry.rs` part of this fix is needed.

Tracker: LR-CROP-FLIP.

title: Dialogs taller than the window can't scroll: on a 1366×768 screen the Export dialog's Cancel / Export buttons are off screen
author: bitshiftza
body:
## Problem

On a 1366×768 screen (Windows, reported on Discord), **File ▸ Export…** is taller than the window. Its title and "1 photo" line run off the top, and **Save preset** and the **Cancel / Export** buttons run off the bottom, so the dialog can't be confirmed. Nothing scrolls, and there is no interface-scale setting to make it fit.

Reproduced headlessly on main (b70ae174) at 1366×690, roughly what a maximised window leaves on that screen after the taskbar and title bar:

![Export dialog at 1366×690: title off the top, buttons off the bottom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bitshiftza/lightcraft/issue-assets/export-dialog-1366x690.png)

```sh
# s.jsonl: {"method":"ui.menu.invoke","params":{"id":"dialog.export"}} then {"method":"ui.screenshot"}
lightcraft-cli snapshot --demo --script s.jsonl -o out.png --size 1366x690
```

## Cause

Every dialog except Import is a fixed, centred `egui::Window` with no height limit and no scrolling (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/dialogs.rs`, `show`: `.resizable(import).vscroll(import)`). body:
## Problem

## Cause

`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/dialogs.rs`, the dialog footer: a dialog gets one **Close** button (no Cancel) only when it's in the `informational` list, which holds `About`, `Shortcuts` and `Settings` (and an unusable model file). `SystemInfo`, `AllMetadata` and `WhatsNew` aren't in it, yet their confirm does nothing (`confirm_dialog`: `Dialog::AllMetadata { .. } | Dialog::SystemInfo { .. } | Dialog::WhatsNew => Ok(Value::Null)`), so they fall through to the default **Cancel / OK** pair.

## Expected

System Info, All Metadata and What's New end with a single **Close**, like About. System Info keeps its **Copy to Clipboard** button.

title: Linux Mint desktop session crashes when resizing LightCraft window (NVIDIA Nouveau)
author: jeffjeffreyjeff
body:
# Linux Mint desktop session crashes when resizing LightCraft window (NVIDIA Nouveau)

## Description

Resizing the LightCraft application window on Linux Mint causes the entire graphical desktop session to crash, returning to the login screen.

The problem also occurs with other ArtCraft applications, but not with ordinary Linux desktop applications or RapidRAW.

## System information

- Hardware: Apple 27-inch iMac
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 775M Mac Edition (GK104M, 2 GB)
- Graphics driver: Nouveau
- Operating system: Linux Mint MATE, Ubuntu 24.04-based
- Kernel: 7.0.0-38-generic
- Display server: Xorg
- GUI framework: egui/eframe 0.36, wgpu 30

## Steps to reproduce

1. Launch LightCraft.
2. Resize the application window, particularly towards the edge of the screen.
3. The graphical desktop crashes and returns to the login screen.

## Expected behaviour

The application window resizes normally without affecting the desktop session.

## Actual behaviour

Nouveau reports a GPU fault, followed by an Xorg crash and a new desktop login session.

Relevant system log:

```text
nouveau ... fifo: fault 00 [READ] ... reason 02 [PTE]
nouveau ... gr: TRAP ch 2 [Xorg]
nouveau ... Xorg: channel 2 killed!
systemd-coredump: Process (Xorg) dumped core.
```

## Troubleshooting performed

- Disabled MATE window compositing — still crashes.
- Launched using `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` — still crashes.
- Launched using `LIGHTCRAFT_GPU_BACKEND=off` — still crashes.
- Tested resizing other Linux applications, including RapidRAW — no crashes.

LightCraft is built with eframe's `wgpu` feature, without the `glow` feature.

## Additional information

The failure appears to involve the interaction between the application's window-rendering path and the Nouveau graphics driver. It may be a Nouveau bug triggered by the application rather than an application defect.

title: Web release zip ships Cargo build artifacts (deps/, build/, .fingerprint/ — ~113 MB)
author: natocool2
body:
`lightcraft-web-0.5.0.zip` (96 MB download, 191 MB unpacked) ships Cargo build artifacts next to the site. Measured on the release asset:

| top-level folder in the zip | files | size |
|---|---|---|
| `deps/` | 81 | 90.6 MB |
| `build/` | 149 | 22.4 MB |
| `.fingerprint/` | 297 | — |
| `examples/`, `incremental/` | 2 | — |
| the site itself (root) | 31 | 78.5 MB |

None of it is referenced by the app; it only makes the download bigger and exposes build paths and crate names to anyone who hosts the zip.

**Cause** (still present on `main` at b70ae17): `xtask/src/web.rs` writes the site to `target_dir.join("web")` (line 110), and the release build uses the Cargo profile named `web` (line 103). When cross-compiling with `--target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, Cargo puts the *host* artifacts of that profile (build scripts, proc-macros) in `target/web/` too — so `deps/`, `build/` and `.fingerprint/` land in the site folder, and `packaging/web/package.sh` copies `$CARGO_TARGET_DIR/web/.` into the zip.

**Fix options:** write the site to a directory that isn't a profile name (e.g. `target/web-site`, and point `SITE=` in `package.sh` at it), or rename the profile (e.g. `wasm-release`). Either way, a guard in `package.sh` that fails if `deps/` or `.fingerprint/` exists in `$SITE` would keep it from coming back.

(Found while hosting the web builds; we strip these folders on our side for now.)

title: Zoomed side by side / top-bottom Before / After: a blurred border around the Before view
author: PiMinusMax
body:
### What

In the side by side and top/bottom Before / After views, zoomed in (e.g. 100 %), the Before pane shows a sharp picture only inside its pane. Around it, in the margins at the canvas edges and in the gap between the two panes, a magnified, blurred picture shows. The Before side looks like it doesn't fill its half, framed by a soft border. At Fit everything is fine.

The Before / After labels also disappear when zoomed in: they sit under the photo's bottom edge, which is then far off screen.

### Steps

1. Open a photo in Detail, press Y (side by side), or choose View → Before/After → Top/Bottom.
2. Zoom to 100 % and pan a bit.
3. Look at the margins around the Before pane and the gap between the panes.

Reproduced headless on main @ b70ae174.

### Cause

`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/detail.rs` (`show`): the window renders (the sharp part on screen) are clipped to their pane (`region::window_clip`), but the whole-frame renders under them are drawn on the whole canvas. Zoomed in, each view's photo reaches far past its pane. The After's whole-frame render is drawn last, so its magnified, low-resolution picture covers the Before pane's margins and the gap.

### Fix

PR to follow: the whole-frame renders are clipped to their pane too, as their windows already are. The labels sit under the photo, or under the pane when the photo reaches past it. Test: zoomed in, the margins and the gap show the background as at Fit (fails without the fix).

Tracker: LR-VIEW-BEFOREAFTER.

body:
A Canon EOS R50 C-RAW CR3 opens preview-only: the import falls back to the embedded JPEG instead of decoding the raw.

title: Lightroom catalog import: every original is read in full and hashed, progress stays near 0 % and Cancel waits for all of it (38k photos ≈ 25 min on a USB SSD)
author: ingolfteetz
body:
I said on #146 that I'm short on time these days, but when my own catalog sat at "14 of 38,556" for half an hour I couldn't resist. And once it went through in a few minutes, the endorphins kicked in ;-)

A data point from a real catalog, and a working branch.

**Measured on main (964d9338)**, macOS, Apple M5 Max: catalog `2026.lrcat` with 38,545 photos (CR3 from an EOS R5 Mark II, Leica M11-P DNG, ORF, JPEG). 1.1 TB of originals on a USB SSD (exFAT, ~850 MB/s).

- Reading the catalog takes 1.6 s. Everything after that is probing the originals: `fs_hooks`' probe reads each file whole and hashes it. That is 1.1 TB, about 22 min of reading alone at the measured rate. I didn't let it run to the end.
- All 38k paths go to `ImportJob::prepare_files` as one batch. `probe_all` counts into a local `ScanProgress`, so the activity row stays at "14 of 38,556" the whole time. Its cancel flag is never set, so ✕ only takes effect after every file has been read.
- Then `apply_prepared` runs on the owner thread for ~5 s: XMP parsing, Lua parsing, `crs` mapping and `apply_partial` for every photo (profiled).
- On exFAT, `find_sidecar`'s four `is_file` checks per photo cost another 8–18 s. Nearly all of them ask for files that aren't there.

**What my branch does** (two commits, `LRC-LIB-CATALOG-IMPORT`):

- `lightcraft_raw::sparse::header_plan` says which byte ranges `probe_info` and `lightcraft_meta::extract` read, given a buffer of the file's length in which only some ranges are loaded. That is everything but the bulk sample data. It keeps the first chunk's coding headers, a CR3's CRX headers, QP maps and CTMD track, and a RAF's compression header. `preview_plan` also loads what `embedded_preview` needs, for raws shown from their preview. NEF, ORF and PEF (their probe looks at samples) and non-raw files are read whole.
- The Lightroom import uses that probe (`ImportOptions::headers_only`). Raws probed this way get no content hash. A later import of a copy hashes same-size photos o…

title: feat(automation): guide desktop users through agent setup

## Summary

Add optional desktop setup that locates lightcraft-cli, prepares client-ready MCP configuration and checks the local server.

## Problem to solve

Desktop installation and agent configuration are separate tasks. Windows packages include the CLI without adding PATH commands; Linux exposure depends on package format; macOS supplies a separate download. Users must locate the executable and adapt documentation to their client. An in-app flow would make this discoverable and check the actual installation.

Provide a Help or Preferences entry that shows the executable's absolute path, version and MCP capability separately from PATH availability. Allow selection of an existing CLI. If none is usable, offer the official matching installation or download and check afterward.

title: feat(distribution): provide supported CLI access from desktop installations
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Give desktop users a documented, reliable way to invoke lightcraft-cli on Windows, Linux and macOS for scripts and agents independently of shell PATH.

## Problem to solve

CLI availability differs across desktop packages. Windows and Linux already include executables in several formats, while macOS uses a separate download. Internal bundling alone does not tell a script how to launch the CLI. Users need a supported invocation that matches their installed release and remains clear after an update.

## Proposed behavior

Define and document a supported CLI path or launcher for each advertised desktop distribution. Make it usable outside the desktop UI and independent of MCP client configuration. For macOS, supply the CLI with the desktop distribution or offer an intentional integrated installation of the matching CLI. Preserve standalone downloads.

Expose shell installation only as an explicit option. Document invocation by absolute path or package launcher without prescribing a bundle layout.

## Acceptance criteria

- Affected packages and added executables retain the existing release signing, notarization and native-package validation requirements.
- Windows MSI installation exposes the installed CLI through a documented full path or supported launcher, including a custom installation directory. Portable ZIP users can invoke their adjacent executable without automatic global writes.

title: Canon EOS R6 CR3: JPEG-fitted colour matrix amplifies noise ~5x (same Bayer data via Adobe DNG is clean)
author: 4ebass-cmyk
body:
## Summary

Canon EOS R6 CR3 at ISO 1600 develops with far more noise in LightCraft than in Lightroom, mostly as bright blue/lavender "salt" speckles on dark blue surfaces. The CR3 decoder is not the cause: the Bayer data is bit-identical to LibRaw and Adobe DNG Converter. The **same Bayer data, opened in LightCraft as an Adobe-converted DNG (with Adobe's ColorMatrix/ForwardMatrix), is clean**. That points at the colour transform used for CR3s without a measured matrix (the JPEG-fitted matrix, see #577), which seems to amplify blue-channel noise about 5×.

## Setup

- LightCraft Windows build (installed 2026-10-10), `lightcraft-cli render` with default settings
- Canon EOS R6, uncompressed (lossless) CR3, 5472×3648, ISO 1600, f/4, 1/200, EF 70-200mm f/4L USM
- Windows 11 Pro, Ryzen 7 5700X3D

## What I checked

1. **Sensor data is identical.** Raw Bayer samples from LibRaw 0.22.1 (on the CR3), from the Adobe DNG Converter DNG, and from LightCraft's own `photo.convertToDng` output match 100% (mean |diff| = 0, max |diff| = 0). Black level is 2048 in all three. So the CRX decode for the R6 is correct.
2. **The DNGs differ in colour metadata.** Adobe's DNG has ColorMatrix1/2, ForwardMatrix1/2, CameraCalibration1, BaselineExposure +0.19, BaselineNoise 0.8 and a NoiseProfile. LightCraft's DNG has only BlackLevel, WhiteLevel (14888), AsShotNeutral and BaselineExposure 0, with no colour matrix. Minor: its UniqueCameraModel is `Canon Canon EOS R6` (the make is duplicated).
3. **A/B inside LightCraft.** I rendered the same 700×500 crop (flat dark-blue car paint) at default settings and measured relative noise (std/mean of linear values on a flat patch):

| Input to `lightcraft-cli render` | Luma noise | Blue-channel noise |
|---|---|---|
| CR3, defaults | 0.43 | **1.56** |
| CR3, sharpen 0, colour NR 0 | 0.32 | 1.12 |
| **Adobe raw (Bayer) DNG, defaults**: same demosaic, Adobe matrix | **0.16** | **0.32** |
| Adobe linear DNG (Adobe demosaic) | 0.13 | 0.29 |

The demosaic (Li…

title: Camera-look fit is refused on dark, muted scenes: only a partial look (tone + chroma) applies
author: radialmonster
body:
Follow-up from #778 / #854.

On dark, muted scenes the full camera-look fit (matrix + hue/sat table fitted to the embedded camera JPEG) is refused by its quality gates. Only a partial look is applied (tone + chroma curve), so these files start duller than the camera JPEG even when the JPEG is decoded correctly.

**Measured on the #778 file** (Sony ILCE-7M2, Adobe RGB, DRO on), render vs the camera JPEG decoded as Adobe RGB:

| | Mean chroma | Median ΔE |
|---|---|---|
| main before #854 | 6.4 | 5.57 |
| with #854 | 7.2 | 5.44 |
| camera JPEG | 7.7 | – |

The look status is "partial (tone, chroma)" before and after #854. #631 (ILCE-7RM4 bursts ~18 L* dark at a third of the JPEG's chroma, while a neighbouring frame is fine) looks like the same family: a fit that passes on one frame and is refused on the next.

**Plan**
1. Log which gate refuses, and by how much, on the #778 file, the #631 frames, and the dark bins of the CC0 raw.pixls.us pairs.
2. Check whether the gates are tuned on bright scenes only, e.g. a fixed residual threshold that a low-signal scene can't meet even when the fit is good on held-out pixels.
3. Try gates scaled to the scene's signal (luminance / chroma spread) and a held-out-pixel check, and confirm that files that pass today don't get worse.

title: Sony A7 II (ILCE-7M2): built-in camera colour profile
author: radialmonster
body:
Follow-up from #778 / #854.

The Sony A7 II (ILCE-7M2) has no built-in camera colour profile, so each file depends on its own camera-JPEG fit. On dark or muted scenes that fit can be refused (#865), and the file then starts muted. The A7 IV (ILCE-7M4) and A7CR have profiles fitted with `lightcraft-cli calibrate` from 597 and 125 of their owners' photos.

**Needed:** a set of ILCE-7M2 ARWs with their in-camera JPEGs (Standard creative style, a mix of scenes and lighting). About 100+ photos makes a solid profile; even 20–30 helps. We only have one A7 II file locally (the #778 sample).

If you shoot an A7 II, a Google Drive folder linked here works. Uploads to [raw.pixls.us](https://raw.pixls.us) (CC0) help even more, because they become permanent test files.

Plan once there are files: calibrate, check held-out ΔE against the per-file fit, and bundle `assets/camera-profiles/ILCE-7M2.json` with an attribution row.

title: Sony DRO on: pooled DRO-off tone curve leaves the A7 II dark scene in #778 brighter than its camera JPEG
author: radialmonster
body:
Follow-up from #778 / #854.

With DRO on, the starting look lowers the fitted tone curve to Sony's DRO-off curve (`assets/camera-tone/sony-dro-off.json`, #244). That curve was pooled from 12 CC0 ARWs of 10 bodies; no ILCE-7M2 was among them.

On the #778 file (ILCE-7M2, DRO on) the render is still **brighter than the camera JPEG: L\* 17.1 vs 14.7**, so on this dark scene the pooled curve doesn't bring the tone down to the camera's.

**Plan**
1. Measure the DRO-off curve on A7 II files shot with DRO off (needs samples; we have none locally) and compare it with the pooled curve.
2. Check the dark end of the pooled curve: is the gap specific to this body, or to low-key scenes on any body? The raw.pixls.us Sony set can test the second.
3. If it's per body, add a per-body override; if it's the shadows in general, refit the toe of the pooled curve.

title: Feature request: multi-device library sync over storage you own (local/NAS, Google Drive, OneDrive, S3/R2 via rclone) using the existing append-only operation log
author: fernandodilland
body:
## TL;DR
LightCraft's catalog is already an append-only log of human-readable operations with snapshots. That is the ideal shape for syncing a library between computers (and people) over dumb storage. Please add an opt-in "Sync target": ship log segments to storage the user owns, merge them deterministically on other devices, and optionally vault the originals. No vendor server, no telemetry, and local-first stays the default.

## How Lightroom does it
- Lightroom Classic keeps the catalog as an SQLite database with a lock file. Adobe disallows catalogs on network drives (corruption risk with network locking), and users report cloud-sync folders (OneDrive, Dropbox) fighting with the open catalog; the usual advice is to keep the catalog local and the backups in the cloud.
- Classic's sync goes to Lightroom's web/mobile apps, not computer-to-computer, so people with two machines end up copying catalogs by hand.
- Lightroom (cloud) syncs originals and edits across devices, but only through Adobe's subscription cloud.

## What LightCraft has today (README only)
Append-only operation log with snapshots, background compaction and crash-safe persistence; XMP sidecars (read/write/auto-write); watched folders; a web build with a library in OPFS/IndexedDB; MCP/CLI. "No account, no cloud, no telemetry" is a stated value, so everything here must be opt-in.

## Proposal
**Phase 1, sync the log (the core):** each device appends to its own log and uploads **immutable segments** (`ops/<device>/<seq>`) to the target; other devices pull and fold them. Merge rules: per-photo, per-setting last-writer-wins with a hybrid logical clock; flags/ratings/labels LWW with author; collections as add-wins sets; nothing is lost because the history is replayable. No SQLite locking, so none of Lightroom's network-drive problems. Snapshots + compaction with a single-compactor lease.
**Phase 2, originals and previews:** originals are **not** synced by default. Optional "originals vault" via rclone to …

title: CR3: later adaptive-QP escape is misread as an extra +128 residual, causing preview-only fallback
author: cyeinfpro
body:
## Summary
The CRX v0x200 adaptive-QP escape parser can reject valid later residuals with `Canon CRX adaptive QP value 290`, causing embedded-JPEG fallback.

Reproduced on v0.6.0 (9e6c4c6fc9c7a7f192ce846c00ceb531e0f64dda); the relevant crx.rs is unchanged on current main. This is distinct from #828 / #829, which concern a real quantization index beyond the currently supported table range.

## Synthetic reproduction (no photos needed)
In the crx.rs unit-test module:

```rust
let src = [0x00, 0x00, 0x01, 0x2c, 0x90, 0x00, 0x00, 0x08, 0xc0];
let map = qp_map(&src, 4, 1).unwrap();
```

The stream has 69 meaningful bits and three zero padding bits:
- Escape literal 44 encodes residual +22.
- Two zero residuals reduce Rice k to zero.
- Escape literal 24 encodes residual +12.

The reconstructed QP values should be [22, 22, 22, 34], giving quantization indices [26, 26, 26, 38]. Those indices are inside the existing supported quantization range.

Current `qp_rice` consumes 16 zero bits plus a 16-bit literal. It interprets the two escapes as 300 and 280, reconstructing [150, 150, 150, 290], and the last value is rejected. The first artificial +128 is accidentally compensated by `adaptive_step` subtracting 124; a second escaped residual exposes the error.

## Direction
Read the complete escape prefix (23 zeros and its terminating one), then its 8-bit literal; keep QP Rice adaptation bounded appropriately. Store unbiased QP values and convert to the quantization index consistently. Do not simply widen the QP range or clamp the value.

An isolated local patch passes the synthetic case and existing CRX/wavelet unit tests. Two private inputs decode full sensor buffers, with the previously supported input byte-identical before/after. Full CLI rendering and wider crate/corpus validation are still in progress. No private input, metadata or identifying file details are attached.

title: Library switching: New Library command, recent libraries, show which library is open
author: radialmonster
body:
A separate library per client or job (for privacy, and to keep each job's data apart) already works in v0.6.0: File ▸ Open Library… opens a folder as a library and creates one there if the folder is empty (`app.openLibrary`, `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/settings.rs:627`). The last-opened library comes back at launch, and `--library DIR` / `LIGHTCRAFT_LIBRARY` pick one from the command line.

Switching between several libraries is still awkward, though:

1. **No New Library command.** You make a library by opening an empty folder, which nobody would guess. A File ▸ New Library… that asks for a name and a location would make this obvious.
2. **No recent-libraries list.** Every switch goes through the folder picker. A File ▸ Open Recent Library submenu (last ~5, with the missing ones greyed out) would make per-client work quick.
3. **No sign of which library is open.** Only Settings ▸ General ▸ Library shows the path. The library name in the window title or at the top of the left panel would stop people editing in the wrong one.

Found by reading the code on current main (menus.rs has only `app.openLibrary`; no recent list or title text). I haven't built a fix.

Related: #891 (Open Library shows the internal folders of other apps' catalogs), #294 and #880 (shared / synced libraries).

title: Choose the thumbnail cache folder per library, like smart previews
author: radialmonster
body:
The thumbnail cache always goes in `<library folder>/thumbs` (`crates/engine/src/library.rs:390`). Settings ▸ Thumbnail cache only sets its size (512 MB-8 GB).

Smart previews already have their own folder setting, per library (Settings ▸ Smart previews ▸ Choose Folder…). That one refuses relative paths and reports a missing drive instead of silently using another folder.

**Why it matters:** if the library itself has to live on a network drive or a small or slow disk, the thumbnails go there too. Grid scrolling then waits on the network, and the cache eats space on the share.

**Suggestion:** give the thumbnail cache the same per-library folder choice as smart previews, with the same safety rules (absolute path, no silent fallback). Keep the current location as the default.

Found by reading the code on current main. I haven't built a fix.

Related: #294, #880.

title: Edit panel: the EXIF values under the histogram run together ("ISO 1000200mm")
author: ingolfteetz
body:
A small one I noticed while going through my R5 Mark II photos.

**Seen on main (964d9338)**, macOS: a CR3 from an EOS R5 Mark II at ISO 1000 and 200 mm shows **"ISO 1000200mm"** in the strip under the histogram (Edit panel, headless snapshot at 1600x1000). The strip puts ISO, focal length, aperture and shutter at fixed thirds of the panel (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/edit.rs`, `// EXIF strip`): ISO is left-aligned, focal length and aperture are centred, shutter is right-aligned. Their widths are never measured. At the default 270 pt panel width the ISO and the focal length end up a few points apart, and at the 250 pt minimum they overlap; ISO 12800 or 1200 mm makes it worse. A missing value leaves a gap where it would be. Lightroom spaces the values evenly.

**What my branch does** (one commit, `LR-VIEW-HISTOGRAM`):

- Measures the values the photo has (missing ones left out) and spreads them like Lightroom: first flush left, last flush right, the free space shared equally between them (`spread_labels`, a pure function).
- When they don't fit with a 12 pt gap, they are drawn smaller, down to 10.5 pt. If that's not enough, the widest values are shortened with "…" so none overlaps the next, at any panel width.

**Results:**

- ISO 12800 / 1200 mm / f/5.6 / 1/8000 fits at full size with even gaps, even at the 250 pt minimum width.
- Tests: the layout function (no overlap for any strip width from 0 to 400 pt, only the widest value cut, NaN and infinite widths), and the Edit panel rendered headlessly at 250–520 pt with ISO 1000/200 mm, 12800/1200 mm and 102400/1200 mm, a missing ISO, and a very long shutter string from a file. The panel tests fail on the old layout.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `export_progress_and_cancel` (#674).

Related: #372 fixed the same kind of overflow for the masking tiles; the new headless test follows the approach of its test.

**Before I open a PR:** is it fine to draw the text smaller before shortening it with "…", or would you rather on…

title: LRTimelapse round trip: write crs: back, honour custom WB, deflicker compatibility
author: quacktastic73
body:
## Summary

Many timelapse photographers keep Lightroom only to edit LRTimelapse (LRT) keyframes. LightCraft already reads LRT sidecars well. With the four changes below, it could replace Lightroom in that workflow. I tested against v0.6.0+3 (`0ba118d`) on Linux, using LRT 7.5.2 sidecars and a 40-frame Canon EOS R6 CR3 night sequence.

### The LRT workflow
1. LRT writes a fixed `crs:` structure into every frame's `.xmp`.
2. The user reads metadata in the editor and edits the keyframes (`xmp:Rating` ≥ 1★).
3. The user saves metadata (`crs:`) back to the sidecars.
4. LRT interpolates every value across the sequence, runs Visual Deflicker, and rewrites all sidecars.
5. The editor reads metadata again and exports.

### What already works (tested)
- All 9 corrections in LRT's `crs:MaskGroupBasedCorrections` are read. These are 4 linear masks, 2 radial masks, and 3 `#LRT internal use (HG/Deflicker/Global)` gradients that sit entirely above the frame.
- The off-frame internal gradients apply uniformly across the image, as they should.
- LRT's `crs:` block, `lrt:` namespace and `xmpMM:History` survive a LightCraft save byte for byte.
- `xmp:Rating` keyframe stars round-trip.
- R6 CR3s decode fine.

---

## 1. Write develop settings back as `crs:` (blocker)

**Current behaviour (tested):** an edit saves only to `lc:settings`. I set exposure to 0.9 and ran Save Metadata to File; `crs:Exposure2012` in the sidecar still reads 0.5. On re-read, `lc:settings` wins (`sidecar.rs` ~L164). I then simulated LRT writing `crs:Exposure2012=1.2` and ran Read Metadata. A frame LightCraft had saved stayed at 0.9, while an unsaved frame picked up 1.2.

**Request:**
- Add an opt-in `library.xmpPreferences {writeCrs: true}`, with a writer that is the inverse of `crs.rs` / `crs_masks.rs`.
- **Update the existing structure in place; don't regenerate it.** Rewrite only the mapped global fields and each existing correction's `Local*` values, `CorrectionAmount` and mask geometry.
- Keep `CorrectionN…

author: radialmonster
body:
On main (0ba118de) and v0.6.0, **File ▸ Import Profiles & Presets…** sends `.cube` files to `profile.import` and everything else to `preset.import` (`crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs`, around line 1360).

Two things go wrong with the messages it shows when only `.cube` files are picked:

1. **Wrong message.** The preset half runs with an empty list, gets `imported: []`, and sets the status to "No new presets". Users read that as the import having failed, and they look for the LUT in the preset list, where it never appears.
2. **Silent failure.** Only the `imported` count of `profile.import` is read. Its `failed` list (for example a 1D LUT, "1D LUTs are not supported (only 3D .cube files)", or a malformed file) is dropped. A `.cube` that can't be loaded gives no toast and no reason, only "No new presets".

Expected:
- Skip the preset message when no preset files were picked.
- Report LUT failures with their reason, like the preset path does ("… file not readable").

Related: #618 (`profiles.list` omits imported LUT profiles; CLI only).

title: HDR merge of CR2 files comes out greenish: merged DNG has no camera colour tags
author: radialmonster
body:
HDR merge of Canon CR2 files gives a greenish, muted result, while each CR2 on its own renders fine (reported by @asten77 in #853). Same on v0.6.0 and main.

**Repro:** merge three copies of the CR2 sample from #853 (EOS 2000D). The merged DNG renders the sky at hue ~103 (green) and the tree at ~60 (olive). The single CR2 renders sky 40/33/38 and tree 54/26/17 (8-bit means).

**Cause:** the merged DNG has no `ColorMatrix*` tags.
- `crates/merge/src/frame.rs:132` keeps `raw.color` from the decoded raw.
- For CR2 that is empty, because the camera colour is fitted from the embedded JPEG at load, not read from tags.
- `output.rs` `color_data` carries the reference frame's colour tags over unchanged, so nothing is written, and the DNG then renders with no camera colour.

**Fix direction:** when the source's colour comes from the fitted look, write that look into the merged DNG (matrix, hue/sat table, tone curve) instead of the empty tags. Other formats whose colour is fitted the same way are probably affected too, so #917 (A6600 panorama colour shift) may have the same cause.

Also in `load_frame`: frames are clamped with `v.max(0.0)` before merging, which cuts negative values from noise in the shadows.

title: Show the image histogram inside the Tone Curve editor (like darktable)
author: zelefogs
body: ## Problem The Tone Curve panel draws the curve on an empty background. While editing, there is no indication of how the photo's actual tonal distribution maps onto the curve, which makes it hard to: - tell which parts of the curve (shadows / midtones / highlights) actually contain this photo's tones, - notice when a curve segment you are moving affects a tonal range that is empty in the image, - see how close an adjustment brings the image to clipping. darktable draws the image histogram as a backdrop inside its curve module, and Camera Raw does the same for its curve panel. It is the main thing I miss coming from darktable — curve edits there are much easier to aim and to reason about. ## Proposal Render the photo's histogram (or a downsampled version of it) as a filled area behind the tone curve plot: - **Live** — recomputed from the current edit state, like the histogram panel, so it reflects the image as adjusted by everything earlier in the pipeline. - **Channels** — at minimum luminance; ideally selectable R / G / B like darktable's curve, or all channels overlaid in their colors. - **Optional nice-to-have** — a toggle to also show the resulting (output) histogram, to visualize what the current curve does to the tonal distribution. The histogram is already computed for the histogram panel, so as far as I can tell the data could be reused, and drawing would just be a filled polygon behind the existing curve in the same plot area. ## Why - Makes it obvious which tonal regions of the current photo a curve edit will affect. - Avoids wasted adjustments on tonal ranges the image doesn't occupy. - Brings the curve tool to parity with darktable / Camera Raw, which matters for people migrating from those tools.

title: main does not build or pass its tests on macOS (995d5ea4): app won't compile, 12 tests fail, one clippy lint
author: nledford
body:
`main` at `995d5ea4` fails `cargo xtask ci` on macOS. I checked this in a clean checkout of that commit (no local changes), on macOS 27.2 (Apple silicon), rustc 1.99.0 / clippy 0.1.99. `main` at `0dd6593d` passed all 8 steps on the same machine earlier today, so these arrived with the merges since. As far as I can see there is no macOS job among the workflows (`freebsd`, `packaging-lint`, `release`, `windows-arm64`), which would explain why none of it showed up.

There are four separate things. The first one means the desktop app can't be built on macOS at all.

### 1. The desktop app does not compile on macOS

```
error[E0061]: this function takes 2 arguments but 1 argument was supplied
  --> apps/lightcraft/src/main.rs:67:13
   |
67 |             eframe::App::on_exit(self);
   |             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^------ argument #2 of type `Option<&eframe::glow::Context>` is missing
```

`88e4188e` ("Fix #812: the window's renderer can't kill the start-up") added the `glow` feature to `eframe` in `apps/lightcraft/Cargo.toml`, which gives `eframe::App::on_exit` a second parameter. The trait impl at line 79 was updated; the call at line 67 was not. That call is inside the macOS-only "Quit from the menu bar" path (from `761631c5`), so only macOS sees it. Passing `None` there should be all it needs.

Seen with `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo test -p lightcraft`.

### 2. A catalog lock test spawns `/bin/true`, which macOS does not have

It runs `Command::new("/bin/true")`. On macOS that is `/usr/bin/true`, so no child is ever spawned. `Command::new("true")` would find it on both.

title: Import from Device: cameras that only talk PTP (e.g. Leica M11-P) are not listed
author: ingolfteetz
body:
## Problem

A Leica M11-P connected over USB-C doesn't show up in **File → Import from Device**.

macOS sees the camera (`system_profiler SPUSBDataType`):

```
LEICA M11-P
  Manufacturer: Leica Camera AG
  USB Vendor ID: 0x1a98
  USB Product ID: 0x2084
  Link Speed: 480 Mb/s
```

The camera doesn't mount as a disk, though. It only talks PTP, so nothing new appears under `/Volumes`. `crates/engine/src/devices.rs` only lists mounted volumes that have a `DCIM` folder, so cameras that use only PTP/MTP are never found. This gap is already noted in `docs/parity-checklist.md` (LR-IMP-DEVICE: "no PTP/MTP (cameras that don't mount as a disk)") and `docs/hardware-parity.md`. Lightroom imports from these cameras directly.

It matters more for the M11 family than for most cameras: the M11 / M11-P can save to **internal memory**. Those photos can't be reached with a card reader at all, so for them the only workaround today is to download with macOS Image Capture first and then add the folder.

## Proposal

Add PTP (and later MTP) devices as an import source next to mounted volumes:

- List PTP still-image devices (USB class 6) in `library.devices` / Import from Device. Use the camera's model name, and mark them as a different kind from DCIM volumes.
- Browse the storages and objects (GetStorageIDs / GetObjectHandles / GetObjectInfo) and feed them into the existing import review. Download with GetObject (or GetPartialObject for large files), then put each copy through the same checks as card imports (`import_move.rs`).
- Write it in pure Rust on top of a pure-Rust USB crate (e.g. `nusb`); no libusb or libgphoto2. The PTP layer is the same one tethered capture (gaps #17, LRC-LIB-TETHER) would need later.
- The download runs as an activity row with a cancel flag (`docs/background-tasks.md`).

## Open questions / risks

- **macOS exclusive access:** the system camera daemon (`ptpcamerad`, behind Image Capture) usually claims PTP cameras. We need to find out whether a user-space clie…

title: Rename Photos: on a case-insensitive volume the sidecar a.xmp becomes Trip.XMP
author: snofla
body:
On a case-insensitive volume (the macOS default), Rename Photos changes the case of a sidecar's extension: `a.xmp` becomes `Trip.XMP`.

## Reproduction

macOS, default (case-insensitive) APFS, `main` at `76b53778`, headless:

```
mkdir t && cp some.jpg t/a.jpg
# t/a.xmp: any valid XMP packet (lowercase extension)
lightcraft-cli run --import t/a.jpg photo.rename template=Trip 'ids=[1]'
ls t
```

Result: `Trip.XMP  Trip.jpg`. Expected: `Trip.jpg  Trip.xmp`, the spelling the file already had.

I did not run this on a case-sensitive volume. From the code, only the spelling that exists is offered there.

## Cause

`sidecars()` in `crates/engine/src/rename.rs` (line 293) lists both spellings for each naming convention, `.XMP` first, and `move_file_with` keeps the candidates for which `fs.is_file(p)` is true. On a case-insensitive volume `a.XMP` passes that test for a file stored as `a.xmp`, so the uppercase candidate is the one that is moved, and its destination is built with `with_extension("XMP")` (around line 713). The renamed sidecar therefore takes the uppercase extension.

## Why it matters

- The name no longer matches what the other tools wrote next to the photo (`a.xmp`), though the file system treats the two as equal.
- The sidecar repair tests of #989 item 3 fail on macOS because of it: their fault injectors match the lowercase path exactly, while the code under test acts on `a.XMP`.

## Possible fix (not attempted)

When both spellings of a candidate are the same file (`same_file`), keep the one that matches the name stored on disk (a directory listing gives it), or prefer the lowercase one when they alias.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Faces: detection and recognition run only on the single-thread CPU interpreter; add a GPU (wgpu) path
author: radialmonster
body:
Face detection (YuNet) and recognition (SFace, AuraFace, or a user-installed `.onnx`) run only on the built-in CPU interpreter in `crates/faces`. That interpreter is checked, pure Rust and single-threaded (`crates/faces/src/lib.rs`, `net.rs`, `runtime.rs`). A face scan gets its speed only from running several photos at once (the scan pace uses one photo, half or four fifths of the machine's threads). The GPU sits idle even when the develop pipeline already uses it through `crates/gpu` (wgpu compute). Recognition with the larger models is the slowest part: the AuraFace entry in `known.rs` itself says "slow on a CPU".

Expected: on a machine with a usable GPU, a face scan can run the networks on it. The CPU path stays the reference and the fallback.

## Ideas

- **Reuse what's there.** `crates/gpu` already has a wgpu compute device, backend selection (`off` included) and the "CPU stays the reference" rule. The face interpreter supports only a small set of ops: Conv, Gemm, MaxPool, Resize, Relu, Sigmoid and Add/Sub/Mul. WGSL kernels for that set would cover the bundled models without pulling in an external ONNX runtime.
- **Same graph, second executor.** Keep `faces::graph` and its validation as they are. Add a GPU executor behind the same `run` interface, chosen per session, with the CPU used whenever the GPU is off, missing or fails a model's self-test (`faces.models.test`).
- **Batch work.** Detect on several downscaled photos per dispatch, and embed all aligned face crops of a photo (or a batch of photos) in one pass. Per-photo dispatch overhead would eat most of the gain for YuNet's small input.
- **Keep weights resident.** Upload a model's weights once per session and keep them on the GPU while a scan runs. Count that memory against the same budget as the develop pipeline's textures, so a scan never starves the editor.
- **Agreement tests.** Compare the GPU and CPU outputs on the synthetic models (`faces::synthetic`) and the bundled ones within a stated tolerance…

title: Help ▸ Report a Bug… next to Send Feedback…: version, system info and a log file to attach
author: radialmonster
body:
## What exists today (v0.6.0)

- **Help ▸ Send Feedback…** (`app.feedback`, `crates/ui-egui/src/links.rs:28`) opens a blank `https://github.com/storytold/lightcraft/issues/new`. No version, OS, GPU or log goes with it.
- **Help ▸ Open Log Folder** (`open_log_folder` in `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs`, #260) reveals `lightcraft.log`; the two previous runs are kept as `lightcraft.1.log` and `lightcraft.2.log`.

So a reporter has to find the version, OS, GPU and log by hand and attach them themselves, and many reports arrive without them. Send Feedback… is also the only way in for feature requests and questions, so it should keep opening a plain issue.

## Proposal: add Help ▸ Report a Bug… next to Send Feedback…

**Send Feedback… stays as it is**, for feature requests, questions and anything else that isn't a bug. **Report a Bug…** is a new item right next to it that opens a small dialog instead of a bare link:

1. **Dialog**: a short "what happened" field, plus a preview of exactly what will be included:
   - app version and build, OS and version, CPU, RAM, GPU adapter and driver backend
   - the log tail (last N lines of this run), with a tick box to also include the previous two runs
   - a tick box (on by default) that replaces home-folder paths and file names in the log with placeholders
2. **Report file**: on Continue, write `lightcraft-report-<date>.zip` (the selected logs plus a `system.txt`) next to the logs and reveal it in Explorer / Finder, so it can be dragged into the issue. A full log is often too long to paste, and an attachment has no length problem (GitHub takes .zip, .log and .txt).
3. **Pre-filled issue**: open `issues/new` with the title, the "what happened" text and the system info filled in through the URL. Keep the URL under ~8 KB: system info plus a short log excerpt only, the rest goes in the zip.

title: Default sharpening (Amount 40) looks much stronger than in Lightroom; is the amount scale calibrated against it?
author: M-Meffert
body:
Environment: LightCraft 0.6.0, Linux, Sony ILCE-6700, Viltrox 27 mm F1.2 and 75 mm F1.2, unedited ARWs

Observation
- On import a raw starts with Sharpening 40, radius 1.0, detail 25, masking 0 (sidecar: sharpen_amount 40, sharpen_radius 1.0, sharpen_detail 25, sharpen_masking 0). The same numbers are Lightroom's raw defaults.
- With these values the image shows much more local contrast / micro-contrast than I remember from Lightroom at the same Amount of 40 with photos from the same lenses. 
- Caveat: I no longer have access to Lightroom, so this is an impression from memory, not a measurement against a Lightroom export.

Question
Is the scale of the Amount slider calibrated against Lightroom's output (as was done for Auto in #628), or only the default numbers were taken over? If it is not calibrated, would it make sense to check it, or to use a lower default Amount until it is?

Workaround that works for me: a preset with only the Detail group ticked and Sharpening 0, chosen under Settings > Import > Raw defaults for this camera (thanks to the explanation in #939).
