title: cargo xtask ci: report what the machine actually tested (GPU adapters, skipped tests) so contributors' runs become hardware coverage
author: THEtheChad
body:
## Summary

Every contributor and agent runs `cargo xtask ci` before each commit (AGENTS.md), on a very wide spread of machines: Apple Silicon, Intel Macs, Windows laptops with Intel iGPUs, Linux boxes with NVIDIA, AMD, Mesa or no GPU at all, WSL, FreeBSD. That is a lot of hardware coverage the project already pays for, but two things throw it away:

1. **Tests that need hardware or data skip and pass silently.** libtest has no "skipped" status and captures the output of passing tests, so a GPU test that returns early on a machine with no usable adapter is indistinguishable from one that ran. `CI summary: all 8 steps passed` can mean the CPU/GPU equivalence tests never ran.
2. **The result is known only to whoever ran it.** A green run on an Intel-iGPU Windows laptop, the class of hardware behind #78, #136, #374 and #620, is evidence nobody else sees. When a run fails, the environment has to be reconstructed by hand (#479 is a good example of a careful manual report).

This issue proposes making `cargo xtask ci` say what it actually tested on this machine, and produce a small report a contributor can paste into a PR. It is distributed hardware coverage from the CI runs people already do, not a new gate.

## Evidence

- `xtask/src/main.rs:243-309` (`cmd_ci`, origin/main `76b53778`): the steps run with `Command::status()`, and the final line is `CI summary: all {n} steps passed`. Nothing is recorded about the machine or about what the tests skipped.
- `xtask/src/main.rs:112` (`ci_jobs`) already sizes jobs from available RAM, so xtask already probes the machine; it just doesn't report it.
- 61 skip sites in 22 files return early with an `eprintln!` that libtest swallows when the test passes:
  - GPU: `crates/gpu/tests/equivalence.rs:20-24` (every CPU/GPU equivalence case), `crates/gpu/tests/fallback.rs:40-42`, `crates/gpu/tests/memory.rs:11-13`, `crates/gpu/tests/shutdown.rs:22-25` (GPU half), `crates/gpu/src/nn.rs:905-913` (denoise net), `crates/engine/src/export.rs:3…

title: Renderer sizing: give the pipeline one exact output size, worked out once from the photo's full-resolution frame
author: THEtheChad
body:
#1041 fixes exports coming out a pixel short (5 × 3 at long edge 4 → 3 × 2; 6000 × 4000 at 800 px → 799 × 533). It does that with an export-only `Sizing::Exact` mode on `RenderRequest`. That fix is deliberately contained. This issue is about the structural cause, which the fix works around rather than removes.

### Why it happened

The output size is decided twice, from two different descriptions of the photo's shape:

1. Export options are resolved to an integer `w × h` from the catalog's dimensions (`Photo::width/height`, read from file headers): `export::output_size` → `Resize::apply`.
2. `pipeline::plan` treats every `RenderRequest` as a fit box and calls `Frame::fit` again, this time against the source it actually decoded. That is often a reduced source level (512 / 2560 px) whose own rounding gives a slightly different aspect (2560 × 1707 for 3:2).

The renderer's API only speaks in fit boxes (`max_w × max_h`). That suits views and thumbnails, but it means a size the caller has already decided can't be passed through unchanged. The usual design in raw developers is the reverse: the caller decides the output size once, from a canonical frame, and the renderer takes exact pixel dimensions plus the mapping into the source. A reduced source then affects only sampling quality, never the output size.

### What the fix leaves behind

- Two meanings share `max_w × max_h`, chosen by a flag.
- `Frame::sized` only accepts an exact pair when it is a rounding of the decoded frame's aspect, with slack for the reduced source's rounding. Otherwise it falls back to fitting so the image is never stretched. That guard exists only because the catalog's dimensions and the decoded source's can disagree (raw header size vs decoded active area, Upright changing the crop). It hides that disagreement rather than resolving it, and in those cases the off-by-one can still appear.
- Any new code that works out a size by fitting can bring the bug back. For example, #593 takes its downsizing…

title: UI decides on error message text (offer a model, cancelled vs. failed); errors and command params are untyped
author: THEtheChad
body:
## Summary

Several places in the interface decide what to do by reading an error's English text: whether to offer a model download, whether a task was cancelled or failed. They break silently when a message is reworded or translated (localization is active: #911, and `docs/localization-parity.md` lists "route lower-layer error messages through translatable message ids" as shared work), and some of them already misfire on messages that only happen to contain the word. The root cause is that errors reach the UI as `String`: `EngineError` has no "cancelled" or "model missing" variant, and `LightcraftApp::run` flattens every error with `to_string()`.

## Evidence (origin/main 76b53778)

Behaviour-bearing matches on error text:

| Where | Match | Decides |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:558` | `id == "faces.detect" && e.contains("Settings > Faces")` | offer the YuNet detector download. The same words are also in the "file far bigger than YuNet" and "could not be loaded" errors, which are not a missing model |
| `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:769` | `e.starts_with(segment::NOT_INSTALLED)` | open the SAM 3 download dialog for an AI mask error |
| `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:740` | SAM 3 download `error.contains("cancelled")` | "download stopped, resumes next time" toast vs. "download failed" error toast |
| `crates/ui-egui/src/lightroom_import.rs:359, 365` | `task.cancel.load(..) \|\| e.contains("cancelled")` | report a Lightroom inspect/import as cancelled instead of failed. Any real failure whose text contains "cancelled" (an OS error, a path) is reported as a cancel |
| `crates/ui-egui/src/export_task.rs:141` | Apple Photos `skipped` reason `.contains("cancelled")` | "(cancelled)" vs. showing the reason |

title: Tests don't run in CI on macOS, Windows or Linux, and the CPU/GPU equivalence tests never run in CI (gap 9)
author: THEtheChad
body:
## Summary

`cargo test` runs in CI only on FreeBSD. Nothing runs the tests on macOS, Windows or Linux x64, the three platforms people install LightCraft on, so platform-specific breakage reaches `main` and stays there until someone builds on that platform by hand. The CPU/GPU equivalence tests, the guard that keeps the GPU twin matching the CPU reference, never run in CI on any platform: they skip when there is no GPU adapter, and the code refuses the software adapters CI runners have.

This is gap 9 in `docs/gaps.md` (beta blocker, 6–12 h). This issue proposes a fix that stays inside the current design and adds no new runner types.

## Evidence

- `.github/workflows/` has `freebsd.yml` (the only workflow that runs `cargo test`), `packaging-lint.yml`, `release.yml` and `windows-arm64.yml`. `release.yml` builds packages on macOS, Windows and Linux but runs no tests. `windows-arm64.yml` runs the CLI natively and has no `cargo test` job (its header comment explains why).
- #989: on 2026-10-11, `main` did not compile on macOS (`eframe::App::on_exit` called with one argument in the macOS-only quit path), and 12 tests failed there. Nothing in CI could have caught it. The follow-ups (#990, #997, #1003, #1007, #1018) are still open.
- `crates/gpu/tests/equivalence.rs:19-25`: `gpu()` prints `skipped: no GPU adapter` and the test passes. `fallback.rs`, `memory.rs`, `shutdown.rs` and `shutdown_first.rs` do the same.
- `crates/gpu/src/ctx.rs:299-302`: `Gpu::new` returns `Err` for `wgpu::DeviceType::Cpu` ("the CPU pipeline is faster"). That is the right call for the app. The side effect is that lavapipe (Linux) and WARP (Windows), the only adapters on GitHub's standard runners, are never used, so the equivalence suite has never run in CI.

## What a test run on the three platforms finds today

I ran the workflow below on my fork, on `main` at 76b53778. All runners were standard GitHub-hosted ones with a cold cache.
